links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of Mòrag the Hard
told_in.section: V. Of the Years That Followed

events.title: Iain Dubh asks Mòrag how she did it
events.body: At the gate on the day he takes the hill, Iain Dubh asks Mòrag the one question no one else in the household has put to her directly, how she went south with eleven spears against a whole shore and came home with only seven lost, and she answers him as plainly as she is able.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of Mòrag the Hard
told_in.section: V. Of the Years That Followed

events.title: Màiri hears the seven names of Mòrag's raid
events.body: As a child at Baile ghorm, Màiri nan Làn learns the seven names kept from Mòrag Chruaidh's raid on the salt-pans a generation before, said slowly at the fire the way a thing is said that must not be said carelessly, and takes the telling for a settled account, its ending already closed.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: I. Of the Pans

events.title: Iain Dubh killed
events.body: Iain Dubh, a son of the king and sixth of the Stone Kings, goes down to raid the salt-pans as Mòrag Chruaidh had done, and is slain on the shingle at Baile ghorm. He is the first of Ailean's children to die by a spear. The list says only that he was brought home.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Iain Dubh takes the hill from Mòrag's hand

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Iain Dubh asks Mòrag how she did it

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Dubh comes down to the salt-pans at dawn

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Tadhg Garbh's spear kills Iain Dubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hill men carry Iain Dubh home

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Baile ghorm learns whose son fell on its clay

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Dubh's cairn raised on the hill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king comes home to a cairn already raised

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The salt-folk raise their own cairn for Iain Dubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod comes to the shore and absolves Tadhg Garbh

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Tadhg Garbh rows out and does not return

events.title: Iain Dubh comes down to the salt-pans at dawn
events.body: Iain Dubh, sixth of Rìghrean na Cloiche and eight years holder of the hill, rides south to Tràigh an t-Salainn as Mòrag Chruaidh had once done, and comes on the pans at Baile ghorm in the grey hour before full light, with more spears behind him than the shore's low bank was ever built to answer.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: II. Of the Coming of Iain Dubh

events.title: Tadhg Garbh's spear kills Iain Dubh
events.body: In the fighting at the bank's gap, Tadhg Garbh of Baile ghorm throws a spear among a scatter of others thrown at the same moment, and it alone finds its mark, taking Iain Dubh through the throat before he closes half the distance to the pans. He is the first of Ailean Mòr's children to die by a spear.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: II. Of the Coming of Iain Dubh

events.title: The hill men carry Iain Dubh home
events.body: The hill spears draw back from the bank around their fallen lord rather than press on for the salt, and carry him north at a pace no one on the shore is willing to call a retreat, though it can honestly be called little else.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: II. Of the Coming of Iain Dubh

events.title: Baile ghorm learns whose son fell on its clay
events.body: Days after the fighting, traders carrying word south tell the salt-folk that the man who fell on the pan's clay was Iain Dubh, holder of the hill and Ailean Mòr's own son, and that no man of the blood has ever before died by a spear.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: II. Of the Coming of Iain Dubh

events.title: Iain Dubh's cairn raised on the hill
events.body: Tormod, Iain Dubh's eldest living son, stands the whole of the cairn's raising without being seen to weep, a young man of eighty-seven still holding nothing in his own right, while the king is away in the north settling a quarrel of grazing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: III. Of the Cairn on the Hill

events.title: The king comes home to a cairn already raised
events.body: Ailean Mòr returns from the north to find his son already under the cairn, and stands by it three days speaking to no one, neither Tormod nor the reciters who stand ready to add his words to the list.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: III. Of the Cairn on the Hill

events.title: The king walks south alone
events.body: On the fourth day the king leaves the hill on foot, alone, taking no household and no spears, and walks the old track through the dunes toward Tràigh an t-Salainn, so that it is some while before anyone understands where he is bound.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king at Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: III. Of the Cairn on the Hill

events.title: The king at Baile ghorm
events.body: Ailean Mòr comes down alone to the shingle at Baile ghorm where his son was slain. The salt-folk come out against him with spears, and none strikes. They bring him the salt of the pans, and the southern shore is his. No blood is shed there, and none is paid.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The king walks south alone

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The salt-folk raise spears against him

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tadhg Garbh lowers his spear a second time

links.label: Answered by
links.title: Mòr gives the double handful of salt

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tràigh an t-Salainn called the king's

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall born to Fearchar Bacach

events.title: The salt-folk raise spears against him
events.body: Màiri, first to see the man alone on the shingle, screams for the men before she can put a name to what she sees. Thirty and more come running with the same spears that killed Iain Dubh, and make a line across the shore between the king and the pans.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king at Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: I. Of the Pans

events.title: Tadhg Garbh lowers his spear a second time
events.body: Tadhg Garbh raises his spear to his shoulder as the king closes the line, holds it until his arm shakes, then lowers it and looks at it in his own hand as though someone else had given it to him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king at Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: IV. Of the Man on the Shingle

events.title: Mòr gives the double handful of salt
events.body: Old Mòr of the salt-folk kneels on the shingle and holds up a double handful of wet salt from the nearest pan. The king takes it, eats a little, and closes her fingers back over the rest before he lets go and walks away north the way he came.

links.label: Answers
links.title: The king at Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: V. Of the Double Handful

events.title: Tràigh an t-Salainn called the king's
events.body: By evening word runs the length of the shore that the salt is the king's, though none can afterward say who first put it in those words. No blood is shed that day, the first time in two raids Baile ghorm's dead need no new name kept.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king at Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: V. Of the Double Handful

events.title: The salt-folk raise their own cairn for Iain Dubh
events.body: The salt-folk of Baile ghorm build a small cairn of their own on the rise above the pans, working in seven stones for the seven of Mòrag Chruaidh's raid though none of the seven died in this second fight, having come to think of both raids as one account.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: VI. Of Tadhg Garbh's Boat

events.title: Tormod comes to the shore and absolves Tadhg Garbh
events.body: Tormod rides south with four men to stand at the new cairn and see the pan where his father fell, asks Tadhg Garbh's name without anyone softening the telling, and says a man defending his own pans with his own hand owes no account for it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: VI. Of Tadhg Garbh's Boat

events.title: Tadhg Garbh rows out and does not return
events.body: Tadhg Garbh takes a hide boat out alone before first light one spring morning and does not come back with the tide or any tide after. No storm is remembered that night, and no wreckage of the boat is ever found.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Iain Dubh killed

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: VI. Of Tadhg Garbh's Boat

events.title: Seonag of An Cnoc Ruadh dies
events.body: Seonag nic Uisdein, who met Mòrag Chruaidh with a bag of pebbles and not with spears, dies on An Cnoc Ruadh in her seventy-second year; the salt tallies she kept go to her heir whole and without a stone out of place.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seonag of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Shingle at Baile ghorm
told_in.section: I. Of the Pans

events.title: Raghnall born to Fearchar Bacach
events.body: A son is born to Fearchar Bacach at Dùn ìseal, fair-headed from his first day, and is called Ceannfhionn before he is called anything else; he grows up with the hill's wool about him and no salt to cure its mutton.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king at Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: III. Of the Ground the Water Never Dried

events.title: The sea drowns the low houses of Cnoc chaol
events.body: In the night the sea rises past every mark it has kept on the coast at Cnoc chaol and comes in over the low houses, taking twelve of the shore's dead and leaving a sheet of grey sand a hand thick over every hearth it does not carry away, threaded with the shells of deep-water creatures no net there has ever brought up.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wave at Cnoc chaol

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: I. Of the Sand

events.title: The wave at Cnoc chaol
events.body: The sea comes far inland over a village on the site of Cnoc chaol and leaves a sheet of sand a hand thick upon its hearths, with the shells of deep-water creatures in it. The village is not rebuilt on the same ground.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The sea drowns the low houses of Cnoc chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seasaidh's father is counted among the drowned

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The old ground at Cnoc chaol is left unbuilt

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The survivors of Cnoc chaol build on the slope

events.title: Seasaidh's father is counted among the drowned
events.body: Seasaidh, carried up the slope at seven years old by her mother, learns in the grey hour after the wave that her father is not among those who reached higher ground, one of twelve of Cnoc chaol's dead counted when the counting is done.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wave at Cnoc chaol

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: I. Of the Sand

events.title: The old ground at Cnoc chaol is left unbuilt
events.body: The old folk of Cnoc chaol sift the sanded ruin for what is worth digging out and find little; no household chooses to rebuild on the drowned ground, level and good as it is, and it is left to grass over.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wave at Cnoc chaol

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: I. Of the Sand

events.title: The survivors of Cnoc chaol build on the slope
events.body: The households of Cnoc chaol carry what can be carried up the slope behind the drowned ground and build again there in stone rather than turf and wattle, keeping the old name of the coast for the new houses and pointing out the low ground to their children as ground not to be built on.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The wave at Cnoc chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seasaidh goes inland to Pàl's valley

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: I. Of the Sand

events.title: Seasaidh goes inland to Pàl's valley
events.body: Seasaidh, twenty-two years old, leaves the coast that raised her to take up a household two days inland with Pàl, a drover's son, in a green valley walled by low scarps that she has never seen and cannot yet well imagine, having known until then only tide and shingle.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The survivors of Cnoc chaol build on the slope

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: II. Of the Slope

events.title: The ground opens below Pàl's byre
events.body: In the night a low groaning felt through the floor of the house opens a crack clean across the floor of the valley a little below the household's byre, wide enough in places for a man to lose his boot to the dark below, running further than any of the valley folk cares to walk to find its end.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The ground opens at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: III. Of the Valley

events.title: The ground opens at Cill ghlas
events.body: A crack a man could fall into opens across the valley at Cill ghlas, and a spring moves a hundred paces downhill. The hill-folk bank the crack with stones and build on neither side of it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The ground opens below Pàl's byre

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The valley's spring moves to a new channel

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The valley folk keep clear of the crack by instinct

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of the opened ground reaches the hill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king walks the length of the crack

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The king forbids nothing at the crack

events.title: The valley's spring moves to a new channel
events.body: The spring that has risen at the valley's upper end for as long as the household remembers runs dry by inches through the season after the ground opens and breaks out afresh a hundred paces downhill, in a hollow none of the valley folk had marked before as ground a spring might choose.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The ground opens at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: IV. Of the Opened Ground

events.title: The valley folk keep clear of the crack by instinct
events.body: No house stands near enough the new crack to be lost to it, and the valley folk, without any rule laid down to tell them so, drive their beasts wide of it and warn their children from it from the first season, a wariness settling over ground that had never before asked for one.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ground opens at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: V. Of the King at the Crack

events.title: Word of the opened ground reaches the hill
events.body: A drover's telling of the crack, carried without any deliberate sending along the ordinary roads of trade and overheard at a hearth by a man travelling to the hill on other business, comes at last to the king by the same slow accident that carries most word to him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ground opens at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: IV. Of the Opened Ground

events.title: The king walks the length of the crack
events.body: The king comes on foot with two men to Pàl's valley and walks the crack's whole length with the household, crouching twice to look down into it though he lets nothing down to measure its depth, and asks whether any beast or soul has gone into it since it opened.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ground opens at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: V. Of the King at the Crack

events.title: The king forbids nothing at the crack
events.body: Standing at the widest part of the opened ground, the king tells the valley folk he will neither have the crack filled nor leave it, only that they keep their beasts and children back from it and build no house nearer it than they would to a drop of a man's own cutting.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The ground opens at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: V. Of the King at the Crack

events.title: Seasaidh begins the line of white stones
events.body: In her seventy-eighth year Seasaidh carries the first white stones up from the stream bed herself and sets them a stride back from the crack's edge, choosing them for their whiteness so a child running in poor light may see the line and know where the safe ground ends.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fault-line kept clear

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: VI. Of the White Stones

events.title: The fault-line kept clear
events.body: A line of white stones is laid along the old crack at Cill ghlas, and for the rest of the age no house is built within a stone's throw of it. Part of the line remains.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seasaidh begins the line of white stones

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The valley finishes the line of stones

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Seasaidh dies above the valley she marked

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: No house is raised within a stone's throw of the crack

events.title: The valley finishes the line of stones
events.body: Seasaidh's children and grandchildren take up the carrying before she has finished the first stretch, and households from both ends of the settled ground add their own stones until the white line runs the crack's full length.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fault-line kept clear

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: VI. Of the White Stones

events.title: Seasaidh dies above the valley she marked
events.body: Seasaidh dies in her eighty-second year in the house Pàl first brought her to, and is buried on the near slope within sight, though not within a stone's throw, of the white line she began; the valley keeps her name chiefly as the woman who marked the crack.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The fault-line kept clear

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: VI. Of the White Stones

events.title: No house is raised within a stone's throw of the crack
events.body: The valley folk who come after Seasaidh mend the white line where frost or flood undoes a stretch of it and never let it go wholly back to grass, and for the rest of the age no household raises a roof within a stone's throw of the opened ground on either side of it.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The fault-line kept clear

told_in.book: Of the Sand on the Hearths and the Opened Ground
told_in.section: VI. Of the White Stones

events.title: The unlit hearth
events.body: In a single dwelling a hearth is laid and never lit. Peat keeps it by chance. It is the eldest sign that someone here chose not to burn what could easily have been burned.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A cleared strip at Achadh dhìreach turns up an unlit hearth

events.title: A cleared strip at Achadh dhìreach turns up an unlit hearth
events.body: Three brothers new to the ground at Achadh dhìreach turn up, clearing a strip for barley, a long-buried hearth laid true and never lit, its wood cut for a first flame and a sliver of an gual dathach set unburned beside it; they leave it as they found it and build their own hearth a stone's throw off.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The unlit hearth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peat over the unlit hearth

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: I. Of the Hearth Never Lit

events.title: Peat over the unlit hearth
events.body: The house of the unlit hearth lies under three yards of peat, its hearth laid with dry wood and a slip of the coloured coal beside it, none of it burned. Whoever laid it went away and did not come back to light it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A cleared strip at Achadh dhìreach turns up an unlit hearth

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The unlit hearth passes out of living memory

events.title: The unlit hearth passes out of living memory
events.body: By the fifty-fourth year after its turning-up the buried hearth at Achadh dhìreach lies three yards under a valley floor's slow rise, and only the oldest households still trouble to show a child the exact ground to leave unbroken, no longer able to say why, only that it has always been so kept.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Peat over the unlit hearth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anna nic Coinnich is born at Achadh dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich is born at Achadh dhìreach
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich is born the youngest of four into a household two fields from the valley's old buried hearth, and grows up measuring an gual dathach by her own cupped hand as a plain fact of the valley, no different to her than the shape of the hills.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The unlit hearth passes out of living memory

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: II. Of the Measure Nowhere Written

events.title: The measured handful
events.body: In all the hill settlements a custom takes hold that no fire shall have more of the coloured coal than one cupped hand can hold. It is nowhere written and everywhere kept. From it the Small-Burning Law of the Holy Age is made.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The measured handful reaches every hearth of Na Glinn Àrda

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Anna nic Coinnich teaches her grandchildren the full hand

events.title: The measured handful reaches every hearth of Na Glinn Àrda
events.body: The custom of the full hand, kept first by a few households at a drovers' ford after a sick child was warmed too generously, spreads within a few years to every hearth of Na Glinn Àrda, nowhere written and nowhere proclaimed, so that a stranger travelling the road finds the same measure kept from one end of it to the other.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The measured handful

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anna nic Coinnich marries Aonghas of the next valley

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: II. Of the Measure Nowhere Written

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich marries Aonghas of the next valley
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich, nineteen years old, marries Aonghas, a byreward of the next valley, and keeps her own hearth within sight of the old buried one at Achadh dhìreach for the rest of her life.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The measured handful reaches every hearth of Na Glinn Àrda

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anna nic Coinnich buries a son

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: III. Of Achadh dhìreach

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich buries a son
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich, thirty years old, buries a son of six years taken by a winter fever, one of the ordinary griefs of a valley the tellers otherwise remember for little beyond its dry summers and its settled quarrels.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Anna nic Coinnich marries Aonghas of the next valley

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach
events.body: A household at Achadh dhìreach burns a whole basket of the coloured coal at once, knowing nothing of what it holds. The house burns down with three within, and the hearth-stone is found cracked through and running with colour. Ever after the tellings use it to show why the handful is kept.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Eanraig Ruadh burns a whole basket of an gual dathach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The house of Eanraig Ruadh burns with three within

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hearthstone of Achadh dhìreach cracks and runs with colour

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The king lays his hand on the cracked hearthstone

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The king names the full hand a good custom

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The greyed hearthstone is kept for a new house

events.title: Eanraig Ruadh burns a whole basket of an gual dathach
events.body: Eanraig Ruadh of Achadh dhìreach, old and feeling the winter's frost in his bones, sets very nearly a whole basket of an gual dathach on his fire in a single night rather than measure it by the full hand, having come, by his own account given beforehand, to doubt the measure applied to a man his age.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: II. Of the Measure Nowhere Written

events.title: The house of Eanraig Ruadh burns with three within
events.body: The house of Eanraig Ruadh at Achadh dhìreach goes up whole in the night in a flame shot through with a colour none of the valley folk have a word for, and burns to its stones before morning with Eanraig, his wife Beathag and a grandchild of six years named Ualan within it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: IV. Of the Basket

events.title: The hearthstone of Achadh dhìreach cracks and runs with colour
events.body: When the ash of Eanraig Ruadh's house is cool enough for hands to search it, the hearthstone at its heart is found split clean through, a finger's width of colour seeping slowly along the crack a full day after the fire itself has gone entirely cold.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: The king lays his hand on the cracked hearthstone
events.body: The king comes down to Achadh dhìreach within two days of the fire and kneels alone over the split hearthstone, laying his open hand across the running crack until the colour fades from it by degrees and the stone is left grey and dead as any ordinary hearth-stone.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: The king names the full hand a good custom
events.body: Standing before the valley folk of Achadh dhìreach, the king names the full hand a good custom and bids them keep it for their own sakes, saying plainly that he will make no law of it, having made none of any custom before.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king sends grain to Achadh dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: The king sends grain to Achadh dhìreach
events.body: The king sends two men back to Achadh dhìreach with grain enough to carry the valley's poorer households through a winter shortened by the loss of Eanraig Ruadh's stored barley along with the rest of his house.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king names the full hand a good custom

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: The greyed hearthstone is kept for a new house
events.body: Eanraig Ruadh's eldest living son raises a new house a little to one side of the burnt footings at Achadh dhìreach and sets the greyed, still-cracked hearthstone as its own hearth rather than break it up or leave it, judging a stone the king himself had greyed the safest hearth the valley was likely to keep.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich teaches her grandchildren the full hand
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich, keeping in her old age the kind of hearth other households' children are sent to, answers her grandchildren's asking why the measure matters by cupping one hand open before them and saying the words her own mother said before her: làn na glaice, 's gun tuilleadh, a full hand and no more.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The measured handful

told_in.book: Of the Unlit Hearth and the Basket
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Hand

events.title: The ground cracks below the slab at Tobar dhìreach
events.body: A wet spring brings down more of the hillside above Tobar dhìreach than any spring before it, and a crack no wider than two fingers opens in the turf below the old stained slab, running toward the burn before losing itself in ground that has not moved.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: I. Of the Line Kept in the Valleys

events.title: White stones laid along the new crack
events.body: The households of Na Glinn Àrda set a line of white stones along the crack below the slab's stain, as the coast has done at the crack Seasaidh's people watch, and build no byre against the ground it crosses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: I. Of the Line Kept in the Valleys

events.title: The watchers of the slab
events.body: Families near the crack take turns to sit by the slab laid over it, a household at a time, through the dark half of the year. What they watch for, none ever says.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The ground cracks below the slab at Tobar dhìreach

links.label: Caused by
links.title: White stones laid along the new crack

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The households agree to sit the slab in turn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathan first sits by the slab

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleonan and Ìde keep their first turn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Wolves come down close to the slab watch

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A light disputed along the crack

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle gives Beathan Sloinneadh a' Chlachair whole

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleonan asks Beathan what the watch is for

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king sits a night at the slab

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleonan dies

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìde sits her last turn at the slab

events.title: The households agree to sit the slab in turn
events.body: At the Samhain gathering the households nearest Tobar dhìreach agree, with no one arguing hard enough against it to be worth outlasting, that a household will sit by the slab from dusk to dusk, turn and turn again, through the dark half of every year from that Samhain on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: II. Of the First Turn

events.title: Beathan first sits by the slab
events.body: Beathan mac Shomhairle, already some five hundred years old and looking a man of thirty, sits among the first six households to keep the new watch, wrapped in the same plaid and eating the same bannock as any herding household of Na Glinn Àrda.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: II. Of the First Turn

events.title: Gilleonan and Ìde keep their first turn
events.body: A newly married herding couple of the shoulder of the hill above the burn, Gilleonan and Ìde, keep their household's first turn at the slab the same winter the watch is agreed, and come to be spoken of, for the decades after, in the same breath as Beathan's own turn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: III. Of Ìde Grown Old

events.title: Wolves come down close to the slab watch
events.body: A hard winter drives wolves nearer the fires of Na Glinn Àrda than living memory holds, and Beathan sits two of Gilleonan's household's nights himself, spear in hand, so that Gilleonan's young children need not lose a father to the season's watch.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: III. Of Ìde Grown Old

events.title: A light disputed along the crack
events.body: Six watchers on duty by the slab give six differing accounts of a light seen, or not seen, along the white stones one frost-misted night, and Somhairle, questioning each apart from the others, sets down no conclusion beyond the plain disagreement.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: III. Of Ìde Grown Old

events.title: Somhairle gives Beathan Sloinneadh a' Chlachair whole
events.body: In the same season his hair first silvers at the temple, Somhairle gives his son Beathan Sloinneadh a' Chlachair entire, twice through by the fire without a name out of place, so that the telling may be carried by more than one head.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: III. Of Ìde Grown Old

events.title: Gilleonan asks Beathan what the watch is for
events.body: Old and white-bearded, Gilleonan asks Beathan plainly, after forty years of sitting the slab beside him, what the households have been watching for; Beathan answers that he does not know, and never has.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: IV. Of the Question Gilleonan Asked

events.title: The king sits a night at the slab
events.body: The king rides up into Na Glinn Àrda alone, unasked and unlooked-for, and sits a whole night among a household keeping its turn at the slab, watching the same grey stone and the same thin crack the valleys have watched for forty winters, and says nothing of why he came.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Night at the Slab

events.title: Gilleonan dies
events.body: Gilleonan dies in the ordinary way at last, three winters after asking his one question of Beathan, who sits the last night of it beside his bed as he sat so many nights beside his watch-fire.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Night at the Slab

events.title: Ìde sits her last turn at the slab
events.body: Carried up the hill by a grandson on a sledge when her own legs no longer make the climb, Ìde sits her last turn beside Beathan at the same fire she first sat beside as a bride fifty winters before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The watchers of the slab

told_in.book: Of the Watchers of the Slab
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Night at the Slab

events.title: The empty salt-kists at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Raghnall Ceannfhionn, opening the salt-kists his grandfather the king left him, finds three of six near empty and thinks for the first time in earnest of the salt running to waste in An Cnoc Ruadh's pans while his own hill wears wool it cannot use fast enough.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: I. Of the Hill Without Salt

events.title: The king declines to speak for either hill
events.body: Raghnall asks the king to settle salt with An Cnoc Ruadh on his behalf. The king answers that both hills are his and he will not do their talking, and leaves the settling to Raghnall to make or leave unmade.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: V. Of the Trodden Ground

events.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace
events.body: Raghnall Ceannfhionn, seventh of the Stone Kings, meets the holder of the Red Hill at the ford where the fair of Muileann òg is held now, and they agree on salt for wool. Both hills are the king's, and neither is the other's. Both lists tell of the meeting, and in neither is the other named before it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The empty salt-kists at Dùn ìseal

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The king declines to speak for either hill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall rides west with nine companions

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Cnoc Ruadh refuses a poor clip

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The unnamed holder of An Cnoc Ruadh dies

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Raghnall's last morning at the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn dies

events.title: Raghnall rides west with nine companions
events.body: Raghnall takes nine men, no more, so the company will not be taken for a raid, and rides the five days' road to the ford, the first of the hill's blood to travel so near An Cnoc Ruadh's country since Uisdean knelt to the king.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: II. Of the Wading at the Ford

events.title: Strangers first set out goods beside the wool and salt
events.body: Traders with no part in either household begin bringing flint, dried fish and pots to the ford on the appointed days, setting their wares apart from the wool and salt. Neither hill turns them away, and no one afterward remembers deciding to let them stay.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The ford gathering

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: III. Of the Ground the Water Never Dried

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh refuses a poor clip
events.body: After a wet shearing season the wool comes down thin and unwashed, and An Cnoc Ruadh's people will not weigh full salt against it. Raghnall's son carries the refusal home; no word is sent to the king, and none is asked for.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: III. Of the Ground the Water Never Dried

events.title: The short year is made good without a law
events.body: Raghnall sends a better clip the following spring with fleece besides to make up the short year, and neither hill presses harder than a fair measure again. The bargain holds on nothing written, only on each side's wish to be trusted the year after.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The ford gathering

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: III. Of the Ground the Water Never Dried

events.title: The ford gathering
events.body: The meeting at the ford becomes a yearly gathering. Salt, flint, wool, dried fish and pots change hands there, and marriages are made. No meeting-place on the island has been used longer without a break.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Strangers first set out goods beside the wool and salt

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The short year is made good without a law

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first marriage of the ford

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Children of both banks cease to be told apart

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Flòraidh sets out for the ford with the amber bead

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Flòraidh sees the king buy nothing at the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Flòraidh's bead laid at the ford

events.title: The first marriage of the ford
events.body: A young man of the hill and a young woman of An Cnoc Ruadh's people, remarked on for three autumns' standing near each other at the weighing, are married on the trodden ground with both banks' households standing for it, the first marriage the meeting ever gave anyone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ford gathering

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh Gearr born

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: III. Of the Ground the Water Never Dried

events.title: Murchadh Gearr born
events.body: A son is born to a kinsman's household of An Cnoc Ruadh's old line and named Murchadh; short in the leg from boyhood, he is Murchadh Gearr to the lake shore long before he holds anything there.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first marriage of the ford

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: IV. Of Murchadh Gearr on the Salt Road

events.title: The unnamed holder of An Cnoc Ruadh dies
events.body: An Cnoc Ruadh's holder who first waded to meet Raghnall in the water dies after sixty years and more keeping faith at the ford, and is followed by a son who does not hold long, and then by a grandson.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: II. Of the Wading at the Ford

events.title: Murchadh Gearr comes to An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Murchadh Gearr, a kinsman of the old holder's line, comes to An Cnoc Ruadh after a grandson's short holding, and is known from his first weighing at the ford as a man who would rather walk a road than ride it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: IV. Of Murchadh Gearr on the Salt Road

events.title: Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill
events.body: Murchadh Gearr holds the Red Hill after Seonag and keeps the peace of the ford. It is told that he walked the salt road himself every year, to be seen upon it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Murchadh Gearr comes to An Cnoc Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh Gearr walks Rathad an t-Salainn to be seen

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh Gearr dies

events.title: Murchadh Gearr walks Rathad an t-Salainn to be seen
events.body: Murchadh Gearr walks the whole of Rathad an t-Salainn on his own feet in the weeks before every autumn meeting, stopping at every household on it, so that no child between Baile ghorm and the ford grows up without having seen An Cnoc Ruadh's holder pass in the flesh.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: IV. Of Murchadh Gearr on the Salt Road

events.title: Children of both banks cease to be told apart
events.body: By this year the children who run between the stalls at the ford on the appointed days make no distinction between the hill's side of the water and An Cnoc Ruadh's, the meeting by then older than any living memory of its making.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The ford gathering

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: II. Of the Wading at the Ford

events.title: Raghnall's last morning at the ford
events.body: In his hundredth year past the wading, Raghnall stands once more on the bank where he first crossed, looks on ground worn bare and hard by ninety-nine autumns of trade, and understands he will be gone from the ford long before the ford is done with anyone.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: V. Of the Trodden Ground

events.title: Hill-folk on the western shore
events.body: Households from the hills settle the bay at Ros bheag, the first of their kind on the west coast. They build in the hill manner, round and turf-roofed, a little back from the beach, and fish from the shore and not from boats.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Three households settle Bàgh an t-Seabhaig

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag walks the whole crossing and is the first buried by that tide

events.title: Three households settle Bàgh an t-Seabhaig
events.body: Three hill households too many for the grazing above Baile ghorm cross the spine of the island and settle a curve of grey sand under a gorse headland on the west coast, the first hill-folk household on that shore, building round and turf-roofed and fishing from the beach with lines and baskets rather than boats.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Hill-folk on the western shore

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: I. Of the Bay of Hawks

events.title: Beathag walks the whole crossing and is the first buried by that tide
events.body: Beathag, eldest of the three households that cross to Bàgh an t-Seabhaig, walks the nine days on her own feet in her old age and dies eleven years after seeing the water for the first time, the first of the hill-folk buried within sound of that particular shore.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Hill-folk on the western shore

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Flòraidh born at Bàgh an t-Seabhaig

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: I. Of the Bay of Hawks

events.title: Murchadh Gearr dies
events.body: Murchadh Gearr, who walked Rathad an t-Salainn every autumn so that no child on it grew up without seeing An Cnoc Ruadh's holder, dies in his sixty-sixth year; the road's households, hearing of it, leave a handful of salt at their doors for a night.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: IV. Of Murchadh Gearr on the Salt Road

events.title: Flòraidh born at Bàgh an t-Seabhaig
events.body: Flòraidh is born at Bàgh an t-Seabhaig in a winter hard enough to freeze salt-rime along the tideline, the middle child of five in the second household of the crossing, to a father who came west already grown and a mother who keeps his people's old telling of the hill valleys.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag walks the whole crossing and is the first buried by that tide

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: I. Of the Bay of Hawks

events.title: Flòraidh finds her first amber in the wrack
events.body: At nine years old Flòraidh pulls a lump of amber the colour of cold honey from a raft of storm-wrack and will not let the returning tide take it back, the find that sets her apart on a shore where sea-stone washes up seldom and is talked of for a season when it does.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amber from the Hawk bay

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: II. Of the Amber and the Wrack

events.title: Flòraidh learns the drill
events.body: A blind drill-master three houses along works a hole through Flòraidh's find over a winter of firelit evenings, and she learns from him, more by watching than by being taught, the weight of hand that keeps a flint point true against amber and the weight that snaps a good stone in two.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amber from the Hawk bay

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: II. Of the Amber and the Wrack

events.title: Traders learn to ask for Flòraidh by name
events.body: Traders on Rathad na Spor come to ask Bàgh an t-Seabhaig households for Flòraidh by name rather than knock at random for worked amber, and go away with beads finished better than any other hand on that shore gives them, paid in salt, wool, and once in a knife of southern flint.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amber from the Hawk bay

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: II. Of the Amber and the Wrack

events.title: A storm brings the great amber piece ashore
events.body: A gale that takes the roofs off two houses at Bàgh an t-Seabhaig leaves half a mile of strand heaped with wrack, and out of it Flòraidh draws the largest piece of amber the shore has ever given up, half again the size of her first find and clouded like smoke inside.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amber from the Hawk bay

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: III. Of the Bead and the Road

events.title: Amber from the Hawk bay
events.body: Amber is gathered from the wrack on the strands of the Hawk bay and drilled for stringing; lumps of it lie in the middens below Seann Skell. A bead of the same amber lies in the oldest ground of the ford gathering, carried there the length of the island.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Flòraidh finds her first amber in the wrack

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Flòraidh learns the drill

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Traders learn to ask for Flòraidh by name

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A storm brings the great amber piece ashore

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Flòraidh's bead laid at the ford

events.title: Flòraidh sets out for the ford with the amber bead
events.body: At five-and-twenty, on her mother's word that so fine a stone should be seen where the whole hill can see it, Flòraidh leaves the western Seann Skell with a trader's party of six households bound the length of the island for the yearly gathering at the ford, the bead carried in a pouch against her body rather than trusted to any pack.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ford gathering

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: III. Of the Bead and the Road

events.title: Flòraidh sees the king buy nothing at the ford
events.body: At Cruinneachadh an Àtha Flòraidh watches the king move slowly along the trading ground for the better part of an hour, weighing pots and running a thumb along flint edges, buying nothing and asking the price of nothing, while the crowd gives way from him without seeming to notice it has moved.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ford gathering

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: IV. Of the Ford and the Man Who Bought Nothing

events.title: Flòraidh's bead laid at the ford
events.body: Flòraidh holds out the amber bead to the king as he passes, and at his word kneels and lays it herself in the old ground of the ford among the ribbons and worked bones other travellers have left there, the finest stone the western strand ever gave up set down the length of the island from where the wrack cast it up.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Amber from the Hawk bay

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ford gathering

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Flòraidh weds the boat-mender's son

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: III. Of the Bead and the Road

events.title: Flòraidh weds the boat-mender's son
events.body: The boat-mender's son who saved a pack of hides from a swollen ford on the road east follows Flòraidh west the next summer with two finished boats on a traded cart, asks for her outright in her father's yard, and marries her that autumn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Flòraidh's bead laid at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: V. Of the Years the Bay Was Told Of

events.title: The first houses at Cathair dhomhain
events.body: Round houses are built by the harbour where Cathair dhomhain now stands, near enough the Red Hill to pay it salt. The Red Hill list counts them among its holder's households.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The round-house harbour begins paying salt to An Cnoc Ruadh

events.title: The round-house harbour begins paying salt to An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: The households at Cala nan Taighean Cruinne, where the king's blood first came down to the sea, begin paying their salt to An Cnoc Ruadh rather than keeping it among themselves, a custom that takes hold within a season with no word sent from Dùn ìseal to start it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first houses at Cathair dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Flòraidh dies on the western shore

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: V. Of the Years the Bay Was Told Of

events.title: Flòraidh dies on the western shore
events.body: Flòraidh dies in her sixty-eighth year in a mild autumn with the wrack lying quiet along the whole strand, four years a widow, and is buried at her own asking facing the water rather than the headland, so that whatever comes in on the tide comes in past her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The round-house harbour begins paying salt to An Cnoc Ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: V. Of the Years the Bay Was Told Of

events.title: Cattle in the north-west
events.body: Cattle come to Cnoc ghorm in the north-west, where the settlements had lived on seal, fish and deer. The herds must have been walked up the flint road.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cattle walked to Cnoc ghorm

events.title: Cattle walked to Cnoc ghorm
events.body: Small herds driven up Rathad na Spor by stages over three summers bring cattle for the first time to the green rise of Cnoc ghorm in the north-west, where the people have lived on seal, fish and deer, and the first calves born there are watched through their first winter by the whole settlement in turn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cattle in the north-west

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: V. Of the Years the Bay Was Told Of

events.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal
events.body: A long-house forty paces long, with byre and hall under one roof, is built on the rise at Cathair gheal. It is the greatest building of the age in the north-west. Twice it burns, and twice it is rebuilt on the same footing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The long-house raised at Cathair gheal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal burns the first time

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal is raised again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iseabail born at the shaft's moor

events.title: The long-house raised at Cathair gheal
events.body: A long-house forty paces long, byre and hall under one roof and greater by half again than any building of the age, is raised above the firth at Cathair gheal, timbered from Rathad na Spor's own hills and roofed with turf a season dried, and is spoken of the length of the coast within the year.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: V. Of the Years the Bay Was Told Of

events.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal burns the first time
events.body: A spark from an untended hearth catches the byre-end thatch of the great long-house at Cathair gheal in the small hours of a still night; every soul under the roof escapes, but the hall burns with the byre before the driven-out cattle can be turned back to help beat down the flame.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: V. Of the Years the Bay Was Told Of

events.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal is raised again
events.body: The household of the burned long-house at Cathair gheal rebuilds it on the same footing before the next winter closes in, holding the ground proved good whatever the fire proved of the roof, and the building stands after that mended, its scorch mark left for anyone to see.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal

told_in.book: Of the Western Shore and the Amber Bead
told_in.section: V. Of the Years the Bay Was Told Of

events.title: Iseabail born at the shaft's moor
events.body: Iseabail is born into the household that keeps the eastern Toll-dubh, the elder of two children, a quiet and watchful girl who grows up among the old plaited cords still hanging inside the household's own door from the diggers' day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The long-house at Cathair gheal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann born

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: I. Of the Household at the Shaft's Mouth

events.title: Eachann born
events.body: Eachann is born five years after his sister Iseabail, a loud, quick, daring child who cannot pass a height without wanting to know what stands at the top of it, nor a hole without wanting to know what lies at the bottom.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iseabail born at the shaft's moor

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann first asks to be let down

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: I. Of the Household at the Shaft's Mouth

events.title: Eachann first asks to be let down
events.body: At fifteen, Eachann asks his father plainly to be let down the household's own shaft to see what four generations of telling have never claimed to know, and is refused without more explaining than the shaft's own long silence has ever been given.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eachann born

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The father of Iseabail and Eachann dies

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: II. Of the Boy Who Would Not Let It Be

events.title: The father of Iseabail and Eachann dies
events.body: The keeper of the eastern Toll-dubh dies of an ordinary fever that takes three others on the moor that same wet spring, and the covering stone passes to his two children, Iseabail twenty-two and Eachann seventeen.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eachann first asks to be let down

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: II. Of the Boy Who Would Not Let It Be

events.title: A youth let down into Toll-dubh
events.body: A youth is let down on a rope of plaited hide into the eastern Toll-dubh, to the rope's end. He is drawn up alive and never tells what lay at the bottom. No one goes down again in this age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A youth let down into Toll-dubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: No one goes down Toll-dubh again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Ròpa dies untold

events.title: A youth let down into Toll-dubh
events.body: Eachann is let down on the household's own plaited-hide cord into the eastern Toll-dubh, to the rope's end, while his sister Iseabail holds it alone at the stake; she draws him up alive, her palms raw from the labour, and he never once tells what he found.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A youth let down into Toll-dubh

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: III. Of the Rope's End

events.title: No one goes down Toll-dubh again
events.body: Iseabail lays the covering stone that autumn and tells every soul who asks after it that the household goes down into Toll-dubh no more; the shaft is not opened again by any hand of that moor in this age.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A youth let down into Toll-dubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iseabail marries

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: III. Of the Rope's End

events.title: Iseabail marries
events.body: Iseabail marries a man of a neighbouring holding who had courted her patiently through the years her brother's silence went unanswered, and raises three children on the same moor within sound of the covering stone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: No one goes down Toll-dubh again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann earns the name Ròpa

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: IV. Of the Question She Carried

events.title: Eachann earns the name Ròpa
events.body: The moor comes, gradually and without any one year's telling saying when it began, to call Eachann by no other name than Eachann Ròpa, a byname he wears the rest of his life without complaint or particular pride in it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iseabail marries

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: IV. Of the Question She Carried

events.title: A fire lit in the Doire uaine hills
events.body: A herding family, new to the hills, lights an open fire at Doire uaine against the custom. Their hut is found empty, the fire still burning. Thereafter the covered hearth is kept more strictly.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A fire lit in Marbh-bheò's hills

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas born of the king's blood

events.title: A fire lit in Marbh-bheò's hills
events.body: A herding family new to Marbh-bheò's hills lights an open fire against the custom of that country; their hut is found afterward standing with the fire still burning and not a soul of the household anywhere about it. The telling reaches Iseabail as a traveller's news.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A fire lit in the Doire uaine hills

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: V. Of the Hut and the Lake

events.title: Eachann Ròpa dies untold
events.body: Eachann Ròpa dies in his own bed of the ordinary failing of a long life, sixty-four years old and easy in his going, and tells his sister on the last night only that some things are carried better than they are told.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A youth let down into Toll-dubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iseabail dies within sight of the stone

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: VI. Of Her Own Ending

events.title: Sìleas born of the king's blood
events.body: A daughter of the king's blood is born in the valleys under Dùn ìseal and named Sìleas, pale-haired from the cradle; no one at her naming thinks of her as a holder of the hill, and she grows up minding grain-pits and not judgements.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A fire lit in the Doire uaine hills

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The high pastures fail at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Store within the Bank

events.title: Iseabail dies within sight of the stone
events.body: Iseabail dies at eighty in the house her father died in, and is buried, at her own asking, within sight of the covering stone she laid every autumn of her life over the question she carried and was never given the answer to.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eachann Ròpa dies untold

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: VI. Of Her Own Ending

events.title: The lake dwellings burn
events.body: The platforms on Loch chrom burn to the waterline, and the charred piles are left standing in the shallows. No one builds on the lake again in this age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lake dwellings burn on Loch chrom

events.title: The lake dwellings burn on Loch chrom
events.body: The platforms built out over the shallows of Loch chrom burn in a single night to the waterline, the charred piles left standing bare in the shallows after; no household of that lake builds there again. The telling reaches Iseabail, by then grey-haired, as a trader's tale.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The lake dwellings burn

told_in.book: Of the Rope's End
told_in.section: V. Of the Hut and the Lake

events.title: Seal-oil lamps at Caol leathan
events.body: Stone lamps with a hollow for seal oil and a wick of moss are used at Caol leathan. They are the first light on Dia-thìr that is not a hearth, and they give little smoke.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first seal-oil lamp at Caol leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Geamhradh Liath

events.title: The first seal-oil lamp at Caol leathan
events.body: A household of Caol leathan sets a hollowed stone with seal oil and a wick of moss on its hearth-ledge and lights it, the first light on the coast that is not a hearth; within three winters every house on that stretch keeps one burning through the dark months.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seal-oil lamps at Caol leathan

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: I. Of the Lamps, the Traps and the Standing Frame

events.title: The fish-traps of Caol fhiadhaich
events.body: Wattle fences are staked across the river-mouth at Caol fhiadhaich to trap salmon on the ebb. The same line of stake-holes is used again and again through the rest of the age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fish-fence staked at Caol fhiadhaich

events.title: The fish-fence staked at Caol fhiadhaich
events.body: Households of the river-mouth at Caol fhiadhaich stake a fence of woven wattle out into the ebb to herd salmon on the falling tide; the fence washes out twice before the third setting holds, and the line of stake-holes it leaves is fished again every year after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fish-traps of Caol fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: I. Of the Lamps, the Traps and the Standing Frame

events.title: Mòrag Chruaidh dies
events.body: Mòrag Chruaidh, who named her seven dead at the hill's fire and never raised another raid, dies in her thirteen hundred and twentieth year; the naming of the seven goes on at the same fire after her, and her own name is added at its foot.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid

told_in.book: Of Mòrag the Hard
told_in.section: III. Of the Bank Behind the Shingle

events.title: The upright looms of Muileann leathan
events.body: At Muileann leathan in the north cloth is woven on standing frames, no longer twined by hand. The loom-weights of fired clay lie in rows in the houses, where they fell from the warp.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The standing frame raised at Muileann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beitris born at Muileann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king stops at Beitris's stall

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king weds Beitris

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beitris dies

events.title: The standing frame raised at Muileann leathan
events.body: A household at Muileann leathan raises the first upright loom on the northern stream, the warp held taut by loops of fired clay at its foot rather than by hand, so that a worker stands free to pass the weft with both hands and beat it home faster than any lap-worked cloth had gone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The upright looms of Muileann leathan

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: I. Of the Lamps, the Traps and the Standing Frame

events.title: Beitris born at Muileann leathan
events.body: Beitris is born into the third household to raise a standing frame at Muileann leathan, growing up under her mother's loom and taking her own frame in her twentieth year, known on the stream for cloth that lies flatter and holds its dye better than any other hand's.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The upright looms of Muileann leathan

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: II. Of the Weaver

events.title: The first tide-count
events.body: Someone begins to mark the high-water line against a fixed rock. Why is not told; but the marks are cut at intervals more even than a fisherman's need would ask.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first tide-count begun

events.title: The first tide-count begun
events.body: An unnamed hand on an unnamed shore begins cutting a mark on a fixed rock at each high tide's furthest reach, a row of cuts kept at intervals no ordinary fisherman's need would ask for; the habit spreads to more than one shore within a generation, and none who keep it can say what it counts toward.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first tide-count

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: I. Of the Lamps, the Traps and the Standing Frame

events.title: The king stops at Beitris's stall
events.body: At Cruinneachadh an Àtha the king stops before a bolt of Beitris's blue-black cloth, tests the flatness of the weave with two fingers as he tests a flint edge with his thumb, and asks how the cloth is made to lie so; it is the only exchange between them any teller claims to have had whole from a witness.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The upright looms of Muileann leathan

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: II. Of the Weaver

events.title: The king weds Beitris
events.body: Beitris goes south from Muileann leathan to Dùn ìseal as the king's wife, raising a frame of her own in a shed built to her asking, and teaches the standing weights to the hill's women in twos and threes until the craft has spread from her own shed to a dozen others.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The upright looms of Muileann leathan

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: III. Of the Wedding and the Grey Winter

events.title: An Geamhradh Liath
events.body: The king's hair goes grey between one moon and the next in a single winter and no further, dark to grey all at one stroke; he says nothing of the cause, and the hill, having talked of little else through the dark months, lets the matter rest by the following Bealltainn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seal-oil lamps at Caol leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh Mòr born

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: III. Of the Wedding and the Grey Winter

events.title: Murchadh Mòr born
events.body: Beitris bears the king a black-haired son, Murchadh, the only child either parent will raise together to see him grown; the women who nurse him remark only that he runs hot for an infant and sleeps sound through cold that keeps other babies crying.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Geamhradh Liath

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: III. Of the Wedding and the Grey Winter

events.title: A second tide-rock at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The high-water marking is copied at Ros dhomhain on a boulder in the harbour mouth, the marks cut at the same intervals as on the first rock. Someone carried the practice there, and the interval with it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second tide-rock cut at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king and Beitris at the rock of Ros dhomhain

events.title: The second tide-rock cut at Ros dhomhain
events.body: A young keeper at Ros dhomhain, hearing of the first tide-rock by report alone, begins a rock of his own in his harbour mouth, cutting the marks at the spacing he judges by memory of the telling, though he has never seen the first rock with his own eyes.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A second tide-rock at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: IV. Of the Rock at Ros dhomhain

events.title: The king and Beitris at the rock of Ros dhomhain
events.body: The king stands before the new-cut tide-rock at Ros dhomhain the better part of an afternoon and tells Beitris that a thing can be worth doing before anyone has worked out why; she carries the answer, the longest she ever had from him on any matter not a household's grazing or a stranger's quarrel, the rest of her life.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A second tide-rock at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beitris asks if she will be forgotten

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: IV. Of the Rock at Ros dhomhain

events.title: Beitris asks if she will be forgotten
events.body: In her seventieth year, with Murchadh grown and spoken of on the hill for the north he means to hold, Beitris asks the king whether he will forget her; he answers not with a plain word but by naming, quietly and in order, every wife he had before her, more names than she can hold the count of.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king and Beitris at the rock of Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: V. Of the Names She Was Given

events.title: Beitris dies
events.body: Beitris dies in a mild autumn in her seventy-fourth year, Murchadh at her graveside a black-haired man of thirty-nine who looks no older than fifteen; the king buries her with his own hands and sits by the turned earth a night and a day, saying once that a warp holds what it is strung with.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The upright looms of Muileann leathan

told_in.book: Of Beitris and the Grey Winter
told_in.section: V. Of the Names She Was Given

events.title: The lake is higher
events.body: The marks on the Ros dhomhain rock creep upward from keeper to keeper, and by the end of the age Loch chrom stands a hand higher on the rock than at the first cut. The keepers go on cutting.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lake still climbing on the Ros dhomhain rock

events.title: Murchadh goes out with the flint-carriers
events.body: Sixteen years after his mother's death, Murchadh can no longer sit in his father's hall and goes north with a train of flint-carriers bound for Cnoc àrsaidh, taking up a yoke among them without a word of who he was; it is three seasons before any man there learns whose son he has been carrying flint beside.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The flint of Cnoc àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: I. Of the Road He Chose

events.title: The lake still climbing on the Ros dhomhain rock
events.body: Passing through Ros dhomhain on his way north, Murchadh stands before the tide-rock his mother once showed him and finds the keeper's line of cuts crept a hand's width further up the stone since his childhood, so slowly that no single year's mark can be told from the year before or after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The lake is higher

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh meets Ailig Spor on Rathad na Spor

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: I. Of the Road He Chose

events.title: The flint of Cnoc àrsaidh
events.body: A pit is worked for flint on the hill of Cnoc àrsaidh in the north-west, the only good flint on Dia-thìr. Its grey flakes are carried to hearths from one end of the island to the other.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Murchadh goes out with the flint-carriers

events.title: Murchadh meets Ailig Spor on Rathad na Spor
events.body: On the road between Cnoc àrsaidh and Cruinneachadh an Àtha, Murchadh comes to know Ailig Spor, a young carrier from the northern flats who tells him plainly that a yoke does not care whose back it is on; the two keep the friendship the whole of the years the road gives them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The lake still climbing on the Ros dhomhain rock

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailig marries by the northern crossing

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: II. Of the Flint Road and Ailig Spor

events.title: Ailig marries by the northern crossing
events.body: Ailig Spor marries a woman of a household by the river-crossing on Rathad na Spor and raises two sons and a daughter on flint-carrying wages, all three walking the near stretches of the road themselves before they are grown; Murchadh stands godfather to the eldest.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh meets Ailig Spor on Rathad na Spor

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: III. Of the Years Between

events.title: The flint road
events.body: A track is worn by the flint-carriers from Cnoc àrsaidh south and east toward the ford gathering. Near Àth leathan their feet sink it a yard deep.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Rathad na Spor worn a yard deep

events.title: Rathad na Spor worn a yard deep
events.body: The track between Cnoc àrsaidh and the northern river-crossing, worn by generations of carriers before Murchadh and Ailig were born, sinks a full yard below the level of the ground on either side, so that a man walking it casts no shadow beyond its banks and a stranger cresting the rise above it mistakes it for a dry ditch dug on purpose.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flint road

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A storm survived in the sunken road's own bank

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: II. Of the Flint Road and Ailig Spor

events.title: A storm survived in the sunken road's own bank
events.body: Caught two days from shelter by a late storm, Ailig thinks to have the yoke-gang dig into the sunken road's bank and roof it with the carriers' own yokes rather than risk the open ground; the gang comes through with nothing worse than cold fingers, where an older carrier swears they would otherwise have lost two or three men.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Rathad na Spor worn a yard deep

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The households along the road remark Murchadh's unaging face

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: II. Of the Flint Road and Ailig Spor

events.title: The households along the road remark Murchadh's unaging face
events.body: It does not escape the households of Rathad na Spor, decade upon decade, that Murchadh carries a yoke with no more sign of years on him than a carrier three seasons in shows; some later carriers will not share a fire with him for reasons they give badly, but Ailig never once asks him the plain question every other man on the circuit wants to ask.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A storm survived in the sunken road's own bank

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailig gives up the road for the pit-mouth

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: III. Of the Years Between

events.title: Ailig gives up the road for the pit-mouth
events.body: In his sixty-fourth year Ailig Spor hands his yoke to his youngest son and takes the lighter work of tallying at the Cnoc àrsaidh pit-mouth; Murchadh, who could by then claim a dozen reasons to walk the far circuits instead, finds himself always coming back through Cnoc àrsaidh at the turn of a season to sit an evening with him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The households along the road remark Murchadh's unaging face

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailig Spor dies

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: IV. Of Ailig Spor's Death

events.title: Ailig Spor dies
events.body: Ailig Spor dies in his sleep in his sixty-eighth year, four years a keeper and not a carrier, found by his own daughter with no mark of pain on him; Murchadh, two days south with a fresh gang who scarcely know his name, walks the two days back in one and stands at the graveside with a stillness the household has not seen on him before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ailig gives up the road for the pit-mouth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh sets the pit-mouth's free flake as a standing custom

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: IV. Of Ailig Spor's Death

events.title: Murchadh sets the pit-mouth's free flake as a standing custom
events.body: Murchadh stays at Cnoc àrsaidh the better part of a month after Ailig's burying and tells the new keeper that the pit's first flake of any new working shall go on being given free to whoever asks, as it always had, and that he will see to it himself that the custom does not lapse.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ailig Spor dies

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: IV. Of Ailig Spor's Death

events.title: The hawk lintel at Àth mhòr
events.body: A hawk is carved on a lintel over a house door at Àth mhòr in the north, wings closed, head turned. It is the oldest carving of a hawk on the island, and of any bird.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hawk carved into the lintel at Àth mhòr

events.title: The hawk carved into the lintel at Àth mhòr
