events.body: Walking the far eastern circuit alone, Murchadh watches a young man of Àth mhòr cut a hawk into his father's door-lintel by firelight over three evenings, wings closed and the head turned back over the shoulder; the carver says only that the shape came to him whole one night and would not leave him alone until he had cut it, and no carrier ever hears of an earlier bird cut in wood or stone anywhere on Dia-thìr.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hawk lintel at Àth mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: V. Of the Bird Carved at Àth mhòr and the Wolves of Tobar fhiadhaich

events.title: Wolves at Tobar fhiadhaich
events.body: At Tobar fhiadhaich wolves are buried whole and with care, laid on their sides as people are. No other beast is so buried in this age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh sees the wolves buried at Tobar fhiadhaich

events.title: Murchadh sees the wolves buried at Tobar fhiadhaich
events.body: In his hundred and eighty-fifth year Murchadh comes upon a household at Tobar fhiadhaich burying a wolf on its side with its legs drawn up as in sleep; asked why, an old woman of the household says the wolf keeps its own dead on the high ground and has earned better than the ditch, a care they have never spoken of outside the household before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wolves at Tobar fhiadhaich

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh asks his father for the north

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: V. Of the Bird Carved at Àth mhòr and the Wolves of Tobar fhiadhaich

events.title: Murchadh asks his father for the north
events.body: Murchadh comes south to Dùn ìseal and asks his father for the whole northern country Rathad na Spor runs through, which he has walked, he says, more times than any man living and knows better than any man living knows it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh sees the wolves buried at Tobar fhiadhaich

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king refuses Murchadh the north

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: VI. Of the Asking and the Refusal

events.title: The king refuses Murchadh the north
events.body: The king answers that the north is Dòmhnall's to hold, given him sixteen hundred years before and well kept since, and that a share once given is not taken back for a better claim that comes after it; Murchadh rides north again within the week without asking a second time.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh asks his father for the north

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first grievance of Ailean's line

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: VI. Of the Asking and the Refusal

events.title: The first grievance of Ailean's line
events.body: Murchadh rides out of Dùn ìseal with a face his father's household has not seen on him before, nearer pride than the young man's face he wore going north the first time, and close under the pride, by the telling of those who marked it, the first grievance the hill ever had cause to lay at a son of Ailean's own naming.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king refuses Murchadh the north

told_in.book: Of the Flint Road
told_in.section: VI. Of the Asking and the Refusal

events.title: The high pastures fail at Dùn ìseal
events.body: A spring of near-ceaseless rain rots the high grazing at the root, and households begin killing beasts they would ordinarily have wintered, for want of anything left to feed them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìleas born of the king's blood

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas opens the store within the bank by the mouth, not the herd

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Store within the Bank

events.title: Sìleas opens the store within the bank by the mouth, not the herd
events.body: Sìleas Bhàn orders the grain-pits cut into Dùn ìseal's own earthwork opened to every household by the count of mouths at its hearth rather than by the size of its herd, the first time the store is shared by that measure; a wealthier herdsman rides up to protest it to her face, and she does not change the measure.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The high pastures fail at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Store within the Bank

events.title: Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years
events.body: Sìleas Bhàn, eighth of the Stone Kings, of the king's blood, holds Dùn ìseal through years of failed grazing. No deed is told of her but that she held, and the list goes on after her.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Households begin refilling the store unasked

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas Bhàn gives Dùn ìseal to Tormod Liath

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas Bhàn dies among her kin

events.title: Households begin refilling the store unasked
events.body: With the grazing still short, households of Dùn ìseal's own ground begin returning grain to the bank's pits beyond what was drawn from them, a custom Sìleas Bhàn lets stand without ordering it, judging it will hold firmer for growing its own root.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The grazing recovers

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Store within the Bank

events.title: The grazing recovers
events.body: The high pastures dry and thicken again within three years of their failing, as such lean spells generally did on that ground, though the store within the bank is not filled to its old level again for a decade.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Households begin refilling the store unasked

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: I. Of the Store within the Bank

events.title: The hunger at Baile chrom is first heard of at the hill
events.body: Word reaches Dùn ìseal, slow and uncertain, of two failed fishing seasons on the north-western shore at Baile chrom, of stores already gone to bark and boiled seaweed, and of graves being laid two deep for want of time to dig them singly.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hunger at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: II. Of Baile chrom

events.title: The hunger at Baile chrom
events.body: Hunger comes to the settlement on the site of the north-western Baile chrom. Its pots are left full of boiled bark and seaweed, and its grave-rows are doubled. No older hunger on Dia-thìr is tied to a place.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The hunger at Baile chrom is first heard of at the hill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king rides north-west with grain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas sends grain along the whole north-western coast

links.label: Leads to
links.title: No household near Dùn ìseal again lets its store run low

events.title: The king rides north-west with grain
events.body: Ailean Mòr rides to the north-western coast himself with the first grain that can be spared, by a road that has never before carried him, and is gone the better part of a season; he returns saying nothing of what he found, save that every hill of the kingdom is to look to its own store before the next storm season.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hunger at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: II. Of Baile chrom

events.title: Sìleas sends grain along the whole north-western coast
events.body: Sìleas Bhàn holds Dùn ìseal in the king's absence and sends three cartloads of grain and a small herd of goats after him, with instruction that they go to whichever hearths along that coast are worst served and not to Baile chrom alone, having heard the hunger reaches wider than one shore.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hunger at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: II. Of Baile chrom

events.title: No household near Dùn ìseal again lets its store run low
events.body: Once the doubled grave-rows of Baile chrom are known at the hill, no household within a day's ride of Dùn ìseal again lets its own grain fall below a season's worth, whatever the grazing does, for fear of what might one day be asked of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hunger at Baile chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wells of Achadh shean run low

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: II. Of Baile chrom

events.title: The wells of Achadh shean run low
events.body: The wells of Achadh shean in the east fall a hand lower than any digger there remembers, a thing thought at first too small to trouble the hill with.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: No household near Dùn ìseal again lets its store run low

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: III. Of Achadh shean

events.title: A shepherd's boy walks to Dùn ìseal to report the cracking banks
events.body: A boy of Achadh shean walks three days to Dùn ìseal on his own feet rather than trust the telling to a rider, to say that the field banks his grandfather raised have cracked from dryness for the first time in three generations; Sìleas Bhàn sends a rider east to look before sending any grain.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The drought at Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: III. Of Achadh shean

events.title: The springs of Achadh shean stop
events.body: The rider sent east returns saying the springs of Achadh shean have not merely run low but stopped outright, their whole visible flow gone at a season when they have never before failed within living telling.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The drought at Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: III. Of Achadh shean

events.title: The drought at Achadh shean
events.body: The springs of Achadh shean in the east run dry so long that the field banks are forsaken and grown over. When people return they cut new fields on another line.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A shepherd's boy walks to Dùn ìseal to report the cracking banks

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The springs of Achadh shean stop

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The field banks of Achadh shean are forsaken

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas refuses to have the dead field pulled down

events.title: The field banks of Achadh shean are forsaken
events.body: With the springs three years dry, the households of Achadh shean walk off their old field banks, leaving the dead barley standing in the row, and cut new fields on another line lower on the slope, where a lesser spring still runs thin but steady.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The drought at Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: III. Of Achadh shean

events.title: Sìleas refuses to have the dead field pulled down
events.body: Riding out to see the forsaken banks of Achadh shean, Sìleas Bhàn refuses her own rider's suggestion that they be levelled, saying a bank tells a household what the ground once gave and what it stopped giving, and is worth more standing than pulled down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The drought at Achadh shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìleas asks the king what her deed will be

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: III. Of Achadh shean

events.title: Sìleas asks the king what her deed will be
events.body: At Cruinneachadh an Àtha Sìleas Bhàn asks Ailean Mòr what the list will say she did, having herself set no boundary stone, fought no war and raided no shore; he tells her that four hundred years of not failing, where failing was always the easier road, is itself the deed the list will keep.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìleas refuses to have the dead field pulled down

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: IV. Of the Deed and the List

events.title: Sìleas Bhàn gives Dùn ìseal to Tormod Liath
events.body: In her five hundred and tenth year Sìleas Bhàn gives the hill to Tormod Liath, a son of Iain Dubh of thirteen hundred and seventy years, ordering the store within the bank counted before witnesses so the new holder takes it up knowing to the basket what it holds.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Liath keeps the grain-measure unchanged

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: V. Of the Giving of the Hill

events.title: Tormod Liath keeps the grain-measure unchanged
events.body: In his first words as holder, Tormod Liath tells the households he will change nothing about the store within the bank, having watched it feed two hungers in his own lifetime and seeing no reason to improve on a measure that has already held.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìleas Bhàn gives Dùn ìseal to Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Hungry Years
told_in.section: V. Of the Giving of the Hill

events.title: Tormod mends the bank and the boundary marks
events.body: In his first seasons holding Dùn ìseal, Tormod Liath sets right what the hungry years let go: the silted ditch, the leaning palisade, and the boundary marks between the hill's fields and the households', blurred by two lean summers of each man taking what he could.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: I. Of the Hill Given Over

events.title: Tormod buries his eldest son
events.body: Tormod Liath's eldest son dies of years, the first of the three heirs Tormod outlives; the old holder stands at the burying still dark-haired, and is named by his own son's grandchildren as their grandfather's father.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: IV. Of the Heirs He Buried

events.title: The naming of the wind directions
events.body: The eight winds are named, and every Dia-thìreach sailor after uses the names. Their meaning is dark even to those who speak them, and they have never been changed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Na h-Ochd Gaothan are named

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Fearchar Gobha brings the wind-names to Tormod

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh born in the valleys under the hill

events.title: Na h-Ochd Gaothan are named
events.body: Na h-Ochd Gaothan of the year, known before only by their feel, are given names all at once by no one the coasts can afterward name. Every coast that tells it uses the same eight names in the same order from that year on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The naming of the wind directions

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: II. Of the Winds Given Names

events.title: Fearchar Gobha brings the wind-names to Tormod
events.body: A salt-carrier of the hill, Fearchar Gobha, hears the eight wind-names at the coast fair and brings them up to Tormod Liath, who says only that a landholder has no business owning what belongs to the sea.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The naming of the wind directions

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: II. Of the Winds Given Names

events.title: Eilidh born in the valleys under the hill
events.body: A daughter of the king's blood is born in the valleys under Dùn ìseal and named Eilidh; grey-eyed from her first year, she grows up at her own hearth with no thought of holding anything more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The naming of the wind directions

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hill in Its Old Age

events.title: Three brothers raise Clachan nan Gaoth at Ceann leathan
events.body: Aonghas, Dùghlas and Ailig mac Torcaill, brothers of the point, quarry eight stones from an outcrop above the landing and raise them in a ring, one for each named wind, so a sailor may lay a hand on the stone of the wind he wants before he puts out.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wind-stones of Ceann leathan

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: III. Of the Stones at Ceann leathan

events.title: The wind-stones of Ceann leathan
events.body: Eight tall stones are set in a ring on the point at Ceann leathan, one for each of the named winds. Sailors of every later age touch the stone of the wind they want before they put out.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Three brothers raise Clachan nan Gaoth at Ceann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The crooked stone reset

events.title: The crooked stone reset
events.body: One bad winter after Clachan nan Gaoth are first raised at Ceann leathan, the stone of the hardest offshore wind is found settled crooked and is dug out and reset on a footing of smaller stones, standing straighter and newer than its seven fellows ever after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wind-stones of Ceann leathan

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: III. Of the Stones at Ceann leathan

events.title: Tormod buries his second son on the western slope
events.body: Tormod Liath's second son, who held the hill's western grazing and never cared for the hall, is buried at his own asking on the slope where he herded, and Tormod says a man ought to be let choose his own ground if nothing else is left him to choose.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: IV. Of the Heirs He Buried

events.title: The wind-names carried to the islands
events.body: The eight wind-names are used on Eilean fhada as on the main island. The markers on its high point bear eight cut notches, one facing each way.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wind-names cut into the rock of Eilean fhada

events.title: The wind-names cut into the rock of Eilean fhada
events.body: The people of Eilean fhada, off the northern cape, keep no ring of stones but cut the eight wind-names as notches into the rock of the island's highest ground, one facing each way, so a man lost in thick weather may find his bearing by touch.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wind-names carried to the islands

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: III. Of the Stones at Ceann leathan

events.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn dies
events.body: Raghnall Ceannfhionn, who waded into the ford to strike the bargain of salt for wool, dies in his fourteen hundred and first year; the ford keeps its autumn meeting that year as every year, and the two hills send more wool and more salt than the bargain asks.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace

told_in.book: Of Salt for Wool
told_in.section: IV. Of Murchadh Gearr on the Salt Road

events.title: Tormod Liath
events.body: Tormod Liath, ninth of the Stone Kings, a grandson of the king, holds the hill so long that he outlives three heirs, and is remembered as old. In his time Dùn ìseal is given its second bank, and its ground is doubled.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Tormod mends the bank and the boundary marks

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Tormod buries his eldest son

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Tormod buries his second son on the western slope

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod paces out the second bank

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The households dig the second bank

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod buries his third son and tells him it does not hurt

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod goes fully grey

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king raises Tormod from the mud at the gate

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A child asks why the old man kneels

events.title: Tormod paces out the second bank
events.body: Tormod Liath walks the line of Dùn ìseal's second bank himself through two winters before calling the households in to dig, taking in the low ground by the spring without losing the height needed for a watch-fire.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: V. Of the Second Bank

events.title: The households dig the second bank
events.body: The households of Dùn ìseal dig through a spring and a summer to raise the second bank, doubling the ground held within the hill's earth from some forty houses to very near a hundred.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: V. Of the Second Bank

events.title: Tormod buries his third son and tells him it does not hurt
events.body: The youngest and last of Tormod Liath's three sons dies asking his father, near the end, whether it hurts to be left each time; Tormod tells him no, the one lie the tellings of that hill ever charge against him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: IV. Of the Heirs He Buried

events.title: Tormod goes fully grey
events.body: By his hundred and seventy-fifth year of holding, Tormod Liath is grey through, brows and beard with the rest, and the young of the hill, who never knew him dark, take him for the oldest thing on Dùn ìseal, older even than the second bank he raised.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: VI. Of the Grey

events.title: The king raises Tormod from the mud at the gate
events.body: The king comes to Dùn ìseal's gate with a handful of his household and no word sent ahead; grey, stooped Tormod Liath kneels to him as every holder before him has knelt, and is raised again by a hand that has not aged since Tormod's father knelt the same way.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: VII. Of the King at the Gate

events.title: A child asks why the old man kneels
events.body: A granddaughter of Tormod's second son, watching from the bank, asks her mother why the young stranger lets the old holder kneel to him as at a common gate; her mother tells her that evening, by the fire, what the hill has long known and rarely says aloud.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Tormod Liath

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: VII. Of the King at the Gate

events.title: The Dia-thìrich name
events.body: In this age the hill-folk begin to call themselves Dia-thìrich and the island Dia-thìr. The first use is not known; the eldest tellings take both names for granted. With the names goes the belief: they did not come; they were here.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Children begin to call themselves Dia-thìrich

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod is told the island's new name by a boy of seven

events.title: Children begin to call themselves Dia-thìrich
events.body: The children of Dùn ìseal begin, unbidden by any elder, to call themselves Dia-thìrich and their island Dia-thìr, in place of hill-folk or the grove-born name Clann nan Dè; within a generation the old words fall out of use among the young.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Dia-thìrich name

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Name They Gave Themselves

events.title: Tormod is told the island's new name by a boy of seven
events.body: A boy of the new ground within the second bank tells Tormod Liath, asked what clan he is, that he is Dia-thìreach and that everyone is; Tormod answers only that it is a good enough name for a good enough island.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Dia-thìrich name

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Name They Gave Themselves

events.title: Ealag and Torcall Tochlair are promised by their households
events.body: Two households of the hill above Dùn ìseal, who share a slope and a spring, treat a match between Ealag and Torcall Tochlair as already settled. Torcall's mother carries the salt across to ask for it in the old way.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first forbidden marriage

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: I. Of Ealag and Torcall Tochlair

events.title: The salt is refused
events.body: Torcall's mother brings the salt back unaccepted. The elders of Ealag's household give her no reason, only that the match cannot be, and she comes home with her face set as it had never been set before.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first forbidden marriage

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: I. Of Ealag and Torcall Tochlair

events.title: The first forbidden marriage
events.body: A marriage between two lineages is forbidden, for a reason no surviving telling gives. Already the Dia-thìrich order themselves by blood, long before the coal gives them cause.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Ealag and Torcall Tochlair are promised by their households

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The salt is refused

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall is turned away at every door

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ealag's mother weeps and will not say

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ealag given to a household of the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ealag dies at the ford

events.title: Torcall is turned away at every door
events.body: Torcall Tochlair goes himself to Ealag's father and her uncles and is told, in the same three words each time, that the marriage cannot be. None of them will say why, and he cannot tell whether none of them know it or all of them have sworn silence.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first forbidden marriage

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: I. Of Ealag and Torcall Tochlair

events.title: Ealag's mother weeps and will not say
events.body: Ealag asks her own mother for the reason and is told only to stop asking, and her mother weeps, which Ealag has never seen her do, not even at a burying.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first forbidden marriage

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: I. Of Ealag and Torcall Tochlair

events.title: Ealag given to a household of the ford
events.body: Ealag is married to Donnchadh, a fisher of the ford town, who asks for her honestly and does not learn of the earlier match for three years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first forbidden marriage

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: II. Of the Marriage at the Ford

events.title: Torcall hears of the black hill in the east
events.body: Torcall Tochlair, restless at the coal-banks under the mountain, hears from traders of ground in the east with a look of coal about it, and begins asking the older diggers whether the vein is the island's only one.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first seeking of another vein

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: III. Of the Trench at the Black Hill

events.title: Lines recited at the ford
events.body: At the ford gathering households begin to recite their lines aloud before any marriage is made, seven names back on either side. These are the first genealogies of the common households; only the Line of the Mason is older. None survives whole.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lines first recited at the ford

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Ealag tells Donnchadh of Torcall

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum born to Eilidh

events.title: The lines first recited at the ford
events.body: Before any match is spoken at the fair, a household stands and gives its line aloud, seven names back on either side, so a forbidden blood may be named before the salt is carried. Ealag hears it and thinks of the four shut mouths that refused her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lines recited at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: II. Of the Marriage at the Ford

events.title: Ealag tells Donnchadh of Torcall
events.body: That evening Ealag tells her husband of the match that was refused her. He says only that it explains a look she sometimes wears at fair-time, and asks nothing further.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Lines recited at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: II. Of the Marriage at the Ford

events.title: Calum born to Eilidh
events.body: A son is born to Eilidh in the valleys under the hill and named Calum, dark from his birth; he will be the elder of her two sons and the one who stands where an heir stands.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lines recited at the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lachlann born on An Cnoc Ruadh

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: Lachann agrees to go east with his brother
events.body: Torcall's younger brother Lachann, easier in temper but loyal to him, agrees to go east to the black hill with two other restless diggers, meaning to see Torcall satisfied and brought home again.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first seeking of another vein

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: III. Of the Trench at the Black Hill

events.title: The first seeking of another vein
events.body: Diggers from Dùn ìseal open a trench on a hill near Cnoc dhubh in the east, seeking coal like the vein's. They leave it unfinished when two of them are crushed by a fall. The trench stays open, and what it would have found is not known.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Torcall hears of the black hill in the east

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Lachann agrees to go east with his brother

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lachann buried at the trench's mouth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall builds a shelter at the trench

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of Torcall reaches Ealag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall Tochlair dies at the trench

events.title: Lachann buried at the trench's mouth
events.body: Torcall will not have his brother carried elsewhere and buries him where he fell, at the mouth of the trench on the black hill. The other man killed with him is carried home by his own people.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first seeking of another vein

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: III. Of the Trench at the Black Hill

events.title: Torcall builds a shelter at the trench
events.body: When the other diggers pack their tools and go back to the coal-banks under the mountain, Torcall Tochlair stays, and builds himself a turf shelter at the trench's edge for the winter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first seeking of another vein

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: III. Of the Trench at the Black Hill

events.title: Word of Torcall reaches Ealag
events.body: A trader who stopped at the black hill brings word to the ford of a man sitting alone beside an open trench with his brother in the ground nearby, still saying he means to find the coal.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first seeking of another vein

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: III. Of the Trench at the Black Hill

events.title: The stone that would not break
events.body: A second opening for a new vein is made elsewhere on the island and fails wholly: common rock, and nothing beneath it. So it is first known that the vein under the mountain is alone of its kind.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The saying of the vein's choosing begins to travel

events.title: The saying of the vein's choosing begins to travel
events.body: After the second opening strikes only unbroken common stone, it is said across the island that the vein under the mountain is alone of its kind and chose its one place the way na Seachd Guail are said to have chosen theirs.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stone that would not break

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: IV. Of the Stone That Would Not Break

events.title: Ealag dies at the ford
events.body: Ealag dies in her own bed at the ford with her children about her, having lived her whole life after the refusal without the reason for it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first forbidden marriage

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: V. Of the Vein That Chooses

events.title: The will for a third opening goes out of the island
events.body: No elder forbids a third trench outright, but the wish for one fades everywhere at once, the way the wish for a refused match fades in two households without a word spoken between them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The prospecting ends

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: IV. Of the Stone That Would Not Break

events.title: A household gathers at the black hill's foot
events.body: Folk who come to the black hill for one reason or another begin to stay, since the ground is as good as any and the man who keeps the open trench asks nothing of them.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The prospecting ends

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: V. Of the Vein That Chooses

events.title: The prospecting ends
events.body: No one tries a third opening in this age. The Dia-thìrich hold that the vein chooses where it lies, and that the choice is not theirs to try.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The will for a third opening goes out of the island

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A household gathers at the black hill's foot

events.title: Torcall Tochlair dies at the trench
events.body: Torcall Tochlair dies at the black hill and is buried beside his brother at the trench's mouth. The household he gathered keeps the ground and does not fill the trench in.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first seeking of another vein

told_in.book: Of the Forbidden Marriage and the Trench
told_in.section: V. Of the Vein That Chooses

events.title: The first shared meal law
events.body: A custom arises, unwritten, that any household with food to spare shall share it before the storm season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A holder shamed into doubling his own surplus

events.title: The shore-woman's catch carried in whole
events.body: A woman of the shore households at Dùn ìseal, whose net takes more mackerel than her family can eat or smoke before it turns, carries three baskets of it to the bank herself rather than let it spoil unshared. Tormod Liath comes down from the hall to help her set them down. After it the sharing before the storms needs no one to ask.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: I. Of the Custom that Had No Beginning

events.title: A holder shamed into doubling his own surplus
events.body: A holder of one of the near valleys mocks a household that brings little to the sharing. His neighbours say nothing against him, but the next year he brings in double his own surplus unasked. No reciter keeps his name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first shared meal law

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beasag born at Àth shean

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: I. Of the Custom that Had No Beginning

events.title: Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal
events.body: At Dùn ìseal the sharing before the storms is done in the open: every household brings its surplus within the bank, and it is divided by the count of mouths. The custom has no earlier place that is known.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The shore-woman's catch carried in whole

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig born to a herder of the near slopes

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A lean storm season at Dùn ìseal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beasag watches the division made by the count of mouths

events.title: Beasag born at Àth shean
events.body: A daughter is born to a careful household at Àth shean, the ford below Dùn ìseal, some years after her father digs a grain pit under the byre floor against nothing he can name. Her mother dies bearing the last of her brothers three winters before the lean year that will end the household's place at the ford.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A holder shamed into doubling his own surplus

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: II. Of the House at Àth shean

events.title: Lachlann born on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: A son is born in An Cnoc Ruadh's hall and named Lachlann, red-headed like so many of that line; he grows up wet to the knee on the lake shore and learns the salt-rake before the spear.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Calum born to Eilidh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi born on An Cnoc Ruadh

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: III. Of the Household of Lachlann Ruadh

events.title: Oighrig born to a herder of the near slopes
events.body: A daughter is born to Dòmhnall, a herder of the near slopes above Tobar dhìreach with no kinship to Rìghrean na Cloiche, and named Oighrig; she grows up sitting her household's turns at the slab and will draw the white stone at three-and-thirty.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: II. Of the Lot

events.title: A lean storm season at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Failed grazing and short-headed barley along the near valleys, with three weeks lost to a wind that will not turn, make the leanest storm season since the sharing began. The division at the bank is thinner than any household remembers, and old people come to be counted though they have nothing to bring.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: III. Of the Lean Year

events.title: Beasag watches the division made by the count of mouths
events.body: Beasag, seventeen, is sent to Dùn ìseal with her household's share in the lean year and sees the sharing divided by the count of mouths: a widow with four children carries home more than she brought, and a boy holds his first full sack too long to trust it. She says nothing of her father's pit.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: III. Of the Lean Year

events.title: A household turned out at Àth shean
events.body: A household at Àth shean hides its spare grain in a pit under the floor and brings nothing to the sharing. When the pit is found the household is put out of the settlement with what it can carry. It is the first punishment under the custom that is remembered.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beasag tells of her father's pit at the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Liath sends to open the floor at Àth shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The household of Àth shean put out with what it can carry

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beasag's household settles east of the vein

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas asks after the pit at Àth shean

events.title: Beasag tells of her father's pit at the ford
events.body: In the first mild days after the storms break, a woman mending net on the bank at Àth shean asks Beasag idly whether her father's byre came through the lean year as thin as the rest. Beasag answers true: there is a pit under the floor, and he never brought it all in.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A household turned out at Àth shean

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: IV. Of the Telling

events.title: Tormod Liath sends to open the floor at Àth shean
events.body: Word of the hidden pit reaches Tormod Liath at Dùn ìseal by way of Àth shean's own holder. He asks only whether the girl told it of her own will, unbeaten and unbribed, and on being told she had, sends his men to open the floor.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A household turned out at Àth shean

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: IV. Of the Telling

events.title: The household of Àth shean put out with what it can carry
events.body: Grain enough for two households through the lean winter is found beneath the byre floor. Beasag's father is given until dark to take what his household can carry on its backs and to be off the ford's ground by morning: the first punishment under the sharing custom that is remembered.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A household turned out at Àth shean

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: IV. Of the Telling

events.title: Beasag's household settles east of the vein
events.body: After eleven days on the road, Beasag's father builds a house on a nameless slope east of the vein, where the king's blood holds no hall and claims no grazing, among households that went out a generation before for their own reasons. He digs no pit under this floor.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A household turned out at Àth shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Liath dies at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: V. Of the Road

events.title: Sìleas Bhàn dies among her kin
events.body: Sìleas Bhàn, who opened the store within the bank by the count of mouths, dies among her own kin in the valley below the bank in her eight hundred and eightieth year; Tormod Liath comes down from the hall to stand at her burying.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years

told_in.book: Of the Eight Winds and Tormod the Grey
told_in.section: I. Of the Hill Given Over

events.title: Peigi born on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: A daughter is born to Lachlann Ruadh and named Peigi, black-haired and loud from her first night; she will meet her father's fosterling at the gate at fifteen and tell him he is too thin.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lachlann born on An Cnoc Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum Ciar stands where an heir stands

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: III. Of the Household of Lachlann Ruadh

events.title: Tormod Liath dies at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Tormod Liath dies in his own hall, without wound or fever, in the three hundred and eightieth year of his holding, having outlived three heirs of his own body and buried each at the bank he built. Dùn ìseal mourns him the length of a season; scarcely a household on the hill remembers a holder before him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beasag's household settles east of the vein

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hill in Its Old Age

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas takes up the hill
events.body: The holding of Dùn ìseal passes to Eilidh Ghlas, of the king's own blood, who has lived out those same generations in the valleys under the hill without thought of holding anything but her own hearth. She takes up the sharing custom with the hill itself, and weighs it at the bank herself in her first years.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hill in Its Old Age

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas asks after the pit at Àth shean
events.body: Before the bank is even swept for the season's grain, Eilidh Ghlas sends to Àth shean to ask after the pit still known by the name of the man who dug it. She is told it stands empty, and says only that this is well.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A household turned out at Àth shean

told_in.book: Of the Sharing before the Storms
told_in.section: VI. Of the Hill in Its Old Age

events.title: Calum Ciar stands where an heir stands
events.body: In the first sharing of his mother's own holding, Calum Ciar stands a pace behind Eilidh Ghlas's shoulder at the bank, and the ford takes notice of him for the first time. No one at Dùn ìseal afterward looks for another heir.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Peigi born on An Cnoc Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh weighs the old custom of the valleys

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: Eilidh weighs the old custom of the valleys
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas turns over, without acting on it, a custom she learned as a girl in the near valleys: that a household with two sons sometimes sends the younger to be raised at another hearth, so that he grows up loved rather than waiting on an inheritance not his.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Calum Ciar stands where an heir stands

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: The younger son born in a high river spring
events.body: A second son is born to Eilidh Ghlas at Dùn ìseal in a wet spring, when the river at Àth shean runs high enough to float the ford-stones. No reciter keeps his day, and none ever will.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas, tenth of the Stone Kings, of the king's blood, sends her younger son to the Red Hill to be fostered, the first fostering in either list. The son's name is not kept; only that he went, and that the peace of the ford held while he was there.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas takes up the hill

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The younger son born in a high river spring

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A boy who does not ask to ride out

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word sent west to An Cnoc Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum Ciar counts the miles at the gate

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh's parting at Àth shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas visits An Cnoc Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas dies

events.title: A boy who does not ask to ride out
events.body: Eilidh's younger son, six years old, watches his brother ride out with the men to renew the boundary stones and does not ask to go. His mother watches him a long while from the hall door and tells her steward that a house with only one door out of it is no house for a second son.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: Word sent west to An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas sends word to Lachlann Ruadh, holder of An Cnoc Ruadh, asking that he take her younger son to be raised in his household. She gives it out as a mother's wish that the boy learn a trade of his own; the ford's peace is served by it besides.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: Calum Ciar counts the miles at the gate
events.body: On the morning his brother leaves for An Cnoc Ruadh, Calum Ciar stands long at the gate after the party is out of sight, and tells a groom who asks him in out of the wind that he is only counting how many days fifty miles there and back will take.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: Eilidh's parting at Àth shean
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas walks with her son's party as far as Àth shean and kneels to his height at the turning of the roads, telling him he is not sent for any wrong of his, that An Cnoc Ruadh will be as much home to him as Dùn ìseal, and that she means to see him grown.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A mound left untouched on Rathad an t-Salainn

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: I. Of Eilidh's Two Sons

events.title: A mound left untouched on Rathad an t-Salainn
events.body: On the road west, the household man Donnchadh stops before a low green mound and will go no nearer to it, telling the boy only that it is older than the road and the salt trade. A wise traveller, he is told, lets such places lie as he lets a wasp's nest lie.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh's parting at Àth shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Rìonach's saying of the forked river

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: II. Of the Road West

events.title: Rìonach's saying of the forked river
events.body: Turning off Rathad an t-Salainn for her own kin at Àth shean, Rìonach tells the fosterling that a household not his own by birth is no loss to him but a doubling, as a forked river becomes two whole rivers rather than two lesser ones.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A mound left untouched on Rathad an t-Salainn

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: II. Of the Road West

events.title: The fosterling comes to An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas's younger son comes down to the western lake shore at evening and is met at the gate by Lachlann Ruadh and his daughter Peigi, who tells her father plainly that he is too thin and will need feeding, and carries in his one bundle herself.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lachlann Ruadh takes the fosterling

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: III. Of the Household of Lachlann Ruadh

events.title: Lachlann forbids the naming of a king's son
events.body: Lachlann Ruadh tells his household that the fosterling shall be called no king's son and no king's grandson, but a boy of the ford's people come to learn a trade, and warns his daughter Peigi he will hear of it if she names him otherwise again.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lachlann Ruadh takes the fosterling

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum Ciar given the boundary stones

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: III. Of the Household of Lachlann Ruadh

events.title: Lachlann Ruadh takes the fosterling
events.body: Lachlann Ruadh, holder of the Red Hill, takes the son of Eilidh Ghlas into his house. For it he is named Lachlann an Altraim, 'Lachlann of the fostering', and the Red Hill list calls him so more often than by his own name.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The fosterling comes to An Cnoc Ruadh

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Lachlann forbids the naming of a king's son

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Cnoc Ruadh list begins to call Lachlann of the fostering

events.title: Calum Ciar given the boundary stones
events.body: Calum Ciar is given the judging of the near valleys' boundary stones, the first trust of its kind laid on him, and settles a dispute between two herders over a shifted marker with a plainness his mother is said to have approved of.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lachlann forbids the naming of a king's son

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fosterling first put out on the lake

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: III. Of the Household of Lachlann Ruadh

events.title: The fosterling first put out on the lake
events.body: The fosterling is let out on Loch chrom in a boat for the first time, and comes back to An Cnoc Ruadh wet through and pleased with himself, word of it carried east along Rathad an t-Salainn to Dùn ìseal by the carriers who walk it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Calum Ciar given the boundary stones

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: III. Of the Household of Lachlann Ruadh

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas visits An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas comes to An Cnoc Ruadh as Lachlann Ruadh's guest and sits at his own board four days, asking after the tallies and the weather as she asks after her son. Walking with her son to the western point of the lake, she tells him she will not come again for some years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fosterling rakes salt without breaking the crust

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: III. Of the Household of Lachlann Ruadh

events.title: The fosterling rakes salt without breaking the crust
events.body: Lachlann Ruadh puts a salt-rake into the fosterling's hands on the drying platform above Loch chrom and shows him the turn of the wrist his own family has kept for generations. By the fourth stroke the boy lifts a clean sheet of crust whole, and Peigi Dhubh tells him it is better than she managed her own first year.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas visits An Cnoc Ruadh

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: IV. Of the Lake and the Name Not Kept

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh list begins to call Lachlann of the fostering
events.body: In these years An Cnoc Ruadh's reciters take up the habit of naming Lachlann Ruadh also Lachlann an Altraim, Lachlann of the fostering, until in time the second name is given by the list where the first once stood, and is never afterward unsaid.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lachlann Ruadh takes the fosterling

told_in.book: Of Eilidh the Grey and the Boy Who Went
told_in.section: IV. Of the Lake and the Name Not Kept

events.title: Beathag gives up the list of the slab's turns
events.body: Beathag, who has kept the household order of the slab's night watch eleven years, says at the Samhain gathering that she will keep the list no longer, after a household comes two nights running to a turn already missed. Thirty-one households now stand on it, too many for one memory to hold true.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig, first keeper by lot

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Turns that Wore Thin

events.title: The families agree to choose the slab's keeper by lot
events.body: At the slab's own clearing the families of Tobar dhìreach and the near valleys meet to settle the watch. An old man of the gathering proposes a single keeper chosen by lot, to hold the slab until death or infirmity, rather than turns by household. No vote is taken; the silence that follows is read as agreement.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig, first keeper by lot

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: I. Of the Turns that Wore Thin

events.title: Oighrig, first keeper by lot
events.body: The families who watch the slab agree to choose one keeper at a time by lot, and no longer to take turns by household. The first lot falls to a woman called Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill, and she keeps the slab for the rest of her life.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Beathag gives up the list of the slab's turns

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The families agree to choose the slab's keeper by lot

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lot falls to Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill dies keeping the slab

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lot falls to Gilleasbuig Beag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lot falls to Giorsal Bhàn

events.title: The lot falls to Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill
events.body: At the next full dark, thirty-one households send one member each to draw from a bag of thirty pebbles and one marked white. The lot falls to Oighrig, a herder's daughter of three-and-thirty, who carries the marked stone in her belt from that night for the rest of her life.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Oighrig, first keeper by lot

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig's father speaks of the shared name

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: II. Of the Lot

events.title: Oighrig's father speaks of the shared name
events.body: Walking home from the drawing, Oighrig's father Dòmhnall, a herder of the near slopes with no kinship to Rìghrean na Cloiche, tells her she will spend the rest of her keeping answering travellers who mistake her for blood of Dòmhnall Clachach, the second of that name to hold the north.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The lot falls to Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: II. Of the Lot

events.title: The keepers' house
events.body: A house is built beside the slab at Tobar dhìreach for the holder of the lot, its door facing the stone. It is rebuilt on the same footing many times. It is the first building on Dia-thìr made only to be near the vein.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh na Lice raised at Tobar dhìreach

events.title: Taigh na Lice raised at Tobar dhìreach
events.body: The families of the near valleys build Oighrig a house on the clearing's edge above the slab, its door set to face the stone and no other way, the first building on Dia-thìr raised for no reason but to stand near the vein.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers' house

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig sits her first winter alone by the slab

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: III. Of the House with the Door to the Slab

events.title: Oighrig sits her first winter alone by the slab
events.body: Moved into the new house at the first hard frost, Oighrig finds the keeper's long unbroken watch harder than any turn shared with her own household, and begins to notice things about the stain and the stone's temper that a thousand years of turned watches had never set down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh na Lice raised at Tobar dhìreach

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: III. Of the House with the Door to the Slab

events.title: The stone cup
events.body: Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill has a cup ground out of grey stone to the size of her own cupped hand, that the handful of coal may be the same for every household. The cup is carried round the hill settlements. Whether it outlasts the age is not known.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig comes to Niocol Snaidhear with her cupped hand

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first two stone cups crack in the grinding

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Niocol finishes the cup ground to Oighrig's hand

events.title: Oighrig comes to Niocol Snaidhear with her cupped hand
events.body: In her third year of keeping, Oighrig goes to the stone-worker Niocol Snaidhear and sets her own hand on his bench, cupped as for water, asking for a cup of grey stone that will hold exactly what it holds, so that no household's handful of coal runs bigger than another's by the accident of whose palm measures it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stone cup

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: IV. Of the Cup Ground to Her Hand

events.title: The first two stone cups crack in the grinding
events.body: Niocol Snaidhear loses a first cup to a hidden vein in the stone and a second to a hair-crack struck too hard near its finishing, and keeps the flawed second on his bench through the grinding of the third as a thing to learn the shape of a mistake by.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stone cup

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: IV. Of the Cup Ground to Her Hand

events.title: Niocol finishes the cup ground to Oighrig's hand
events.body: After eleven sittings across two summers, Niocol Snaidhear finishes a cup of grey stone fitted to Oighrig's hand, veined faintly white, holding exactly what her two cupped hands together cannot quite hold. She says the hand it copies is not her own but the hand of every hearth; Niocol begins a second cup as a copy before he is asked.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stone cup

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: IV. Of the Cup Ground to Her Hand

events.title: Word of the stone cup travels the near valleys
events.body: News of Oighrig's cup and the trouble it answers reaches stone-workers at three other places within the year: a woman at Àth gharbh, an old man at Achadh dhìreach, and a household at Cnoc chaol, each asking to grind a copy against it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The stone cup copied

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: V. Of the Copies

events.title: The stone cup copied
events.body: Copies of the keeper's cup are ground at Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol, each tried against the first by filling it with water. Thereafter the hill settlements measure the coal with one measure.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Word of the stone cup travels the near valleys

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig carries the first cup to Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The four cups are ground true at Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol

events.title: Oighrig carries the first cup to Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol
events.body: Oighrig walks the near valleys over a year with the first cup wrapped in wool, testing each new copy against it by pouring water from one to the other on a flat stone, and sending two cups at Achadh dhìreach and one at Cnoc chaol back to the wheel when the levels do not match.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stone cup copied

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: V. Of the Copies

events.title: The four cups are ground true at Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol
events.body: The copies of the stone cup are finished: quickest at Àth gharbh, where the worker measures against Niocol's cup throughout rather than a hand alone; slowest at Achadh dhìreach, an old man's hands steadied by his grandson through the last evenings; and, despite two false starts, fastest of all begun at Cnoc chaol.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The stone cup copied

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: V. Of the Copies

events.title: The meeting of the cups
events.body: The keeper's cup and its three copies are carried to a spring on the moor between Àth gharbh and Tobar dhìreach, set side by side on a flat stone and filled from the spring in turn. The place is called Coinneachadh nan Cupan, the meeting of the cups. The hill settlements return to it whenever a cup is broken and a new one must be tried.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneachadh nan Cupan on the moor

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hills measure the coal with one measure

events.title: Coinneachadh nan Cupan on the moor
events.body: At a nameless spring on the moor between Àth gharbh and Tobar dhìreach, chosen because it lies equal walking from all four places and belongs to no one household, the four keepers of the cups fill each from the same water on a flat stone and pass every cup down the line for each hand to weigh. The water stands level in all four; the place is called from that morning Coinneachadh nan Cupan.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The meeting of the cups

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: VI. Of the Meeting of the Cups

events.title: The hills measure the coal with one measure
events.body: From the year of Coinneachadh nan Cupan, the households from the slopes above Tobar dhìreach to the poor ground of Cnoc chaol measure their handful of the vein's coal by the one cup and its three copies, and not by the hand that happens to do the measuring, a change the reciters afterward give no more than a single line.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The meeting of the cups

told_in.book: Of Oighrig's Lot and the Stone Cup
told_in.section: VI. Of the Meeting of the Cups

events.title: Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill dies keeping the slab
events.body: Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill keeps the slab for the rest of her life, as the lot gave it her, and that rest is shorter than anyone at the clearing looked for: she dies in Taigh na Lice in the winter after Coinneachadh nan Cupan, and the families ask that a new lot be drawn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Oighrig, first keeper by lot

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: I. Of Gilleasbuig's Turn

events.title: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal
events.body: A keeper by lot, Gilleasbuig Beag, is found with a basket of broken coal from the vein in his own house. The households of the hills sit in judgement at the slab, row him out to Eilean chrom, and leave him there without a boat. He is the first known to be exiled for the vein.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A basket found under the bed-place

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleasbuig does not deny it

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The families judge Gilleasbuig by silence

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag rowed to Eilean chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A fire seen three nights on Eilean chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilean chrom left to itself

events.title: The lot falls to Gilleasbuig Beag
events.body: The bag of pebbles is filled again and passed among the households near the crack. The white stone comes out in the hand of Gilleasbuig Beag, a broad, quiet man known for mending roofs and cutting hazel, who goes pale rather than glad at what his open hand shows.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Oighrig, first keeper by lot

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: I. Of Gilleasbuig's Turn

events.title: A basket found under the bed-place
events.body: A kinswoman of Gilleasbuig, in his house on another errand, lifts a cloth expecting food and finds a basket of broken coal from the vein, more than any hand is owed by the handful. She says nothing that day, but tells her husband before she sleeps, and within three days the near valley knows.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: I. Of Gilleasbuig's Turn

events.title: Gilleasbuig does not deny it
events.body: Called to the clearing, Gilleasbuig Beag owns the basket at once and says he took the coal against a hard winter, for an old mother who sleeps cold, and for no other use. He asks, when the judgement is given, what the stone gains by the coal's return that his mother does not lose by going without it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: II. Of the Judgement at the Slab

events.title: The families judge Gilleasbuig by silence
events.body: The households argue long in the cold before an old woman of Cnoc chaol says what none of the near families will say first: that the vein was never any one hearth's to keep behind a cloth, however true the love that took it. The clearing's silence, held past any voice rising to answer it, stands as the judgement.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: II. Of the Judgement at the Slab

events.title: Gilleasbuig Beag rowed to Eilean chrom
events.body: Three men of the near households row Gilleasbuig Beag out to Eilean chrom and put him ashore, then pull back to open water and leave him without a boat to return in. He is the first anyone remembers exiled for the vein.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: III. Of Eilean chrom

events.title: A fire seen three nights on Eilean chrom
events.body: The near coast watches a small fire on Eilean chrom's low rise the first night, smaller the second, and a coal's worth of red at dusk the third, gone before full dark. No fire is seen there again, and no boat is sent to learn why.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: III. Of Eilean chrom

events.title: The basket set inside Taigh na Lice
events.body: The kinswoman who found the coal carries the basket to Taigh na Lice at Tobar dhìreach and sets it under its cloth just inside the door. No household proposes burning it; it was not theirs to burn before Gilleasbuig took it, and the judgement has settled that it never will be.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The coal returned to the crack

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Lot and the Basket Unburned

events.title: The lot falls to Giorsal Bhàn
events.body: A new lot is drawn from the same bag that gave the stone to Oighrig and then to Gilleasbuig, and this time it is Giorsal Bhàn's hand that opens on the white pebble. She closes her hand on it and says she will keep it, and moves into Taigh na Lice before the month is out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Oighrig, first keeper by lot

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Lot and the Basket Unburned

events.title: The coal returned to the crack
events.body: The coal from Gilleasbuig Beag's house is neither burned nor kept. The keeper after him carries it back to the slab and lays it beneath, piece by piece. The tellings make much of it: the coal went home.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The basket set inside Taigh na Lice

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Giorsal lays the coal back under the slab

links.label: Leads to
links.title: "The coal went home"

events.title: Giorsal lays the coal back under the slab
events.body: On a still morning near the year's turn, Giorsal Bhàn kneels at the slab's lower edge and presses the broken coal back into the gap between stone and earth, piece by piece, returning a second day to finish it, until the basket holds nothing at all.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal returned to the crack

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal that Went Home

events.title: "The coal went home"
events.body: By the summer after Giorsal Bhàn empties the basket into the slab's edge, the four words are already going round the near valley as if they had always been there: that the coal went home. No one near the crack can afterward say who spoke them first.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal returned to the crack

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: V. Of the Coal that Went Home

events.title: Eilean chrom left to itself
events.body: The island stands ungrazed and unfished through the years after Gilleasbuig Beag's exile. Children of the near coast are told not to ask about the island with the spring on it, and are given the same short answer when they ask anyway.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: III. Of Eilean chrom

events.title: Calum Ciar asks for the lot
events.body: Calum Ciar, the elder son of Eilidh Ghlas and eleventh of the Stone Kings, asks that the keeper's lot be drawn at Dùn ìseal in his sight. The households at the slab refuse him. The list sets down the refusal, which is more than it sets down of most things.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum Ciar comes to the clearing

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The families refuse Calum Ciar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum Ciar dies at Dùn ìseal

events.title: Calum Ciar comes to the clearing
events.body: Calum Ciar, elder son of Eilidh Ghlas and eleventh to hold Dùn ìseal under the king, walks up the valley to the slab and asks that the next lot be drawn at Dùn ìseal in his own sight, so the hill may see the vein's lot drawn as honestly as the hill's own.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Calum Ciar asks for the lot

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: VI. Of Calum Ciar and the Lot at Dùn ìseal

events.title: The families refuse Calum Ciar
events.body: The households near the crack answer Calum Ciar with the same held silence they gave Gilleasbuig Beag: the lot has been drawn at the slab since the custom began and will go on being drawn there, in the sight of whoever near the crack cares to watch. Calum Ciar thanks them and does not argue it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Calum Ciar asks for the lot

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: VI. Of Calum Ciar and the Lot at Dùn ìseal

events.title: Calum Ciar puts the question to the king
events.body: At the ford that summer, Calum Ciar carries the same question to the king. The king hears him without anger or haste and says only that the slab is older than the hill, and older than the grove of his own crowning, and that he will not overrule so old a thing for the asking of a man not two hundred years in the world.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The kings and the keepers

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: VII. Of the Unwritten Line

events.title: The kings and the keepers
events.body: After the refusal of Calum Ciar the lot is still drawn at the slab. The holders of the hill rule the grazing and the gatherings under the king, but not the vein, and the king does not overrule the slab. The line between the two holds for the rest of the age. It is not yet written anywhere.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Calum Ciar puts the question to the king

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The line between hill and slab holds unwritten

events.title: The line between hill and slab holds unwritten
events.body: Calum Ciar goes home from the ford and asks nothing more of it. The hill rules the grazing and calls the gatherings, answering to the king for both; the keepers rule the vein, answering to no one the telling can name. The line is sworn to in no words either side writes down, and it holds.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The kings and the keepers

told_in.book: Of the Coal that Went Home
told_in.section: VII. Of the Unwritten Line

events.title: A' Ghaoth Dhubh
events.body: A storm called A' Ghaoth Dhubh, the Black Wind, strips the thatch from every house on the east coast from Cuan ruadh to Ceann chiar. Of all storms it is the eldest whose name is kept.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Ghaoth Dhubh strips the east coast

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The coast's fishing fails before winter begins

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The coast names the storm A' Ghaoth Dhubh

events.title: The sharing holds after the Black Wind
events.body: The settlements of the east coast feed the people of Cuan ruadh through a whole winter out of their shared surplus. None on that coast is known to die of hunger that season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inland valleys hear of the coast's ruin

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The valleys send grain to Cuan ruadh unasked

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The sharing reaches the east coast

events.title: A' Ghaoth Dhubh strips the east coast
events.body: A storm out of the south-east strikes before dawn with almost no warning, stripping the thatch from every roof between Cuan ruadh and Ceann chiar and driving three unhauled boats onto the rocks below the headland. No one of that coast dies in it, though many households lose stores, shelter and boats within a single day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A' Ghaoth Dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: I. Of the Wind that Took the Thatch

events.title: The coast's fishing fails before winter begins
events.body: Of Cuan ruadh's eleven boats, four are broken past mending and a fifth needs a new keel; granaries stand open to the sky along the whole stripped coast. A fishing that has never in memory failed outright fails that winter for want of boats and stores enough to work it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A' Ghaoth Dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: I. Of the Wind that Took the Thatch

events.title: The coast names the storm A' Ghaoth Dhubh
events.body: The eldest of that coast, having no name ready when the storm struck, name it afterward for the ash-dark sky it leaves behind for three days. No reciter of the hill amends the name; every storm to strike that shore since is measured against it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A' Ghaoth Dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: I. Of the Wind that Took the Thatch

events.title: Inland valleys hear of the coast's ruin
events.body: A trader who meant to buy salt fish at Cuan ruadh finds instead a shore of broken boats and bare roof-trees, and carries word of it a day and more west to valleys that had never before troubled themselves over that coast's weather.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The sharing holds after the Black Wind

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: II. Of the Winter the Custom Reached the Coast

events.title: The valleys send grain to Cuan ruadh unasked
events.body: Single households send what they can spare because a neighbour has already sent something, until the scatter of gifts grows too large for any one house to account for, and the valleys' holders agree to weigh and send it on by the count of mouths, as the sharing is kept at Dùn ìseal, though none there had been taught the custom directly.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The sharing holds after the Black Wind

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: II. Of the Winter the Custom Reached the Coast

events.title: The beacon at Baile ìseal
events.body: A fire is built on the eastern cape where Taigh-solais Baile ìseal now stands, kept by the households of the coast in turn. It is lit to bring boats home in a storm, the tellings say, and not to warn them off.

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The second cairn on the eastern cape

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lìleas begins to watch the dark return of the boats

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lìleas's household agrees to the fire

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eastern fire is first kept

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A boat is brought home to the eastern fire

events.title: The sharing reaches the east coast
events.body: Grain, salted meat and wool for roofing come down to Cuan ruadh through the winter on carts and cattle-backs, weighed by mouths and given without reckoning who at the coast has lost most. No household of that coast starves; the coast calls the custom only the bringing-in, or the help.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The sharing holds after the Black Wind

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: II. Of the Winter the Custom Reached the Coast

events.title: Lìleas begins to watch the dark return of the boats
events.body: One-and-twenty that hard winter, with her father's hand maimed and the household's boat unfit to swim, Lìleas of Cuan ruadh spends idle hours on the shingle and comes to notice what the coast has never put into words: that a boat coming home after dark has nothing to steer the last stretch by but memory and the sound of the surf.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Baile ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: III. Of Lìleas, Who Watched the Boats Come In

events.title: Lìleas's household agrees to the fire
events.body: Lìleas puts the keeping of a fire on the cape east of the village to her own household over a thin meal; her father, no longer trusting his maimed hand on a line, sees no harm in it and asks only that she carry the work herself.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Baile ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fire She Kept on the Eastern Cape

events.title: The eastern fire is first kept
