events.body: Lìleas and her younger brother carry driftwood and peat up the cape through a month of short winter days and build the fire in a stone-walled pit, driving flame and smoke seaward. She keeps it alone through nights that find no boat needing it, and more than one household of the village climbs the cape only to sit an hour with her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Baile ìseal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of the eastern fire travels the coast roads

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fire She Kept on the Eastern Cape

events.title: The beacon at Muileann bheag
events.body: A second shore-fire is kept on the north coast, on the point where Taigh-solais Muileann bheag stands now. Under the tower the ash goes down through three yards of fire-reddened soil.

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Three yards of ash at Muileann bheag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A fire is raised on the northern point

events.title: The beacon at Àth dhearg
events.body: Households of the north-east coast keep a fire on the cape where Taigh-solais Àth dhearg now stands, and cut steps up to it from the shore. The steps are narrower than those at Seann Bhral, and less worn.

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The households of Àth dhearg asked hearth by hearth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seathan mac Pheadair keeps the north-eastern fire

events.title: Word of the eastern fire travels the coast roads
events.body: Traders and travellers carry word of the fire on Cuan ruadh's cape along the roads faster than its own light could reach, and coasts that have suffered their own bad weather begin to want fires of their own.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The eastern fire is first kept

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: V. Of the Fires that Answered It

events.title: A fire is raised on the northern point
events.body: On ground already scorched black by older shore-fires, the households of the hardest-running coast raise a fire that burns steadier from its first season, having Lìleas's year of trial to learn by before laying their own wood.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Muileann bheag

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: V. Of the Fires that Answered It

events.title: Seathan mac Pheadair keeps the north-eastern fire
events.body: On the cape where the passage to the deeper water runs narrowest, a man named Seathan mac Pheadair takes up the keeping of a fire much as Lìleas had, and cuts a stroke on a stone at its edge for every ship's light he sees pass safe by it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Àth dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: V. Of the Fires that Answered It

events.title: The beacon at Tobar dhearg
events.body: A fire is kept for the boats of the south coast on the southern cape where Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg stands. With Baile chrom, Baile ìseal, Muileann bheag and Àth dhearg the coasts of the island are lit at five points.

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: Torcall's first cairn on the Tobar dhearg headland

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The southern cape completes the five fires

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A reciter names them the five fires

events.title: The southern cape completes the five fires
events.body: Last of the four new fires and by every account the surest, the households of the southern cape raise theirs on a mound of stacked stone breast-high, clear of the spray. With the older fire on the Baile chrom headland, the coasts of Dia-thìr are now lit at five points.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Tobar dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: V. Of the Fires that Answered It

events.title: A reciter names them the five fires
events.body: Before the southern mound is even finished, a reciter of that coast says that a boat lost off any shore of Dia-thìr now has a fire somewhere within its sight to steer toward, and names the five together the five fires, a name the coast keeps on every telling since.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Tobar dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: V. Of the Fires that Answered It

events.title: A boat is brought home to the eastern fire
events.body: Blown off its own water by a wind that will not hold steady, a boat out of a coast two villages north finds the coast of Dia-thìr only by Lìleas's fire, burning high on the cape with no house near it. The crew comes ashore whole, and Lìleas tells the captain the fire is kept for whichever boat needs it, no more for him than for any other.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon at Baile ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Black Wind and the Five Fires
told_in.section: VI. Of the Boat that Came Home by It

events.title: The Sea-Watcher seen from Seann Skell
events.body: Four watchers on the north-western tower at Seann Skell see a back as long as three boats rise and go under off the point. It is the first sighting of the Sea-Watcher tied to a named place and a count of witnesses.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The watchers see the long back in the water

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of the sighting runs round the bay

events.title: Wreckage in the western water
events.body: For a season planks of stitched boats, broken small, wash up along the western shore below the waters where raiders are afterwards seen. No bodies come with them, and no settlement on that coast lacks a boat.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Stitched planks come ashore south of Seann Skell

links.label: At the same time
links.title: No household will claim the wreck

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Micheil Beag lays the planks against his wall

events.title: The watchers see the long back in the water
events.body: Four men keeping the tower at Seann Skell watch a back long as three boats rise off the point in the failing light and go under without a sound. Their four tellings differ in every small particular but agree on the length and the silence.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The Sea-Watcher seen from Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: I. Of the Watch at Seann Skell

events.title: Word of the sighting runs round the bay
events.body: The tale of the tower's watch grows a head and a neck by the time it has gone twice round the bay of Seann Skell, though the old women of that coast say only that the sea shows itself when it chooses and take no boat off the water for the telling.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Sea-Watcher seen from Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: I. Of the Watch at Seann Skell

events.title: Stitched planks come ashore south of Seann Skell
events.body: Through a season the wrack south of the tower gives up narrow stitched planks from more than one hull, shaped for open water and like nothing built on that coast, with not one scrap of cord, tool or bone to say what rode in them.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Wreckage in the western water

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: II. Of the Planks on the Western Sand

events.title: No household will claim the wreck
events.body: Asked along the shore, no household admits to a boat of its own building broken among the planks, nor lacks a man, woman or child it cannot otherwise account for; the wreck stays a wreck with no name and no mourner.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Wreckage in the western water

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: II. Of the Planks on the Western Sand

events.title: Micheil Beag lays the planks against his wall
events.body: A fisherman of that coast, Micheil Beag, gathers the stitched wood along one wall and pieces two curved lengths of hull back into shape, finding boats narrower and longer in the beam than any the coast builds for its own close fishing.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Wreckage in the western water

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: II. Of the Planks on the Western Sand

events.title: Anndra Breac comes to the wall of planks
events.body: Anndra Breac, a teller who has walked the western shore twenty years and more without a household of his own, hears Micheil Beag out and returns to look at the planking again by firelight more than once before the season turns.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: III. Of Anndra Breac, Who Made a Telling

events.title: Anndra shapes a fourth telling
events.body: Turning the planks and the tower's tale over through the winter, Anndra comes to think a boat lost whole but for its wood argues not a wreck close to shore but a crossing once made, long before any telling now kept remembers the making of it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: III. Of Anndra Breac, Who Made a Telling

events.title: The coast hears him out without agreeing
events.body: Anndra tries the telling first on households that have fed him twenty years running; none of them denies it outright, and an old woman near Seann Skell tells him a tale a man cannot leave alone wants telling somewhere it will be properly heard.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: III. Of Anndra Breac, Who Made a Telling

events.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'
events.body: At the ford gathering Anndra Breac, a teller of the western coast, recites a telling in which the people came to Dia-thìr over the sea. The households of the hills shout him down, and he is put out of the ford for the rest of his life. His telling is not kept; only the memory that he told it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Anndra Breac comes to the wall of planks

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Anndra shapes a fourth telling

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The coast hears him out without agreeing

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Anndra Breac tells the crossing at the ford

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The crowd shouts him down

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Every hearth of Dia-thìr closes to him

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The king laughs once and falls quiet

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king will not choose between the tellings

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anndra Breac walks south along the western strand

events.title: Anndra Breac tells the crossing at the ford
events.body: At the yearly gathering, by the largest fire he can get a footing at, Anndra Breac tells a telling in which the hill-folk crossed the sea in boats once and lost more of themselves to the crossing than any telling now remembers.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: III. Of Anndra Breac, Who Made a Telling

events.title: The crowd shouts him down
events.body: An old man of a hill household calls out that no teller says the hill-folk came from anywhere, for they were always here, and others take up the shout until Anndra's own voice can no longer be heard over the fire.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: IV. Of the Ford

events.title: Every hearth of Dia-thìr closes to him
events.body: No household strikes him and none needs to; by the roads home from the ford it is already understood that Anndra Breac is not to be fed at a hill hearth again, and by the following spring not one has.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: IV. Of the Ford

events.title: The king laughs once and falls quiet
events.body: Standing near enough his own fire to hear the telling, the king laughs low at some point in it those nearest him cannot agree on afterward, does not join the shouting nor still it, and is seen quiet the rest of that evening in a way his own kin know to read.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: V. Of the King, Who Laughed and Then Was Quiet

events.title: The king will not choose between the tellings
events.body: Asked afterward by a woman of his own kin whether the teller spoke true, the king answers only that he has heard many tellings of where his own people came from and has never troubled to choose one over another.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: V. Of the King, Who Laughed and Then Was Quiet

events.title: The doctrine said at the column
events.body: After Anndra Breac, the saying cut on the column at Cnoc ghorm is spoken aloud at the opening of the ford gathering: we did not come; we were here. From this time it is said as a rule, and not only held as a belief.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The saying is spoken at the opening of the gathering

events.title: The saying is spoken at the opening of the gathering
events.body: The gathering at the ford opens for the first time with the saying of Calbh Cnoc ghorm spoken aloud before any business begins, we did not come, we were here, a thing said together from that year rather than kept only in each hearth's own quiet belief.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The doctrine said at the column

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: VI. Of the Saying Spoken at the Opening

events.title: Anndra Breac walks south along the western strand
events.body: Seen once more below the tower at Seann Skell, walking the strand where the stitched planks still lie against Micheil Beag's wall, Anndra Breac walks on and does not look back; no teller of that coast claims to have fed, spoken to or buried him after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Anndra Breac says 'we came'

told_in.book: Of Anndra Breac
told_in.section: VI. Of the Saying Spoken at the Opening

events.title: The keepers of the Ros dhomhain rock
events.body: The tide-rock at Ros dhomhain passes to Seònaid Mhòr, who cuts her marks in pairs, one for high water and one for low. Her pairs can be read still. The keepers after her go back to single marks.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seònaid Mhòr cuts paired marks at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seònaid Mhòr cuts a last pair of marks for him

events.title: A third tide-rock at Inis thais
events.body: Households at Inis thais cut their own high-water marks on the harbour rock, at the interval of Ros dhomhain. So three rocks are kept side by side. None tells why the interval is what it is.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The spacing of the marks travels without its reasoning

events.title: Seònaid Mhòr cuts paired marks at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The keeper of the Ros dhomhain tide-rock takes to cutting two strokes for every tide instead of one, a mark for the water's highest reach and a shorter mark beside it for its lowest ebb, so that whoever reads the rock after her has the whole of the water's motion and not only its rising.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers of the Ros dhomhain rock

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: I. Of the Paired Marks at Ros dhomhain

events.title: The spacing of the marks travels without its reasoning
events.body: Households at Inis thais's own harbour, hearing only that Ros dhomhain's keeper cuts her marks at a certain interval, begin cutting their own high-water marks at that same spacing on a rock of their own, though none of them can say why that width and no other.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A third tide-rock at Inis thais

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: II. Of the Third Rock at Inis thais

events.title: Peigi Dhubh calls for a landing of laid stone
events.body: At the household's board, Lachlann Ruadh's daughter says plainly that a hill whose wealth now travels by water deserves better than an open shingle beach a winter tide can rearrange. Her father agrees, and the households of An Cnoc Ruadh give a season's labour to the work.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Red Hill's harbour

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: III. Of the Landing of Laid Stone

events.title: Ros dhomhain grows
events.body: Ros dhomhain becomes the greatest settlement on the shores of Loch chrom, some sixty houses round the tide-rock. Its people fish now from boats and not from the shore.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Houses draw in round the rock and the landing

events.title: The stone landing is set at the river-mouth
events.body: Course on course of quarried stone is laid where the fresh water of the lake meets the tide from the sea, until a boat can come alongside at any state of the water without a hand needed to haul it clear of the mud: An Cnoc Ruadh's first way onto open water that does not depend on a beach's mercy.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Red Hill's harbour

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: III. Of the Landing of Laid Stone

events.title: Lachlann Ruadh falls ill
events.body: A chill taken wading the shallows to right a boat settles in Lachlann an Altraim's chest and will not lift with the spring. He is five-and-sixty years old, an age An Cnoc Ruadh reckons past complaint for a man who has spent his whole life wet to the knee in cold water.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Dhubh of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: IV. Of Lachlann's Dying

events.title: Lachlann asks that the fostering be ended
events.body: On one of his last evenings Lachlann tells his daughter that a fostering kept a season too long stops being a kindness and becomes only a habit no one has ended, and asks her not to let her own fondness be the reason the peace of the ford goes one day longer without its proper marking.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Dhubh of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: IV. Of Lachlann's Dying

events.title: Lachlann Ruadh dies at five-and-sixty
events.body: He dies in the hall he was born in, his daughter's hand in his own, the household gathered at the door with no closer claim on the bedside than the years they gave the hill. He held An Cnoc Ruadh one-and-sixty years.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Dhubh of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: IV. Of Lachlann's Dying

events.title: Peigi Dhubh holds An Cnoc Ruadh at forty
events.body: She sits down at the board the morning after her father's burial and asks for the tallies before she asks for anything else. An Cnoc Ruadh's own steward says afterward that she keeps them straighter than her father ever did.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Dhubh of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: V. Of Peigi Dhubh's Holding

events.title: The Red Hill's harbour
events.body: The households of the Red Hill build a landing of laid stone at the river-mouth below the hill, where the harbour of Cathair dhearg is now. It is the Red Hill's first way onto the water, and by the lake and the Abhainn gheal to the sea.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Peigi Dhubh calls for a landing of laid stone

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The stone landing is set at the river-mouth

events.title: Peigi Dhubh of the Red Hill
events.body: Peigi Dhubh holds the Red Hill after Lachlann an Altraim. She sends the fostered son of Dùn ìseal home grown, with gifts of salt, and the peace of the ford holds a generation more.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Lachlann Ruadh falls ill

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Lachlann asks that the fostering be ended

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Lachlann Ruadh dies at five-and-sixty

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Peigi Dhubh holds An Cnoc Ruadh at forty

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi tells the fosterling he is to go home

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Dhubh dies on An Cnoc Ruadh

events.title: Houses draw in round the rock and the landing
events.body: Boats from harbours further down the coast begin putting in at the new landing rather than carrying on to open beaches, and the scattered houses of that shore draw in closer round the tide-rock and the stone together until some sixty stand there, their people fishing now from boats of their own building.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ros dhomhain grows

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: III. Of the Landing of Laid Stone

events.title: The foster-son returns
events.body: The son of Eilidh Ghlas comes home from the Red Hill to Dùn ìseal, bringing the salt-songs of the west. The Stone Kings' list gives him no name and no reign; he is remembered only as the one who went.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The foster-son of Dùn ìseal comes home

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum Ciar does not know his own brother

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas knows her son at the door

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Rìghrean na Cloiche' list keeps him no name

events.title: Peigi tells the fosterling he is to go home
events.body: Walking the new stone landing with him in the last light of an evening, Peigi says her father was right, and that she means to send him home before the year turns, with salt enough for a household to carry as gift and not as trade, so the hill of Dùn ìseal will know he is sent back with honour.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Peigi Dhubh of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: V. Of Peigi Dhubh's Holding

events.title: Seònaid Mhòr cuts a last pair of marks for him
events.body: On the evening before the train leaves, the keeper of the tide-rock cuts one more pair of marks at the rock's edge, though the tide calls for none, and will not say plainly what they are for beyond that the rock has marked every tide of his years there and should mark the last of them too.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers of the Ros dhomhain rock

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: VI. Of the Leaving of the Red Hill

events.title: The first songs kept
events.body: The salt-songs of the south and west are sung at the raking of the pans. They are the oldest songs on Dia-thìr whose words are said to survive: a refrain of four lines, which no one can now wholly construe.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The salt refrain is sung at the pans of Baile ghorm

events.title: Bone pipes at Cnoc àrsaidh
events.body: Pipes of hollow bird-bone, bored with four holes, are made in a house at the southern Cnoc àrsaidh near the panther road. They are the oldest instruments of the island.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Gilleonan bores the first bone pipes

events.title: The panthers turn back
events.body: The great cats come down the panther road near Imrich nam Pantar and turn back at the foothills without crossing. The hill-folk read it for a hard winter and store double. The winter is hard.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Three cats turn back at the pass

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The households along the road store double

events.title: Gilleonan bores the first bone pipes
events.body: At Cnoc àrsaidh, Gilleonan bores four holes along a hollow bird-bone and finds a note he can raise and lower at will; children of three households gather to hear him play, the first instrument the island's tellers count as more than a horn blown flat.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Bone pipes at Cnoc àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: I. Of the Bone Pipes and the Turning of the Cats

events.title: Three cats turn back at the pass
events.body: Watchers along Imrich nam Pantar see three great cats, on three different days, halt at the throat of the highest pass and turn back south rather than finish the crossing every household's memory says they always finish.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The panthers turn back

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: I. Of the Bone Pipes and the Turning of the Cats

events.title: The households along the road store double
events.body: Reading the cats' turning for a kinder ground left behind and a harder winter ahead, the households nearest the pass lay in double against a season no cat that year would risk crossing into, and go short of nothing before the thaw.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The panthers turn back

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: I. Of the Bone Pipes and the Turning of the Cats

events.title: Iain drives cattle onto Imrich nam Pantar
events.body: With the household's grazing run thin, Iain of Muileann bhàn takes four men and forty head of thin cattle up into the passes against the custom that keeps the crossing season's road clear of herds, meaning to bring them down fattened within the week.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The cattle lost in the passes

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: II. Of Iain Buachaille and the Cattle in the Passes

events.title: The cattle lost in the passes
events.body: Herders from Muileann bhàn drive cattle into the passes out of season, against the custom of the crossing. The panthers take thirty head in a night, and the herders come down with nothing.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Iain drives cattle onto Imrich nam Pantar

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The panthers take thirty head in the night

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Iain is lamed in the dark

events.title: The foster-son of Dùn ìseal comes home
events.body: He walks Rathad an t-Salainn east with a train of laden pack-beasts and three of An Cnoc Ruadh's household, and comes in sight of the hill of Rìghrean na Cloiche on the seventh evening, four-and-twenty years after he first walked the same road west at six years old.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The foster-son returns

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road East

events.title: Calum Ciar does not know his own brother
events.body: Meeting An Cnoc Ruadh's train at the gate in his mother's stead, Calum Ciar asks the fosterling which of the household he might be, a lake wind and four-and-twenty years having left nothing in him his brother's eye could fasten on as kin.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The foster-son returns

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Brother Who Did Not Know Him

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas knows her son at the door
events.body: Carried out to the hall door, Eilidh speaks her younger son's name before he has said a word to tell her who he is, and weeps and holds him a long while before she lets even her elder son greet him in turn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The foster-son returns

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Brother Who Did Not Know Him

events.title: The salt refrain is sung at the pans of Baile ghorm
events.body: At the fires of the salt-rakers he teaches, without meaning to teach anything, the four-line refrain sung at the crust on An Cnoc Ruadh's own lake shore. An old raker keeps it whole from a single hearing, and it runs on afterward at the sea-shore pans in words An Cnoc Ruadh itself can no longer wholly construe.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first songs kept

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: IX. Of the Songs Sung at the Pans

events.title: Rìghrean na Cloiche' list keeps him no name
events.body: When the reciters after Eilidh set down her reign and her sons, Calum Ciar takes his place among the holders as every holder before him; of the one who went to An Cnoc Ruadh and came home grown, no year, no reign and no deed is written, and the list stands as if she bore only the one son.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The foster-son returns

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: IX. Of the Songs Sung at the Pans

events.title: The panthers take thirty head in the night
events.body: On the fourth night a string of cats, the last and largest of that year's crossing, comes down on the herd; by first light thirty of the forty head are taken or scattered beyond finding.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The cattle lost in the passes

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: II. Of Iain Buachaille and the Cattle in the Passes

events.title: Iain is lamed in the dark
events.body: Throwing himself clear of a claw he never clearly sees, Iain twists his leg under him against a hidden stone; it sets crooked at the hip, and he walks from that winter with a stick and a roll to one side.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The cattle lost in the passes

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: II. Of Iain Buachaille and the Cattle in the Passes

events.title: Baile dhomhain cuts the first season's sign
events.body: The households of Baile dhomhain begin cutting a mark into every gatepost at the start of the crossing season and scraping it away at its close, the first mark the island's tellers know cut for a season rather than for any single event.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The panther season kept at Baile dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: III. Of the Gatepost Sign and the Boats Named for Wind

events.title: Caol bheag names its boats for the winds
events.body: The fishing households of Caol bheag fix the custom of naming each boat for the wind it is built to fish in, holding a boat unlucky under any other wind and never giving a drowned boat's name again.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Boats named for the winds

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: III. Of the Gatepost Sign and the Boats Named for Wind

events.title: A wind-name is cut at Seann Chwen
events.body: A cutter of that household sets one of Na h-Ochd Gaothan' names beside Seann-Dhaoine' own marks on the great boulder at Seann Chwen, choosing that stone, by his own word, because the name wanted a stone already old.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The wind-stone at Seann Chwen

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: IV. Of the Wind-Stone and the Broken Grave

events.title: A family takes up the old burial ground unasked
events.body: Kin new to that country begin clearing the thorn from the old burial ground's rows each spring though none of their own dead lie there, and within a few years every household near it has come to trust the keeping to them alone.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The Tuam keepers

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: IV. Of the Wind-Stone and the Broken Grave

events.title: The panther season kept at Baile dhomhain
events.body: At Baile dhomhain in the south the households cut a sign on their gateposts at the start of the crossing season and scrape it off at its end. It is the first mark made on the island for a season.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Baile dhomhain cuts the first season's sign

events.title: The wind-stone at Seann Chwen
events.body: One of the eight wind-names is cut in the Dia-thìreach manner on a boulder at the central Seann Chwen, over an older mark of the Seann-Dhaoine. In few places do the marks of the two peoples touch.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A wind-name is cut at Seann Chwen

events.title: Boats named for the winds
events.body: The fishing households of Caol bheag, who fish the north coast from the mouth of the Abhainn ghorm, name their boats for the winds they fish in. A boat named for the wrong wind is held unlucky, and the name of a boat that sinks is never given again.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Caol bheag names its boats for the winds

events.title: The Tuam keepers
events.body: A family dwelling by Tuam Cnoc dhìreach takes on the clearing of thorn from the old graves. They bury none of their own there. They only keep it.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A family takes up the old burial ground unasked

events.title: A grave at Tuam opened
events.body: Diggers laying a new row at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach break into a grave older than any they knew, lined with slabs cut in the manner of the Seann-Dhaoine. They close it and move the row, and none opens that grave again.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Diggers break into a slab-lined grave

links.label: Leads to
links.title: No digger tries the older grave again

events.title: Diggers break into a slab-lined grave
events.body: Cutting a new row further back than any before it, the keepers' own diggers break into an older grave lined close with cut slabs in the manner of Seann-Dhaoine; they close it as carefully as they opened it and move the row a spear's length off.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A grave at Tuam opened

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: IV. Of the Wind-Stone and the Broken Grave

events.title: No digger tries the older grave again
events.body: The keeping family's eldest holds that a ground kept for the dead does not want its keepers asking after graves it was never given to keep, and no digger of that ground troubles the older grave a second time.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A grave at Tuam opened

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: IV. Of the Wind-Stone and the Broken Grave

events.title: Pilgrims at Coille Naomh Muileann chiar
events.body: People begin to walk to the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar and sit a night at the line of the trees without entering. Their small fires, each of a single night, lie all along the edge.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Pilgrims begin sitting at Coille Naomh Muileann chiar

events.title: Pilgrims begin sitting at Coille Naomh Muileann chiar
events.body: People from households that have never before walked so far begin coming singly and in pairs to sit a single night at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, keeping a small fire that burns out before morning, and go home saying only that the night leaves them quieter.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Pilgrims at Coille Naomh Muileann chiar

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: V. Of the Pilgrims and the Child Lost at Cnoc bheag

events.title: Settlers from An Cnoc Ruadh raise the first house at Cnoc bheag
events.body: Households come down from An Cnoc Ruadh to build at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, taking timber only from the river's far side and never from the unclaimed wood, a line later marked by a row of unhewn stones.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The first house at Cnoc bheag

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: V. Of the Pilgrims and the Child Lost at Cnoc bheag

events.title: A child lost in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag
events.body: A child of the settlement at Cnoc bheag goes past the line of stones into Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag and is not found. The searchers stop at the stones, and the telling does not blame them.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A child of Cnoc bheag is lost past the stones

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Iain among the searchers who stop at the stones

events.title: A child of Cnoc bheag is lost past the stones
events.body: A boy not yet seven goes missing near the line of stones at Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag's edge; the settlement and its neighbours search three days into the wood without one sign of him.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A child lost in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: V. Of the Pilgrims and the Child Lost at Cnoc bheag

events.title: Iain among the searchers who stop at the stones
events.body: Lame still from the passes, Iain of Muileann bhàn joins the search at Cnoc bheag and is the first to say aloud that a wood no household will fell or build nearer than its own river is not a wood that gives back what it takes; the searchers stop at the line of stones, and no teller lays the stopping at their door.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A child lost in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: V. Of the Pilgrims and the Child Lost at Cnoc bheag

events.title: The first house at Cnoc bheag
events.body: Settlers from the Red Hill build at Cnoc bheag, near the edge of the forest. They take their timber from the far side of the river, and never from the unclaimed wood.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Settlers from An Cnoc Ruadh raise the first house at Cnoc bheag

events.title: The spring at Muileann ruadh
events.body: Pilgrims come in numbers to the warm springs at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, and a ring of shelters is built there. Here is set the eldest healing-tale of Dia-thìr: a herder came lame and walked home.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Iain goes to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Iain walks home whole; the cure-tale is set

events.title: Iain goes to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
events.body: Seven-and-twenty years lame, and told by a neighbour of a warm water under the mountain that has eased other travellers' old hurts, Iain walks south on his stick and sits in the pool at first light, the heat working into the crooked hip as no binding ever had.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The spring at Muileann ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: VI. Of the Warm Springs

events.title: Iain walks home whole; the cure-tale is set
events.body: Iain stays three days at the warm water and walks the road home to Muileann bhàn on his own two legs without the stick, in half the days the journey south had cost him; his own household, seeing him come up the rise, takes him at first for a stranger. The tale kept of it is the oldest cure the springs are told for: he came lame, and he walked home.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The spring at Muileann ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: VI. Of the Warm Springs

events.title: The Hollow Man seen again
events.body: Two herders passing the Doire uaine hills after dark see a figure walk the ridge with no breath showing in the cold. They had no fire lit, and so, the telling says, they lived.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Two herders see Marbh-bheò on the ridge

events.title: Two herders see Marbh-bheò on the ridge
events.body: Caught by dark on the way home, two herders near Marbh-bheò's hills see a shape walk the ridge above them showing no breath in the bitter cold, though their own hangs white before them; they had lit no fire that evening, and so, the telling says, they lived.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The Hollow Man seen again

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: VII. Of the Hollow Man and the Covered Hearth

events.title: The covered hearth spreads
events.body: The covered hearth, pit-dug and roofed, spreads from the Doire uaine hills to the settlements about Muileann chiar. From this comes the later rule that no open fire is lit on those slopes after dark.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The covered hearth spreads and the night rule hardens

events.title: Peigi Dhubh dies on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Peigi Dhubh, who laid the stone landing and kept the tallies straighter than her father, dies on An Cnoc Ruadh in her seventy-sixth year, having held it five-and-thirty years; her boats go out the morning after her burying as she asked.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Peigi Dhubh of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: V. Of Peigi Dhubh's Holding

events.title: The covered hearth spreads and the night rule hardens
events.body: The pit-dug, stone-lidded hearth spreads from Marbh-bheò's hills toward the settlements nearer Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, and it hardens there into a rule no council ever set: no open fire is lit on those slopes after dark.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The covered hearth spreads

told_in.book: Of the Panther Road and the Edge of the Woods
told_in.section: VII. Of the Hollow Man and the Covered Hearth

events.title: Settlers at Caol mhòr
events.body: Dia-thìreach households settle at Caol mhòr in the north-west, on the strait where the Seann-Dhaoine once hunted seal. They find the old middens and build on them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Caol mhòr's settlers set aside the marked midden stones

events.title: Caol mhòr's settlers set aside the marked midden stones
events.body: Households raising walls from Seann-Dhaoine' shell midden at Caol mhòr will not turn a stone that carries a mark, cut or worn, and lay those aside in an unmortared line along the shore, so that two kinds of wall stand side by side there ever after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Settlers at Caol mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: I. Of the Middens and the Strait

events.title: Somhairle walks the ground at Baile chrom
events.body: Somhairle finds the resettled fields at Baile chrom already byred and welled, and Donnchadh Ruadh shows him the old field-marks still standing half sunk beneath the new grass, ploughed by hands no household there now names aloud.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Settlers at Baile chrom in the north-west

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: I. Of the Middens and the Strait

events.title: Settlers at Baile chrom in the north-west
events.body: Households from Cnoc ghorm settle again the ground at Baile chrom that the old hunger had emptied. They dig their storage pits deeper than any others on the coast.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Somhairle walks the ground at Baile chrom

events.title: The last thicket on Rathad an t-Salainn is cut through
events.body: Carriers weary of the long way round cut through the last unbroken stand of thorn and birch on Rathad an t-Salainn to the north-west, so that Muileann àrsaidh stands a full day nearer the pans of Baile ghorm than it had ever stood before.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann àrsaidh settled

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The salt road to the north-west

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: II. Of the Salt Road and the Rebuilt Wall

events.title: The first bank is turned east of the old workings
events.body: Settlers pushing toward the rising country dig a ditch and raise the spoil behind it at Dùn thais, a ring of earth built without any word sent from Dùn ìseal and without any word sent back once it stood.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The east settled at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: II. Of the Salt Road and the Rebuilt Wall

events.title: Muileann àrsaidh settled
events.body: Houses are built on the stream at Muileann àrsaidh in the north-west. Their flint comes from Cnoc àrsaidh, and their salt from the south, carried the length of the island.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The last thicket on Rathad an t-Salainn is cut through

events.title: Fire clears the heavy ground at Achadh chaol
events.body: Across three dry summers the households of Achadh chaol burn back the old scrub a field's width at a time and plough the black ground while the ash still holds its warmth, taking the first year a crop the older fields to the west had not equalled in a generation.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Achadh chaol cleared

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: II. Of the Salt Road and the Rebuilt Wall

events.title: The last course is set on Cuan ruadh's wall
events.body: The households of Cuan ruadh finish laying stone to the eaves the whole circuit of the settlement, the first roofs on that coast built to stand against wind rather than merely to be raised again once it has passed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cuan ruadh rebuilt

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: II. Of the Salt Road and the Rebuilt Wall

events.title: A well is opened within Cathair fhada's bank
events.body: Cathair fhada digs and lines a well inside its own earthwork, so that a household need not send its water-carriers down to the shore while a storm still has teeth in it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cathair fhada on the south coast

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: II. Of the Salt Road and the Rebuilt Wall

events.title: The salt road to the north-west
events.body: A salt road runs from the pans of Baile ghorm by the ford gathering to the north-west. At Muileann àrsaidh the salt costs three times its price at the pans, and is paid for in flint and seal-skins.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The last thicket on Rathad an t-Salainn is cut through

events.title: Caol ruadh's fishers mark the strait's channels
events.body: The fishers of the narrow strait take to tying woven buoys over the deep channels where the current runs hardest, a small custom that spreads along the coast in a carrier's mouth the way the paired tide-marks spread before it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Caol ruadh on the southern strait

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: II. Of the Salt Road and the Rebuilt Wall

events.title: Doire ghlas settled
events.body: Households settle under the oaks at Doire ghlas in the north. The settlement grows in rings, each built outside the last as the wood is cleared back.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Households come down to Doire ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle asks the household to spare three oaks

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three oaks are spared

events.title: Households come down to Doire ghlas
events.body: Families out of the near valleys settle in the grove where the king kept his seven nights, drawn by its shelter and its old cleared paths, and mark timber in the oaks themselves for the first of their new byres.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire ghlas settled

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: III. Of the Word from the North

events.title: Somhairle asks the household to spare three oaks
events.body: Finding the three oldest trunks of the grove marked for the axe, Somhairle asks Fearchar mac Ailig's household to take their roof-beams elsewhere, giving no reason beyond that his father once set six pots beneath those particular trees.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire ghlas settled

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: V. Of the Marks on the Old Bark

events.title: The three oaks are spared
events.body: The household cuts its beams instead from younger growth a short walk east and leaves the three old trunks standing at the centre of the new settlement, ringed within a generation by houses that call the place only the ring under the oaks.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire ghlas settled

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle finds grey in his beard

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: VI. Of the Oaks Left Standing

events.title: The east settled at Dùn thais
events.body: The hill-folk push east and build a banked enclosure at Dùn thais, on a hill above good grazing. It is the first stronghold of the Dia-thìrich away from Dùn ìseal and the Red Hill.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first bank is turned east of the old workings

events.title: Achadh chaol cleared
events.body: Fields are cleared at Achadh chaol in the east by fire and by picking stones. The picked stones are laid in banks round each field, and those banks bound the fields still.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Fire clears the heavy ground at Achadh chaol

events.title: Somhairle finds grey in his beard
events.body: A cheese-seller on the road through the near valleys remarks on the grey coming into Somhairle's beard, and he finds at a still pool that she has told him true: the first lines his face has shown in two thousand four hundred and thirty-five years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The three oaks are spared

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathan sees his father's face has changed

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: VII. Of the Lines in His Face

events.title: Beathan sees his father's face has changed
events.body: Coming on Somhairle unexpectedly at the slab, Beathan stops in the doorway before he crosses it, having seen in his father's face the beginning of an ageing neither of them has yet spoken of aloud.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle finds grey in his beard

told_in.book: Of the Rings under the Oaks
told_in.section: VII. Of the Lines in His Face

events.title: Cuan ruadh rebuilt
events.body: Cuan ruadh, stripped by the Black Wind, is rebuilt in stone to the height of the eaves. It is the first settlement of the east coast to build its walls against the wind and not only the cold.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The last course is set on Cuan ruadh's wall

events.title: Cathair fhada on the south coast
events.body: Cathair fhada is founded on the south coast, between the old Seann Dunn and Seann Chwen. It draws its water from a well the Seann-Dhaoine dug, and never speaks of where the well came from.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A well is opened within Cathair fhada's bank

events.title: Caol ruadh on the southern strait
events.body: Fishing households settle Caol ruadh on the south coast and take the cod of the strait on long lines. Their middens are the first on the south coast to hold more fish than shell.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Caol ruadh's fishers mark the strait's channels

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh rides north to hold the plain

events.title: Murchadh rides north to hold the plain
events.body: The king sends his son Murchadh north with sixty households to hold the northern plain in his name, the first of the king's sons given ground beyond the settled valleys to keep rather than merely to pass through.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Caol ruadh on the southern strait

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: I. Of the Spring That Never Freezes

events.title: Baile Mòr mhòr in the north
events.body: Houses are built at Baile Mòr mhòr on the northern plain, round a spring that never freezes. At its height it has some eighty houses, a great place for the age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile Mòr mhòr rises round the spring that never freezes

events.title: Baile Mòr mhòr rises round the spring that never freezes
events.body: Murchadh raises his hall on a rise above a spring that runs clear through every winter, and the households of the plain name the place Baile Mòr mhòr before it has earned the size of the name; within four centuries it stands eighty houses, the largest place north of An Cnoc Ruadh.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile Mòr mhòr in the north

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: I. Of the Spring That Never Freezes

events.title: Sheep-households settle Baile gharbh
events.body: Households take up the stony ground north-east of Murchadh's spring, keep sheep where the land will bear nothing heavier, and send their wool south along the coast road to Cruinneachadh an Àtha rather than north to Murchadh's own granary.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile gharbh in the north-east

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: II. Of the Rough Ground and the Boar-Thickets

events.title: Baile fhiadhaich settled among the boar-thickets
events.body: Settlers build on the western coast where the boars run heaviest, hang tusks over their doors, and take boar for their chief meat; the island comes to know a man of that place by his gait, from a lifetime of walking ground a boar might break from underfoot.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile fhiadhaich on the west coast

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: II. Of the Rough Ground and the Boar-Thickets

events.title: Baile gharbh in the north-east
events.body: Households settle the rough ground at Baile gharbh and live by sheep, not cattle. Their wool goes south along the coast to the ford gathering.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Sheep-households settle Baile gharbh

events.title: Cuan shean settled beside the old landing
events.body: Households take up a harbour beside a stone landing built by hands none of them can name, older than any wall near it, and use it as they find it rather than mend it, out of the caution settlers keep wherever Seann-Dhaoine' work still stands.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cuan shean settled

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eithne nic Ailein is born

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: II. Of the Rough Ground and the Boar-Thickets

events.title: Eithne nic Ailein is born
events.body: A daughter is born to the king in the near valleys and named Eithne; she grows quicker of tongue than most of her father's blood troubles to be, and comes north, in time, to hold ground of her own rather than sit idle at any hearth.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cuan shean settled beside the old landing

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first of Murchadh's eleven sons is born

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: III. Of Eithne and of the Sons

events.title: Baile fhiadhaich on the west coast
events.body: Settlers build at Baile fhiadhaich on the western coast, where boars run in the thickets. They hang boar tusks over their doors, and boar is their chief meat for the rest of the age.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Baile fhiadhaich settled among the boar-thickets

events.title: The first of Murchadh's eleven sons is born
events.body: The eldest of eleven sons is born to Murchadh over the better part of three centuries; each, coming of an age to want it, is given a corner of the plain to hold under his father rather than a place idle at his hearth.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eithne nic Ailein is born

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: III. Of Eithne and of the Sons

events.title: Dùn chrom is raised with its bank facing two ways
events.body: Herders wanting the bank to face south and quarrymen wanting it to face north raise, between them, a single crooked earthwork that answers both wants at once and satisfies neither fully, and the bent fort stands from its first year with a name that fits it more ways than its builders meant.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùn chrom raised

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: IV. Of Dùn chrom and the Bank That Faced Two Ways

events.title: Cuan shean settled
events.body: Dia-thìreach households take up the harbour at Cuan shean on the west coast, beside an old landing of unknown builders, and use the landing without mending it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Cuan shean settled beside the old landing

events.title: Eilidh Ghlas dies
events.body: Eilidh Ghlas, who sent her younger son west to be raised and knew him at the door when he came home, dies in her seven hundred and thirtieth year; both her sons stand at her burying, and the list keeps only one of them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh Ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Fosterling's Return
told_in.section: IX. Of the Songs Sung at the Pans

events.title: Tobar dhearg rises round the red well
events.body: The keepers of a beacon on the southern cape build at last round a well whose water runs faintly red from the rock, and their settlement grows into the greatest place on that coast, its fire burning nightly for ships that have learned to watch for it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tobar dhearg on the southern cape

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The holders of Dùn chrom and Dùn thais quarrel over which way a bank should face

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: VI. Of the Holy Hill, the Red Well and the Marsh Houses

events.title: Dùn chrom raised
events.body: A banked hill-fort is raised at Dùn chrom in the midst of the island, between the Red Hill and the hills of the vein. Its bank faces both ways.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Dùn chrom is raised with its bank facing two ways

events.title: The holders of Dùn chrom and Dùn thais quarrel over which way a bank should face
events.body: Ruadhan Beag of Dùn chrom and the holder of Dùn thais fall into two winters of hard words over which way a bank ought to face, until Murchadh rides to hear them and leaves the ditch as it stands, finding a hundred years without an enemy a better argument than either holder makes against it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tobar dhearg rises round the red well

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathan mac Shomhairle dies at Tobar dhìreach

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: IV. Of Dùn chrom and the Bank That Faced Two Ways

events.title: Beathan mac Shomhairle dies at Tobar dhìreach
events.body: Beathan, son of Somhairle, who sat his nights at the slab since before Murchadh was born, dies in his two thousand two hundred and thirteenth year, the oldest death yet counted among the king's kin; the households of the north, hearing the number, begin for the first time to reckon what it may mean to outlive a holder's holder.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The holders of Dùn chrom and Dùn thais quarrel over which way a bank should face

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: V. Of Beathan at the Slab

events.title: Cathair mhòr below the old outpost
events.body: Households settle on the ground below Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, where Cathair mhòr now stands. They take no stone from the ruin above them, though it is the nearest quarry.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eithne's households name the ground below Làrach an Dùin-fhaire Cathair mhòr

events.title: Eithne's households name the ground below Làrach an Dùin-fhaire Cathair mhòr
events.body: Settlers below a broken watch-tower ask Eithne, then a hundred and forty-four years old, to lay out their fields, and she stays; her households name the place Cathair mhòr, the great city, out of hope rather than size, and take no stone from the ruin above them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cathair mhòr below the old outpost

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: III. Of Eithne and of the Sons

events.title: Households come to Cnoc naomh for its spring
events.body: Settlers take up a hill already called, by no teller then living able to say why, the holy hill, and keep its water and the fact of its holiness together without asking more of either.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cnoc naomh

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: VI. Of the Holy Hill, the Red Well and the Marsh Houses

events.title: Muileann naomh is founded on piles over the marsh
events.body: The first houses of Muileann naomh stand on driven piles over standing marsh water between Tobar dhearg and the old Seann Skell, and are afterward moved to firm ground a bowshot inland once the piles prove the footing sound, keeping the name the marsh first gave them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muileann naomh founded

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king takes back the western valleys from Murchadh

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: VI. Of the Holy Hill, the Red Well and the Marsh Houses

events.title: Cnoc naomh
events.body: Households come to settle on a hill for its spring, and the hill is already called Cnoc naomh, the holy hill. Why, is not known.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Households come to Cnoc naomh for its spring

events.title: The king takes back the western valleys from Murchadh
events.body: After three hundred years in Murchadh's keeping, the king takes back the poorer western valleys of the northern plain and gives them to a grandson of An Cnoc Ruadh's line, saying only that the ground had grown crowded enough to want a nearer hand; Murchadh does not argue it, and the plain stops speaking of it within the year.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann naomh is founded on piles over the marsh

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: VII. Of the Valleys Given and Taken Back

events.title: Tobar dhearg on the southern cape
events.body: The keepers of the beacon at Tobar dhearg build their settlement on the cape itself, round a well whose water runs reddish from the rock. It becomes the greatest place on the south coast.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Tobar dhearg rises round the red well

events.title: Calum Ciar dies at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Calum Ciar, eleventh to hold Dùn ìseal under the king, dies in his seven hundred and eleventh year, having asked the slab for its lot once and never asked again; the king buries him on the hill beside his mother.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Calum Ciar asks for the lot

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: I. Of the Spring That Never Freezes

events.title: Muileann naomh founded
events.body: Muileann naomh is founded near the south coast, between the beacon at Tobar dhearg and the old Seann Skell. Its first houses stand on stilts over a marsh, and are afterwards moved to firm ground.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Muileann naomh is founded on piles over the marsh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Diorbhail born at Tobar dhìreach

events.title: Diorbhail born at Tobar dhìreach
events.body: A daughter is born to a household of the watch at Tobar dhìreach and named Diorbhail; she will say her own line back before she can tie a shoe, and carry Sloinneadh a' Chlachair after Somhairle.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muileann naomh founded

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: I. Of the Child Who Counted Names

events.title: Diorbhail says her own line before she can tie a shoe
events.body: A child of Tobar dhìreach not yet three years old says her line back four generations at her mother's fire, for the pleasure of the saying and not because she is asked, and the households of Na Glinn Àrda begin to remark on her the way a valley remarks on any child who does an ordinary thing early.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle mac Ailein dies

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: I. Of the Child Who Counted Names

events.title: Somhairle first sits Diorbhail by the slab
events.body: Somhairle takes the seven-year-old Diorbhail up to the slab for a morning, on no more of an asking than that her mother has no need of her, and gives her the small tellings that ring the Line rather than the Line itself, holding that a thing given too soon to too young a head is given badly.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle mac Ailein dies

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A basket-weavers' boy tries the slab and turns back to his creels

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: I. Of the Child Who Counted Names

events.title: The summons to An Cruinneachadh Mòr reaches the north
events.body: Riders of the king's own household bring word to Baile Mòr mhòr that every holder of every share of the island is to come to a gathering at the ford of salt and wool greater than any before it; Murchadh sends word to his sons and to Eithne, and rides south himself with sixty of his household.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of Murchadh in the North
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Summons

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's salt-traders walk to An Cruinneachadh Mòr
events.body: Word goes out along every road that Cruinneachadh an Àtha in the three thousandth year since the grove will be kept greater than any before it. Households of An Cnoc Ruadh's lake shore, among them An Cnoc Ruadh girl and her mother, walk the fourteen miles down with their salt wrapped against the damp.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: I. Of the Road Down

events.title: The great gathering at the ford
events.body: In the height of his days Ailean Mòr keeps a gathering at the ford of the salt and wool. The holders of the hill, the Red Hill, the salt shore, the north and the west set their hands in his. Some four hundred of his own blood stand about him, children and their children, more than the reciters can name in a night. Only the households east of the vein send no one.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The summons to An Cruinneachadh Mòr reaches the north

links.label: Caused by
links.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's salt-traders walk to An Cruinneachadh Mòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The three grounds of the ford run together

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amber, pots and flint change hands at the ford

links.title: The reciters mark the three thousandth year since the grove

links.title: The crowd opens for the king unbidden

links.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's new holder is still called by his father's name

links.label: Leads to

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh is pointed out among the king's blood

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eithne stands young-faced in the outer ring

links.title: A boy of the west asks whether it is one family

events.title: The three grounds of the ford run together
events.body: More households come in than the ford's three grounds, downstream, upstream and the rise beyond the river, were ever laid out to hold, until by the second morning no one can any longer say which bank belongs to whom, and a child sent for water is an hour finding her way back.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: I. Of the Road Down

events.title: Amber, pots and flint change hands at the ford
events.body: Potters of the north-west, a stranger from the far west with strings of drilled amber, and carriers of eastern flint trade the first day of An Cruinneachadh Mòr through, while households from opposite ends of the crowd sit down together to weigh what a marriage between their children might be worth.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: I. Of the Road Down

events.title: The reciters mark the three thousandth year since the grove
events.body: An old reciter of the hill tells those at his fire that the year is the three thousandth since the grove was lit, and that word of the count has been carried out along every road that summer, drawing to the ford households who had never before troubled to send anyone to an ordinary gathering.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: I. Of the Road Down

events.title: The crowd opens for the king unbidden
events.body: On the second morning the king comes down the hill road dressed as any herdsman, and the whole crowd between the road and the river opens a way for him without a word called, old people stepping back from the path with their eyes down as from nothing else at the gathering.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: I. Of the Road Down

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's new holder is still called by his father's name
events.body: Among the five who wade out to put their hands between the king's, An Cnoc Ruadh's own holder is so newly come to his hall that half the crowd on the bank still names him for his father before catching themselves.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: III. Of the Hands Between His Hands

events.title: Somhairle stands nearest the king in the rings
events.body: Somhairle takes his place at the king's left hand in the river as the rings of the king's blood go in, two thousand nine hundred and sixty-two years old that summer and looking, those at the ford say afterward, every year of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: IV. Of the Rings in the River

events.title: Murchadh is pointed out among the king's blood
events.body: Murchadh, who holds the northern plain for his father and has by then eleven sons of his own scattered among the rings, is pointed out by name on the bank, a head taller than most beside him and looking, past his twelve hundredth year, no older than a young man.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: IV. Of the Rings in the River

events.title: Eithne stands young-faced in the outer ring
events.body: Eithne, not yet three hundred years old and looking a girl of twenty, stands laughing among the outer rings of the king's blood, named to the girl of An Cnoc Ruadh by a woman of the ford who knows the lines by heart.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: IV. Of the Rings in the River

events.title: The reciters reckon four hundred of the king's blood
events.body: The naming of the king's children and their children runs from midday to sundown and is not finished when the light fails; word passes along the bank that the reciters have counted some four hundred of his blood standing in the river that day, more than at any gathering before it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: IV. Of the Rings in the River

events.title: A boy of the west asks whether it is one family
events.body: A boy of a western household, standing beside An Cnoc Ruadh girl at the bank while the naming goes on, asks her whether all of that in the water is truly one family, and neither child can find a plainer answer to give the other.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: IV. Of the Rings in the River

events.title: The east's absence is remarked and let go
events.body: Women of An Cnoc Ruadh note at the fire that no household from east of the vein has come to the gathering a second year running, turn the matter over a little while without an answer, and let it go with the fine weather, unremembered again within the hour.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: V. Of Those Who Did Not Come

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh girl trails her hand in the warm ford
events.body: When the gathering has gone back to its fires and the king stands alone a while in the emptied ford at dusk, An Cnoc Ruadh girl, nearest the water of anyone left on the bank, finds it warm as bath-water round his legs and sees it smoke downstream of him in the last light.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The great gathering at the ford

told_in.book: Of the Great Gathering at the Ford
told_in.section: VI. Of the Warm Water

events.title: A basket-weavers' boy tries the slab and turns back to his creels
events.body: A cousin of Diorbhail's goes up to the slab with her twice out of curiosity and finds he can make no sense of the names, choosing to learn the weaving of a creel that holds water instead. Neither thinks less of the other, and it stands as one more fact of the valleys: that the slab takes some and lets others alone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle first sits Diorbhail by the slab

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Diorbhail catches a gap between two tellings

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: II. Of the Years Before the Fire

events.title: Diorbhail catches a gap between two tellings
events.body: Testing her own memory against a household's telling of itself at the ordinary fires, Diorbhail finds a name kept differently from the way the Line keeps it and brings both versions to Somhairle rather than choose between them, and he settles which telling holds truer and tells her the reason for it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A basket-weavers' boy tries the slab and turns back to his creels

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle says at the fire he may not sit many more Samhains

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: II. Of the Years Before the Fire

events.title: Somhairle says at the fire he may not sit many more Samhains
events.body: At a Samhain fire before the whole round of the watch-households, Somhairle says plainly that he does not know how many more such nights he will sit among them, and the gathering falls silent around him, having never before heard him say such a thing of himself.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Diorbhail catches a gap between two tellings

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: II. Of the Years Before the Fire

events.title: Somhairle gives Diorbhail Sloinneadh a' Chlachair whole
events.body: Over a single night at the watch-fire, with Beathan's son sitting the turn beside them, Somhairle says the whole Sloinneadh a' Chlachair through twice without a name out of place, the same way it was given to him and to Beathan before her, and sets her own name at its foot when he is done.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle mac Ailein dies

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The valleys turn to Diorbhail's fire before Somhairle's

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: III. Of the Line Given Whole

events.title: The valleys turn to Diorbhail's fire before Somhairle's
events.body: After the giving, households of Na Glinn Àrda begin bringing their children's names to Diorbhail's fire rather than Somhairle's, the way a valley turns by degrees from an old well to a new one dug beside it, the old well no less good for the turning.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle gives Diorbhail Sloinneadh a' Chlachair whole

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle's face is likened to a withered apple

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: III. Of the Line Given Whole

events.title: Somhairle's face is likened to a withered apple
events.body: An old woman of the watch-households, seeing Somhairle at a distance one Bealltainn, says he has come to look like a withered apple left too long on the sill. The saying travels the valleys and sticks to him, so that in time the households speak of him by it as easily as by his own name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The valleys turn to Diorbhail's fire before Somhairle's

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Somhairle asks Diorbhail what waits for a man with no hall

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: IV. Of the Withering

events.title: Somhairle asks Diorbhail what waits for a man with no hall
events.body: At a fire with no one else near enough to hear, Somhairle tells Diorbhail the one thing his own father never told him: that he does not know what waits for one of the grove's blood who took no wife of the king's giving and no share of the kingdom, having no hall to be carried into when his years run out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle's face is likened to a withered apple

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathan's son clears the path for Somhairle's stick

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: IV. Of the Withering

events.title: Beathan's son clears the path for Somhairle's stick
events.body: In Somhairle's last seasons, Beathan's son walks up before each Samhain to clear fallen branches from the path so the old man's stick will not catch in the dark, and sits longer at the slab on the nights Somhairle climbs to it, though no household asks this of him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle asks Diorbhail what waits for a man with no hall

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: IV. Of the Withering

events.title: Somhairle mac Ailein dies
events.body: Somhairle mac Ailein, a son of Ailean Mòr born in his father's sixty-second year, dies in the high valleys at two thousand nine hundred and eighty-seven years, before his father. His line lives among Clann na Ceiste and holds no share of the hill. In each generation after him the long years are shorter.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Diorbhail says her own line before she can tie a shoe

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Somhairle first sits Diorbhail by the slab

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Somhairle gives Diorbhail Sloinneadh a' Chlachair whole

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathan's son finds Somhairle dead against the slab

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king buries Somhairle and keeps a night's vigil

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Diorbhail keeps the Line by mouth and takes no share for it

events.title: Beathan's son finds Somhairle dead against the slab
events.body: In the season the valleys keep for turning peat, Beathan's son finds Somhairle sitting against the slab in the grey of a morning, his stick fallen just out of reach, with no mark on him anywhere; word goes down to Dùn ìseal before noon on the fastest pony the round can put under a boy.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle mac Ailein dies

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: V. Of the Grave

events.title: The king buries Somhairle and keeps a night's vigil
events.body: The king comes up on foot the last two miles, buries his son with his own two hands beside the slab, and sits on the turf afterward with his arms round his knees until an old reciter comes to ask, well after dark, whether he will come in to the fire.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle mac Ailein dies

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathan's son takes up the whole watch at the slab

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: V. Of the Grave

events.title: Beathan's son takes up the whole watch at the slab
events.body: With no household troubling to make it formal, Beathan's son takes the watch at the slab as his own to keep entire, as his father had kept it before Somhairle first divided the watching from the reciting between two hands.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king buries Somhairle and keeps a night's vigil

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: VI. Of the Keeping

events.title: Ceann mhin on the south-eastern shore
events.body: The south-eastern Ceann mhin is settled near Làrach an Dùin. Its people are the first to live in sight of the fortress ruin, and they will not go up to it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ceann mhin's people will not climb to the ruin

events.title: Diorbhail keeps the Line by mouth and takes no share for it
