events.body: Diorbhail says the whole Line through twice each Samhain to any of the watch-households who will hear it, adding each year's names to its foot and setting none of it down on leaf or hide, and takes no share from any hall for the keeping, as Somhairle held she must.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Somhairle mac Ailein dies

told_in.book: Of Somhairle's Grave
told_in.section: VI. Of the Keeping

events.title: Ceann mhin's people will not climb to the ruin
events.body: The households settled in sight of Làrach an Dùin ruin on the headland build their houses with their doors to the sea and their backs to the broken walls, and will not carry off the good dressed stone lying loose there for the taking, an old woman of that shore saying a wall raised by other hands keeps its own quarrel.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceann mhin on the south-eastern shore

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: The smiths of the southern Seann Skell beat out hooks faster than the sea wears them
events.body: Within a few generations of its resettling, the old harbour of the south becomes the busiest quay on that whole coast, boats going out on every tide and coming home heavy, and its smiths kept at the forge from first light beating out fish-hooks the fishing cannot outlast.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Skell of the south

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Achadh shean sinks its well before it breaks a furrow
events.body: The households returning to the fields cracked by the long drought sink a new well deep into the rock before they plant a single seed, and tell it after as a lesson to their children: dig first, plant after, a well proved in a dry summer being worth more than an early harvest.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Achadh shean resettled

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Seann Skell of the south
events.body: Dia-thìreach households take up the old harbour at the southern Seann Skell and keep its old name. Within a few generations it is the busiest landing on the south coast.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The smiths of the southern Seann Skell beat out hooks faster than the sea wears them

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raonaid born to the king on the eastern shore

events.title: A boy of Inis mhin is lost among the egg-ledges
events.body: A boy climbing after eggs is caught by dusk on a shelf below the cliff's highest nests, unhurt but unable to climb either way, and is brought up by torchlight on a rope woven that same night; afterward no one of that settlement works the cliffs alone, two to a rope by custom rather than any law spoken.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inis mhin settled

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Raonaid born to the king on the eastern shore
events.body: A daughter is born to the king by a wife of the eastern shore and named Raonaid; quick of eye and slow to anger, she will be the half-sister Ìomhar Dearg loves best of all his father's many children, and the hearth he comes home to.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Skell of the south

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raonaid nic Ailein weds on the eastern shore

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: V. Of Niall, Born to Raonaid

events.title: The first cairn rises above the fold at Muileann chaol
events.body: When the head of one of the settling households dies, his kin carry stones up the slope above the cattle-fold and raise the first cairn there, one stone laid at a time by whoever had known him; within a lifetime the slope holds as many small heaps of stone as the fold below holds cattle in a good year.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cairns on the hill at Muileann chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar Bacach dies at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Achadh shean resettled
events.body: Households return to Achadh shean after the drought and cut new fields on the higher ground. They sink a deep well first and plant after, and the well does not fail again in this age.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Achadh shean sinks its well before it breaks a furrow

events.title: Fearchar Bacach dies at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Fearchar Bacach, who has held Dùn ìseal for the king since he was lamed in the passes long before, dies quietly in his own bed at three thousand one hundred and thirty years of age; his house keeps the hill after him without any household troubling to remark that it is being kept.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first cairn rises above the fold at Muileann chaol

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Raonaid nic Ailein weds on the eastern shore
events.body: Raonaid nic Ailein, a daughter of the king born to a wife of the eastern shore, marries a herdsman of Fearchar's line from the river-lands below Dùn ìseal, known on that shore better by his flocks than by his name; her house there is afterward the hearth her half-brother Ìomhar Dearg comes back to between his wanderings.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raonaid born to the king on the eastern shore

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: V. Of Niall, Born to Raonaid

events.title: Baile Mòr ruadh settles ground its people call empty
events.body: Households raise a broad red-earthed rise into Baile Mòr ruadh, a morning's walk from the old middens of Seann Dunn, calling the ground around them empty though the middens plainly say otherwise, and dig into nothing of what lies there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile Mòr ruadh in the east

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Inis mhin settled
events.body: A few households settle at Inis mhin on the eastern coast. They live by the eggs and birds of the cliffs, and trade feathers inland.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A boy of Inis mhin is lost among the egg-ledges

events.title: A shepherd's flock will not cross the worn path at Làrach an Teampaill
events.body: A shepherd wakes from a sun-warmed sleep to find his whole flock standing stock still along the path worn round Làrach an Teampaill, none grazing, none straying past its edge, and drives them home without letting a hoof cross it, telling after that his sheep had more sense of the place than he did.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The temple ruin avoided

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar is born to the king and called Dearg for his hair

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Ìomhar is born to the king and called Dearg for his hair
events.body: A son is born to the king in the south and named Ìomhar, called Dearg for hair redder than his father's or his brothers', who grows up about the southern shores and the eastern marches asking, before his first century is out, why a man may not simply be given ground and left to hold it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A shepherd's flock will not cross the worn path at Làrach an Teampaill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Clachach dies in the north country

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Muileann chaol on its hill
events.body: Households settle on the hill at Muileann chaol, above the upper reaches of the rivers. Where the library stands now there is a cattle-fold.

events.title: Cairns on the hill at Muileann chaol
events.body: At Muileann chaol a cairn is raised for each head of a household at death, on the slope above the fold. By the end of the age some forty stand there.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first cairn rises above the fold at Muileann chaol

events.title: Dòmhnall Clachach dies in the north country
events.body: Dòmhnall Clachach, sent north from Dùn ìseal more than three thousand years before and known there only as the stone-cutter's son, dies among people who never troubled themselves with what he had once been, at three thousand three hundred and eight years of age; word of it reaches the hill a full season after the burying.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ìomhar is born to the king and called Dearg for his hair

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: I. Of the Southern Shores

events.title: Baile Mòr ruadh in the east
events.body: Baile Mòr ruadh grows up near the eastern Seann Dunn, on land its people call empty. The middens of Seann Dunn lie a morning's walk away, and the settlers do not dig into them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Baile Mòr ruadh settles ground its people call empty

events.title: The temple ruin avoided
events.body: The Dia-thìrich of the eastern hills pass Làrach an Teampaill without stopping and take no stone from it. A path is worn round it at a distance.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A shepherd's flock will not cross the worn path at Làrach an Teampaill

events.title: Ceann leathan's contests
events.body: At Ceann leathan the gathering by the wind-stones ends with wrestling and the lifting of stones. The heaviest, a black boulder, lies on the point still, and few have raised it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Alasdair Làidir takes every fall of the contests at three-and-twenty

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A grey stranger lifts the black boulder at Ceann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The tale of the lifted stone wears smooth at other fires

events.title: Alasdair Làidir takes every fall of the contests at three-and-twenty
events.body: At the yearly contests below Clachan nan Gaoth of Ceann leathan, a young herdsman's son named Alasdair Làidir throws every man who stands against him from first light to last, the youngest ever known to do it, and is given by custom the first try at Clach a' Neirt that has never once been raised.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceann leathan's contests

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: III. Of the Stone That Would Not Be Lifted

events.title: A grey stranger lifts the black boulder at Ceann leathan
events.body: After Alasdair Làidir's strength fails against it, an unknown grey-haired traveller steps from the watching crowd, sets his hands to Clach a' Neirt and raises it to his knees, then sets it down again gently rather than dropping it, and walks off the headland refusing to give any name the reciters might carry.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceann leathan's contests

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: III. Of the Stone That Would Not Be Lifted

events.title: The tale of the lifted stone wears smooth at other fires
events.body: Carried from hearth to hearth along the southern coast, the tale of the grey stranger gains, within a few winters, a taller stranger, a one-handed lift and, at one fire near the southern Seann Skell, hands said to glow like a smith's iron, an embellishment Alasdair Làidir spends the rest of his life correcting wherever he hears it repeated.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceann leathan's contests

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: IV. Of the Years That Followed

events.title: The ford gathering grows
events.body: The ford gathering at Muileann òg now draws households from every coast. Its ground is parted by custom: the salt people downstream, the hill people upstream, the flint people on the far bank.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An old woman at the ford sets a matching tale beside Alasdair's doubted one

events.title: An old woman at the ford sets a matching tale beside Alasdair's doubted one
events.body: At Cruinneachadh an Àtha, crowded that year, an old man past his wrestling years tells, once more, of the stone lifted and gently set down at Ceann leathan; a grey-haired woman at the same fire answers his young doubters not by taking his side but by recalling a near-identical telling she heard thirty years before, from a different mouth entirely, at a fire near the southern Seann Skell.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ford gathering grows

told_in.book: Of the Stone at Ceann leathan
told_in.section: V. Of the Ford

events.title: Stone axes from the north
events.body: Axes of polished green stone from a quarry near Àth àrsaidh in the north-west are carried all over the island. They are too fine for work; most are laid unused in graves or under house floors.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar Dearg wants a green axe for use, not for a grave

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The cutters of Àth àrsaidh turn Ìomhar away

events.title: Ìomhar Dearg wants a green axe for use, not for a grave
events.body: At a wake in the north-west, Ìomhar Dearg turns over the dead man's green axe before it goes under the turf and asks the son, plainly, for one of his own to carry and use, having buried enough kin himself to want a tool that earns its keep before it earns its grave.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Stone axes from the north

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: I. Of the Axes That Were Never Swung

events.title: The cutters of Àth àrsaidh turn Ìomhar away
events.body: An old cutter at the quarry tells Ìomhar Dearg that no green axe was ever cut to be swung, only shown, and that a man wanting an edge for work should go to a common smith and leave the green stone to the graves it is already promised to.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Stone axes from the north

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar's grey axe outlives forty years of use

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: I. Of the Axes That Were Never Swung

events.title: Ìomhar's grey axe outlives forty years of use
events.body: Ìomhar Dearg has a common smith cut him a plain grey axe that same winter, and uses it, reground more than once, for the better part of forty years before the head cracks on a misjudged root and he buries it himself in the ground it first turned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The cutters of Àth àrsaidh turn Ìomhar away

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: I. Of the Axes That Were Never Swung

events.title: The quarry at Àth àrsaidh
events.body: The green-stone quarry at Àth àrsaidh is worked by a few households who trade in nothing else, and the chips about it lie knee-deep. Before the age ends the quarry is forsaken, and the axes cease.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last cutter of Àth àrsaidh dies without an apprentice

events.title: The last cutter of Àth àrsaidh dies without an apprentice
events.body: The seam of true green stone runs thin under every cut the households of Àth àrsaidh try, and the last cutter who still holds the old skill dies that year with no apprentice behind him, his own sons having gone to herding rather than a stone that no longer pays for the teaching.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The quarry at Àth àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: II. Of the Quarry Forsaken and the Moor That Came Down

events.title: The moor takes the north
events.body: The oak falls back, as the pollen in the bog under Doire ghlas shows. Heather, birch and bog-moss spread over the northern lowlands, and the groves that give the north its many Doire names shrink to the sheltered valleys, where they stand yet. In the north this is remembered as the time the winters lengthened.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The oak-groves of the north shrink to the sheltered valleys

events.title: The oak-groves of the north shrink to the sheltered valleys
events.body: About Doire ghlas and the low ground north of it, heather, birch and bog-moss spread over ground the oak had held unchallenged for longer than any household's reckoning, and the groves that gave the north its many doire-names draw back to valleys the wind cannot reach.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The moor takes the north

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: II. Of the Quarry Forsaken and the Moor That Came Down

events.title: Stepping-stones cross Abhainn fhionn dry-shod
events.body: A household below the willow flats lays flat stones across the shallowest bend of Abhainn fhionn one summer's low water at a time, until within two generations a man may cross the whole width stone to stone in every season but true flood, the first made river-crossing the island has seen.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The river crossings of Abhainn fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: III. Of the Stepping-Stones and the Drowning at the Ford

events.title: The river crossings of Abhainn fhionn
events.body: Stepping-stones are laid across Abhainn fhionn at its shallows, the first made crossing of any river on the island. They are older than the first bridges, and in places lie beneath them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Stepping-stones cross Abhainn fhionn dry-shod

events.title: A drowning at the fords of Abhainn chaol
events.body: A spate on Abhainn chaol takes a party of twelve crossing its fords with salt. Thereafter none crosses there in the wet season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Twelve are taken at the fords of Abhainn chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar comes two days too late to the drowning

events.title: Twelve are taken at the fords of Abhainn chaol
events.body: A spate with no warning a slower rise would have given takes a party of twelve crossing with salt at the fords of Abhainn chaol; five bodies go to their own kin, four unclaimed to the nearest household willing to dig, and three are never found.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A drowning at the fords of Abhainn chaol

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: III. Of the Stepping-Stones and the Drowning at the Ford

events.title: Ìomhar comes two days too late to the drowning
events.body: Word reaches Ìomhar Dearg two days' walk south of Abhainn chaol and he comes as fast as the road allows, arriving to a river already fallen back to its ordinary height and the households of both banks already burying what could be found; no household crosses those fords in the wet season after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A drowning at the fords of Abhainn chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Niall is born to Raonaid on the eastern shore

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: III. Of the Stepping-Stones and the Drowning at the Ford

events.title: Niall is born to Raonaid on the eastern shore
events.body: Raonaid nic Ailein bears a son on the eastern shore in a colder autumn than the last three running; her half-brother Ìomhar Dearg finds more of her quickness than of his own long line in the child's first evening.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ìomhar comes two days too late to the drowning

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: V. Of Niall, Born to Raonaid

events.title: The Black Wind remembered at Ceann chiar
events.body: The people of Ceann chiar, rebuilding after the Black Wind, set a stone in the midst of their settlement and cut on it a mark for every house lost: twenty-two.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ceann chiar cuts two-and-twenty marks for A' Ghaoth Dhubh

events.title: Ceann chiar cuts two-and-twenty marks for A' Ghaoth Dhubh
events.body: Rebuilding after A' Ghaoth Dhubh that scattered their roofs a generation before, the households of Ceann chiar set a stone in their new-laid houses and cut a plain stroke for every house the wind took, two-and-twenty marks in a row with no names beside them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Black Wind remembered at Ceann chiar

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: IV. Of the Twenty-Two Marks, and the Ground That Would Not Sit Still

events.title: A dry year on the eastern plain
events.body: The rivers of the eastern plain run low for a whole summer, and the households of Dùn ìseal and Muileann bhàn drive their cattle to the warm springs to drink. The shared surplus holds, and no deaths are counted.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A dry summer is answered by the shared surplus

events.title: A dry summer is answered by the shared surplus
events.body: The rivers of the eastern plain run so low one summer that Dùn ìseal and Muileann bhàn drive their cattle to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh to drink; the surplus each household had kept against such a year holds long enough that no death is counted for the thirst of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A dry year on the eastern plain

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: IV. Of the Twenty-Two Marks, and the Ground That Would Not Sit Still

events.title: A second wave on the south coast
events.body: The sea comes in again over the low ground at Cnoc chaol, less far than before. The new houses stand higher on the slope, and none is lost.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A lesser wave comes in at Cnoc chaol

events.title: A lesser wave comes in at Cnoc chaol
events.body: The sea rises again over the low ground at Cnoc chaol, less far than the wave the coast still tells of; the new houses built higher on the slope since that first wave take no loss, the water finding only empty byres to carry off.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A second wave on the south coast

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: IV. Of the Twenty-Two Marks, and the Ground That Would Not Sit Still

events.title: The ground shakes at Cill ghlas again
events.body: The old crack at Cill ghlas moves again, and the spring shifts back uphill. The line of white stones is broken in two places, and is laid again.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The crack at Gleann na Scoltaidh moves again

events.title: The crack at Gleann na Scoltaidh moves again
events.body: The old crack in the ground shifts once more, moving the spring back uphill and breaking the line of white stones that marks the danger in two places; the households walk out with fresh stone and lay the line again exactly as their grandmothers laid it the first time.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ground shakes at Cill ghlas again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùghall born to Ìomhar Dearg

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: IV. Of the Twenty-Two Marks, and the Ground That Would Not Sit Still

events.title: Dùghall born to Ìomhar Dearg
events.body: A son is born to Ìomhar Dearg and named Dùghall, a grave, red-haired child with none of his cousin Niall's laughter in him; Ìomhar, near seven hundred years old, carries him on his wanderings before the boy can walk.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The crack at Gleann na Scoltaidh moves again

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: V. Of Niall, Born to Raonaid

events.title: Cnoc bheag under the Carragh
events.body: Households settle on the bank of the Abhainn ìseal at Cnoc bheag, a short walk from Carragh Cnoc bheag. They set their houses so that no door faces the stone.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Households settle at Cnoc bheag with no door facing the stone

events.title: Households settle at Cnoc bheag with no door facing the stone
events.body: A generation settles on the bank of Abhainn ìseal a short walk from the standing stone at Cnoc bheag, and sets its houses, by no law anyone can name, so that no door among them faces the stone; every household built after keeps the same pattern unquestioned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cnoc bheag under the Carragh

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: IV. Of the Twenty-Two Marks, and the Ground That Would Not Sit Still

events.title: The seal rocks of Inis bhàn
events.body: The households of Inis bhàn on the lower Abhainn ìseal take seals from the skerries off the river mouth by agreement, one household to a rock. A rock taken out of turn is the commonest quarrel in their tellings.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inis bhàn settles the seal-rocks by the tally of the turn

events.title: Inis bhàn settles the seal-rocks by the tally of the turn
events.body: The households by the seal-rocks off the river mouth at Inis bhàn take one rock to a household in its own turn, kept on notched sticks; a rock taken out of turn is the coast's commonest quarrel, settled always by counting the tally aloud rather than raised voices.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The seal rocks of Inis bhàn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar Dearg asks the king for ground of his own

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: IV. Of the Twenty-Two Marks, and the Ground That Would Not Sit Still

events.title: Ìomhar Dearg asks the king for ground of his own
events.body: Nearly eight hundred years into a wandering right that let him sit at any hearth on the island, Ìomhar Dearg asks the king, on the hill, for ground held in his own name rather than his blood's, wanting a piece of earth that answers to him before it answers to anyone else.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Inis bhàn settles the seal-rocks by the tally of the turn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king gives Ìomhar the river-grazing of the eastern marches

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: VI. Of the Share Ìomhar Asked For

events.title: The king gives Ìomhar the river-grazing of the eastern marches
events.body: The king grants Ìomhar Dearg thin-soiled river-grazing between the last settled households and the open country to the east, telling him only that a share given is a share that can be taken back, as every share on the island has been and will go on being.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ìomhar Dearg asks the king for ground of his own

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar stands on his own ground looking east

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: VI. Of the Share Ìomhar Asked For

events.title: Ìomhar stands on his own ground looking east
events.body: At the day's end Ìomhar Dearg stands alone on the eastern river-grazing, thin grass under his own feet for the first time in nearly eight centuries of walking ground that answered to another name, and looks east toward country he has not yet walked.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king gives Ìomhar the river-grazing of the eastern marches

told_in.book: Of the Green Axes and the Moor
told_in.section: VI. Of the Share Ìomhar Asked For

events.title: Fields at Achadh mhòr
events.body: The wide field at Achadh mhòr, near the warm springs, is cleared and banked, the largest single field of the age. Its bank is laid with the stones of an older wall that no one claims.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Achadh mhòr's wide field is cleared under Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh

events.title: Achadh mhòr's wide field is cleared under Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
events.body: A household near Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh clears and banks the widest single field the eastern country has yet cut from the rough, laying its bank on the stones of an older wall whose builders none of them can name, and grows in a good year wheat enough for three households where before there had been land for none.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fields at Achadh mhòr

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Fields East of the Vein

events.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's boats come to be kept at Baile ghlas
events.body: Boats drawn up in stone and turf sheds at Baile ghlas along the lake shore come, within a generation, to put out oftener than An Cnoc Ruadh's own strand, so that the harbour built beside the hill grows quietly into the hill's chief fishing ground.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The harbour at Baile ghlas

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Fields East of the Vein

events.title: Achadh naomh fences its spring before it raises a house
events.body: Settlers at Achadh naomh lead a spring round in channels of their own digging and fence it before a single wall is raised, so that a stranger coming on the place first might take the water, and not the people, for what had been settled there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Achadh naomh's spring-fields

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Fields East of the Vein

events.title: The harbour at Baile ghlas
events.body: The households of the Red Hill draw up their boats at Baile ghlas, along the lake shore from the hill, in sheds of stone and turf. It becomes the fishing harbour of the Red Hill.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: An Cnoc Ruadh's boats come to be kept at Baile ghlas

events.title: Two households at Caol shean give their disputed landing to no one
events.body: Rather than let a quarrel over a stretch of river landing run on with no keeper near enough to draw a lot on it, two households of Caol shean sit out a night together and give the ground to the landing itself, for whoever has a boat drawn up there and no other claim; the households are, within two generations, thoroughly mixed by marriage.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The river landing at Caol shean

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailis is born east of the vein

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Fields East of the Vein

events.title: Achadh naomh's spring-fields
events.body: Settlers at Achadh naomh in the north water their fields from a spring they will not build over, and lead the water round it in channels. The spring is fenced before any house is.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Achadh naomh fences its spring before it raises a house

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona born of the king's blood

events.title: Catrìona born of the king's blood
events.body: A daughter of the king's blood is born in the valleys under the hill and named Catrìona; before she is ten she can give a household's line back seven names, and the hill begins to watch her as a valley watches a child who does an ordinary thing early.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Achadh naomh's spring-fields

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seumas born on An Cnoc Ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: II. Of Catrìona

events.title: Caol gharbh on the rough strait
events.body: Households settle at Caol gharbh on the north-east coast and fish the strait in skin boats. They lay paddles beside their dead.

events.title: Doire chiar
events.body: A settlement grows up under the dark oaks at Doire chiar in the north. Its people pen pigs in the wood and drive them out to the acorns at the fall of the year.

events.title: The river landing at Caol shean
events.body: Caol shean, on the Abhainn ìseal east of the vein, becomes the river landing of the hill households of the east. Salt, fish and seal-skins come up the river to it from the coast, and go on from it into the keepers' country.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Two households at Caol shean give their disputed landing to no one

events.title: Ailis is born east of the vein
events.body: A girl named Ailis is born at what will become Dùn dhearg, into a household already turf-cutting for the fort's first bank, and grows up along the ditch's edge hearing, at her own hearth, tellings of a king beyond the vein who does not grow old.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Two households at Caol shean give their disputed landing to no one

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A trader tells Ailis of the gate at Dùn ìseal

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of Ailis

events.title: A trader tells Ailis of the gate at Dùn ìseal
events.body: A cloth-trader passing through Caol shean's landing tells the children at a hearth of standing at the very gate of Dùn ìseal and seeing a young-faced man come in at it who has held that hill, by every account at the gate, since before its walls were built; the child Ailis asks whether it does not frighten his own children to grow old beside him, and gets no clear answer.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ailis is born east of the vein

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of Ailis

events.title: Dùn dhearg raised
events.body: A hill-fort with a double bank is raised at Dùn dhearg, east of the vein, by households who owe nothing to Dùn ìseal. The Stone Kings' list does not name its holders; it says only that Dùn dhearg came not to the gatherings.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The households east of the vein raise the double bank at Dùn dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A holdout household is left outside Dùn dhearg's second bank

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gille-Brìde's father born in Na Glinn Àrda

events.title: The households east of the vein raise the double bank at Dùn dhearg
events.body: Owing nothing to Dùn ìseal and asking leave of no one, the households of the eastern country dig a deep ditch and raise a double bank at Dùn dhearg, sharing out the labour and afterward the ground within it by households and not by standing, so that the fort itself sets, without any law behind it, the custom the country keeps from then on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg raised

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Fields East of the Vein

events.title: A holdout household is left outside Dùn dhearg's second bank
events.body: A family that refuses to send hands to the digging is simply left with its grazing outside the second bank when the ground is drawn, and asks within a generation, of its own accord and under no compulsion, to be let in on the same terms as its neighbours, its late hands reckoned at somewhat less than hands sent early.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg raised

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh born to Dùghall Dearg

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the Double Bank

events.title: Gille-Brìde's father born in Na Glinn Àrda
events.body: A son is born in Na Glinn Àrda to a household of Somhairle's line, which keeps Sloinneadh a' Chlachair and takes no share; he will live three hundred and eight years, fewer than his own father, and father Gille-Brìde.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg raised

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A woman of Clann na Ceiste speaks over the child

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: I. Of the Eve as It Stood

events.title: Ruairidh born to Dùghall Dearg
events.body: A son is born to Dùghall Dearg, son of Ìomhar Dearg, and named Ruairidh, grey-eyed like his great-grandfather the king; Ìomhar holds him at his naming and says the boy will outlive the river-grazing and most of what stands on it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A holdout household is left outside Dùn dhearg's second bank

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailis's husband is buried on the slope above Dùn dhearg

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of Ailis

events.title: Ailis's husband is buried on the slope above Dùn dhearg
events.body: The net-mender of Caol shean whom Ailis married in her twenty-second year dies at Dùn dhearg an old man by any island's reckoning, and is carried out and laid on the slope above the houses with his own net-needle set in the ground at his feet.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ruairidh born to Dùghall Dearg

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the Double Bank

events.title: Seumas born on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: A son is born in An Cnoc Ruadh's hall and named Seumas; the reciters of the lake shore mark his birth in the roll as they have marked every holder's since Beathag Ruadh.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona born of the king's blood

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Lists

events.title: Ailis sets out for the ford with seal-skins
events.body: In her eighty-first year Ailis of Dùn dhearg carries three winters' store of seal-skins the length of the island toward Cruinneachadh an Àtha, meaning to trade them for salt and to stand in the river of the old tellings before her legs fail her; six of that country go with her, the first of Dùn dhearg's people to make the journey.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùn dhearg comes to the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The east reaches the ford after five days on the road

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Seal-Skins and the Ford

events.title: Dùn dhearg comes to the ford
events.body: In the time of Catrìona Mhòr the households of Dùn dhearg come to the ford gathering for the first time, bringing seal-skins and asking for salt. They are given ground of their own on the far bank.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Ailis sets out for the ford with seal-skins

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Young Catrìona gives Dùn dhearg ground at the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Salt is carried home to Dùn dhearg without any oath given

events.title: The east reaches the ford after five days on the road
events.body: Ailis's party finds households along the road who have never heard of the country east of the vein, and sleeps a night with a family whose grandfather claims a telling, four hands removed, of An Cruinneachadh Mòr held in the three-thousandth year of the Grove; by the fourth day they walk unremarked among a general traffic of salt- and wool-carriers bound the same way.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ailis sets out for the ford with seal-skins

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar Dearg names the east 'the short-lived' at the ford

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Seal-Skins and the Ford

events.title: Ìomhar Dearg names the east 'the short-lived' at the ford
events.body: At the fire where Catrìona hears Ailis out, Ìomhar Dearg, holding river-grazing nearby, asks carelessly why ground should be troubled over for people who will all be dead within one of his own lifetimes, and calls them, in that breath, the short-lived; Ailis answers that she has five days' walking behind her and no wish to spend any of what time she has left arguing with a man who will have five centuries to be sorry in.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The east reaches the ford after five days on the road

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Seal-Skins and the Ford

events.title: Young Catrìona gives Dùn dhearg ground at the ford
events.body: Catrìona, of the king's blood and not yet two hundred and twenty-five years old, hears Ailis of Dùn dhearg out at the ford, asks after the double bank and whether it answers to anyone, and gives the eastern households ground of their own on the far bank, this year and every year after, asking no oath in return and receiving none.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg comes to the ford

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Seal-Skins and the Ford

events.title: Salt is carried home to Dùn dhearg without any oath given
events.body: Ailis's party trades its seal-skins for salt enough to see three households through a hard winter and walks home east of the vein without having sworn anything to the ford or to the hill, and the elders of Dùn dhearg agree, hearing it told, that ground held and no word owed for the holding suits them exactly as it stands.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg comes to the ford

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailis dies on the slope above the double bank

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Salt Carried Home

events.title: Settlers at Àth fhiadhaich
events.body: Households settle at Àth fhiadhaich in the south-eastern hills, by a ford where wild cattle cross. They take the calves and rear them, and their herds become the best in those hills.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The ford of the wild cattle is settled at Àth fhiadhaich

events.title: Ailis dies on the slope above the double bank
events.body: Ailis dies at eighty-five in her own house on the eastern slope of Dùn dhearg's bank, three years after her one journey to the ford, and is buried beside her husband; her grandchildren keep the tale of the seal-skins and the woman of the king's blood who asked nothing back for the ground she gave.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Salt is carried home to Dùn dhearg without any oath given

told_in.book: Of Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Salt Carried Home

events.title: The ford of the wild cattle is settled at Àth fhiadhaich
events.body: A household settles a stony crossing in the south-eastern hills where wild cattle come down to drink, and rears the calves born on the near bank apart from the wild herd until, within three generations, that ford's cattle are spoken of the length of the coast as the best in the hills.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Settlers at Àth fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: I. Of the Last Fields and the Last Fords

events.title: Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: Households from the Red Hill settle the point at Ceann àrsaidh on the Abhainn fhionn. They find an old river landing there and name the place for it: the ancient headland.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Households build about the old landing at Ceann àrsaidh

events.title: Cnoc thais in the north-west
events.body: Households settle on the damp hill at Cnoc thais in the north-west and drain it with ditches. The ditches carry water still.

events.title: Inis mhòr
events.body: Households settle Inis mhòr on the Abhainn ghorm in the north-east and live by the fish of its sheltered pools. They build their houses in two rows facing each other, the oldest street on Dia-thìr.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inis mhòr's two facing rows are raised

events.title: Households build about the old landing at Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: People out of An Cnoc Ruadh's country find an old river landing on the Abhainn fhionn, stones set for a boat's keel by hands none living can name, and build their houses about it, naming the place for what they found.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceann àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: I. Of the Last Fields and the Last Fords

events.title: Inis mhòr's two facing rows are raised
events.body: Households settle Inis mhòr on the Abhainn ghorm and build their houses in two rows facing each other across a single trodden way, so that a neighbour's fire may be borrowed without crossing open ground in the rain; it is the oldest street any teller remembers on Dia-thìr.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Inis mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: I. Of the Last Fields and the Last Fords

events.title: Baile gheal in the south-west
events.body: Baile gheal is founded on the south-western plain round a house with white-limed walls. The lime is burned from the shells of the old middens along the coast.

events.title: Àth bheag on the eastern coast
events.body: Households settle the small ford at Àth bheag on the far eastern coast, the easternmost dwelling of the age on the main island. Their boats go out after the geese on the islands.

events.title: Catrìona Mhòr
events.body: Catrìona Mhòr, twelfth of the Stone Kings and of the king's blood, holds Dùn ìseal under him; hers is the last name in the spoken list. It is told that she knew every household of the hills by its line seven names back.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona takes the hill of Dùn ìseal

events.title: Seumas Òg of the Red Hill
events.body: Seumas Òg holds the Red Hill, and with him the spoken list of the Red Hill ends. In the next age what the reciters kept of it is written down.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seumas Òg takes An Cnoc Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seumas Òg dies on An Cnoc Ruadh

events.title: The two lists recited together
events.body: At the ford gathering, in the time of Catrìona Mhòr, the list of the Stone Kings and the list of the Red Hill are recited one after the other from the first name to the last. It takes from dusk to dawn. For the first time both are heard whole.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The two rolls are spoken whole at the ford in one night

events.title: Catrìona takes the hill of Dùn ìseal
events.body: Catrìona, of the king's blood and two hundred and forty-seven years old, takes Dùn ìseal formally as the twelfth to hold it of Rìghrean na Cloiche' line, known already for a memory that can give any household's line back seven names without pausing to think.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona Mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: II. Of Catrìona

events.title: Seumas Òg takes An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: A young man of seven-and-twenty named Seumas takes up the holding of An Cnoc Ruadh his own line has kept since the palisade first burned, the same season Catrìona takes Dùn ìseal; his name will be the last An Cnoc Ruadh's own spoken roll carries.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seumas Òg of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: II. Of Catrìona

events.title: The two rolls are spoken whole at the ford in one night
events.body: Eòin gives the whole roll of Rìghrean na Cloiche from Ailean Mòr to Catrìona's own name, and Ùna gives the whole roll of An Cnoc Ruadh from Beathag Ruadh to Seumas Òg's, from dusk to the grey before morning; it is the first time either roll is heard whole, and those nearest the king see him smile when his own name is spoken.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The two lists recited together

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Lists

events.title: Lots drawn for the slab
events.body: The lot for the keeper of the slab is drawn now among households from every part of the hills, not only those near the crack. The keepers' house at Tobar dhìreach becomes a place of pilgrimage.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lot for the slab is drawn from every part of the hills

events.title: The lot for the slab is drawn from every part of the hills
events.body: Where the lot for the keeper of the slab was once drawn only from households near the crack, it comes in these years to be drawn from every part of the hills alike, and Tobar dhìreach becomes a place walked to for its own sake by households whose grandparents never heard the crack mentioned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lots drawn for the slab

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: IV. Of the Cord and the Districts

events.title: A nameless hand recuts Calbh Cnoc ghorm
events.body: A hand from Catrìona's own hill goes out to Calbh Cnoc ghorm and recuts its worn grooves along their old lines before the rain can lose them; some who come after hold that a single stroke changed in the recutting, though none can agree which, or prove any changed at all.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The saying on the column recut

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VI. Of the Column and the Old Middens

events.title: The keepers number nine
events.body: The keepers of the slab are made nine, one drawn by lot for each of nine districts of the hills. They meet at the slab when a keeper dies, and at no other time.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Luchd-faire na Lice settle at nine

events.title: Luchd-faire na Lice settle at nine
events.body: The keepers settle at nine, one drawn by lot for each of nine districts of the hills that no household has ever marked on the ground but every household somehow knows the edge of; the nine meet at the slab only when one of their number dies.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers number nine

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: IV. Of the Cord and the Districts

events.title: Coal in every hearth by the handful
events.body: Every household of the hills burns its handful of the coloured coal, measured in a copy of the stone cup, on one night in the dark of the year, the night later kept as Samhain. All burn at once by agreement, so that the low fires of the handful show on every hillside on the same night.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The handful comes to be burned all at once by agreement

events.title: A handful refused at Cnoc dhubh
events.body: The household of the Cnoc dhubh trench, where the two diggers were crushed, refuses its handful of coal for as long as any remembers. No household before it is known to have chosen not to burn at all.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cnoc na Claise's household refuses its handful

events.title: The handful comes to be burned all at once by agreement
events.body: Without any lot or law behind it, every household in reach of another comes to burn its measured handful of an gual dathach on the same dark night, each watching for the first low flame on the nearest hill before lighting its own; the night comes to be called Oidhche na Glaice.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Coal in every hearth by the handful

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: V. Of the Handful That All Burned Together

events.title: Cnoc na Claise's household refuses its handful
events.body: The descendants of Torcall Tochlair, who stayed by the trench where his brother was crushed, will not burn the handful with the rest of the hills and give no single answer twice for it; Catrìona sends no one to compel them, and none at the slab asks her to.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A handful refused at Cnoc dhubh

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: V. Of the Handful That All Burned Together

events.title: The cord of Dùn ìseal grows to nine hundred knots
events.body: Finding she can no longer carry the whole tally of households in her own head, Catrìona sets her people to counting them plainly on a knotted cord, a knot to a hearth, which grows through her years of holding to some nine hundred knots, the largest count made on Dia-thìr in the age; the king's own kin are never upon it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Counting the households

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: IV. Of the Cord and the Districts

events.title: Counting the households
events.body: The people of Catrìona Mhòr count the households of the hills by knots on a cord, a knot to a hearth. The cord of Dùn ìseal is said to have borne some nine hundred knots, the greatest count made on Dia-thìr in this age.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The cord of Dùn ìseal grows to nine hundred knots

events.title: The saying on the column recut
events.body: The words on the column at Cnoc ghorm, worn shallow, are recut in their old grooves by a hand from the hill of the Stone Kings. Some later readers hold that the recutting changed a letter; none can prove which.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A nameless hand recuts Calbh Cnoc ghorm

events.title: The tally stones of Seann Dunn are set back in their old order
events.body: A family digging a house-floor into an old midden at Seann Dunn strikes a row of upright stones each cut with a single stroke, knows them for the tally stones of the coast's old people, and sets them back as they lay rather than break them for the floor, building further along the midden's shoulder instead.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last Seann-Dhaoine midden disturbed

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VI. Of the Column and the Old Middens

events.title: The last Seann-Dhaoine midden disturbed
events.body: Households at the eastern Seann Dunn cut into the old midden for a house-floor and find the tally stones. They put them back in the order they lay and build elsewhere.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The tally stones of Seann Dunn are set back in their old order

events.title: The south-eastern coast rows its dead to Eilean ìseal
events.body: The custom grows along the south-eastern coast of rowing the newly dead out to Eilean ìseal rather than burying them on the mainland shore, whether learned from the old coast people's graves across the strait or come to of itself; the tellings let the question stand unsettled.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilean ìseal given to the dead

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VI. Of the Column and the Old Middens

events.title: Eilean ìseal given to the dead
events.body: The households of the south-east coast begin to row their dead to Eilean ìseal, after the old manner of the Seann-Dhaoine. Whether they learned it from the Seann Vell graves on Eilean dhearg, or came to it of themselves, is not told.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The south-eastern coast rows its dead to Eilean ìseal

events.title: Eilean chrom stays unfished
events.body: No household puts out a boat to fish the waters of Eilean chrom, where Gilleasbuig Beag was left with no boat to come back in; his fire was seen three nights running the first year and then no more, and the island stays empty and unfished.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleasbuig Beag's island

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VI. Of the Column and the Old Middens

events.title: Gilleasbuig Beag's island
events.body: Eilean chrom, where Gilleasbuig Beag was left, stays empty and unfished. His fire is seen on it for three nights, the tellings say, and then no more.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Eilean chrom stays unfished

events.title: The keepers ask to be named
events.body: The nine keepers of the slab ask Catrìona Mhòr to declare their charge before the whole ford gathering, so that no king after her may draw the lot at Dùn ìseal. She neither refuses nor agrees, and the matter is left to the next age.

links.label: Fulfilled by
links.title: Aodh Crom's asking

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The nine keepers ask Catrìona to declare their charge

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again

events.title: The nine keepers ask Catrìona to declare their charge
events.body: The nine of Luchd-faire na Lice come up together at the ford and ask Catrìona, then in her twenty-ninth year of holding, to declare their charge over the slab, the lot and the handful before the whole gathering so that no king after her may reach for it as Calum Ciar once did; she names the eldest of them by his own line before he finishes bowing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers ask to be named

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VII. Of the Asking of the Nine

events.title: Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again
events.body: Catrìona gives the nine keepers neither refusal nor consent, telling them only, "Not this year," and then, before the eldest can press her further, "Ask me again"; the nine go back to their own fires by the slab to wait.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers ask to be named

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eòin Beul-binn and Ùna Ruadh die within two years of each other

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VII. Of the Asking of the Nine

events.title: Eòin Beul-binn and Ùna Ruadh die within two years of each other
events.body: Eòin, whose voice carried the whole roll of Rìghrean na Cloiche across one night at the ford, dies in his eightieth year, and Ùna, who answered him roll for roll for An Cnoc Ruadh, follows him within two years in her seventy-third; the telling of that single night passes from then on at second hand.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona falls ill on the hill

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VIII. Of Her Growing Years

events.title: Catrìona falls ill on the hill
events.body: In her two hundred and eighty-ninth year the sickness comes on Catrìona that will not leave again; she keeps her seat at Dùn ìseal as long as she is able, still able to give a household's whole line back seven names, and the nine keepers, hearing of it, send no word asking again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eòin Beul-binn and Ùna Ruadh die within two years of each other

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: VIII. Of Her Growing Years

events.title: Seumas Òg dies on An Cnoc Ruadh
events.body: Seumas Òg, the last name An Cnoc Ruadh's spoken roll carries, dies in his seventy-first year in the winter before Catrìona Mhòr, and the lake shore keeps no holder's fire for him after, only its own.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seumas Òg of the Red Hill

told_in.book: Of the Two Lists and the Asking of the Nine
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Lists

events.title: The king's kin bring their claims to the hill
events.body: After Catrìona Mhòr's death every soul of the king's blood within three days' walk comes to Dùn ìseal to press a claim on the hill, each able to say the two names of a line whose second name is always Ailean's; the king hears every claim with the same still face.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king takes back the hill

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: I. Of the Hill Left to No One

events.title: The king takes back the hill
events.body: Catrìona Mhòr dies, and with her the list of the Stone Kings ends. Her kin put forward many claims to Dùn ìseal, and Ailean Mòr gives the hill to none of them. He comes to it himself and holds it in his own hand, as in the first days.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The king's kin bring their claims to the hill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king holds the hill and gives it to none

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word runs that the kin will gather below Dùn ìseal

events.title: The king holds the hill and gives it to none
events.body: The king tells the gathered claimants that no line among them is better than another and that Catrìona Mhòr's line cannot be handed to a stranger's open palm; he will hold the hill himself, as before Gormshuil first took it up in his name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king takes back the hill

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: I. Of the Hill Left to No One

events.title: The first marriage reckoned openly for a share
events.body: A young man of a minor line is married to a woman three lines removed from the king, and his father says openly at the betrothal fire that the match is made to bring five lines instead of three nearer the front of the reckoning, should the king ever name an heir.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eve of the Binding

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A daughters' claim disputed at a betrothal

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: II. Of the Marriages Made for a Share

events.title: A daughters' claim disputed at a betrothal
events.body: A household holding good grazing but no claim of its own is joined by marriage to one that claims through four generations of daughters, and the hill argues without settling whether a claim run through daughters weighs more or less than one run through sons.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first marriage reckoned openly for a share

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A betrothal broken over a nearer claim

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: II. Of the Marriages Made for a Share

events.title: A betrothal broken over a nearer claim
events.body: A grandmother breaks off her granddaughter's marriage within the month of its making, having found a nearer claim on the groom's own side that she judges would weigh the match's worth downward; the hill takes it as proof that every marriage among the blood is now made for its shares and not for anything else.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A daughters' claim disputed at a betrothal

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: II. Of the Marriages Made for a Share

events.title: A household of the western slopes loses its grazing
events.body: A household that has held grazing on the western slopes eleven generations is told, without reason given, to remove itself to ground of equal size two valleys over before winter; asked directly why, the king says only that a share given has always been a share that can be taken back.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eve of the Binding

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raonaid nic Ailein dies at the river-meadow

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: II. Of the Marriages Made for a Share

events.title: Raonaid nic Ailein dies at the river-meadow
events.body: Raonaid nic Ailein, the king's daughter, dies at her own river-meadow in her one thousand three hundred and eightieth year; the king sits with her the better part of a day and a night, as he sat once with Gormshuil and once with Somhairle, and speaks of it to no one after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A household of the western slopes loses its grazing

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: III. Of Raonaid's Share Taken Back

events.title: The king takes back Raonaid's grazing
events.body: Within the month of Raonaid nic Ailein's burying the king sends word that the river-meadow grazing is wanted elsewhere and that Niall Òg, her nearest of that line, is to remove his household from it; Niall answers, as he has come to answer every such word, with a laugh.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eve of the Binding

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: III. Of Raonaid's Share Taken Back

events.title: Dùn dhearg will not bow
events.body: The king sends to Dùn dhearg and to the households east of the vein, bidding them come in to him. They send his messenger back with nothing, and swear among themselves that they will owe nothing to Dùn ìseal nor to its king. From that year the spears of the east are gathered at Dùn dhearg.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king sends Niall Òg to Dùn dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearghal Donn refuses the king's asking

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Niall Òg carries the refusal home

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The spears of the east are kept to hand

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sluagh an Ear begins to gather at Dùn dhearg

events.title: The king sends Niall Òg to Dùn dhearg
events.body: The king chooses Niall Òg to carry word east of the vein, bidding the households of Dùn dhearg come in to him at last, judging that a man known for asking nothing on his own account is less likely to be mistaken for the leading edge of a conquest.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg will not bow

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Niall Òg finds Dùn dhearg wanting nothing of the hill

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: IV. Of Niall Sent East

events.title: Niall Òg finds Dùn dhearg wanting nothing of the hill
events.body: Niall Òg crosses the vein and finds the double bank of Dùn dhearg larger and better kept than any western telling had prepared him for, its forges and granary proof of a country that has gone far, by its own hands, toward needing nothing from Dùn ìseal.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king sends Niall Òg to Dùn dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: IV. Of Niall Sent East

events.title: Fearghal Donn refuses the king's asking
events.body: Fearghal Donn, holder of Dùn dhearg, hears the king's messenger before the whole household and answers that his people have raised their own bank and buried their own dead without any man's leave, and will not be counted among a kin who marry for shares and wait a thousand years for a hill never given.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg will not bow

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: V. Of the Word Sent Back

events.title: Niall Òg carries the refusal home
events.body: Niall Òg rides back to Dùn ìseal and gives Fearghal Donn's word to the king plainly; the king says he had looked for no other answer, thanks him for the carrying of it, and turns to the next claim waiting for him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg will not bow

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: III. Of Raonaid's Share Taken Back

events.title: The spears of the east are kept to hand
events.body: Word reaches Dùn ìseal by traders, not by any messenger sent for the purpose, that the households about Dùn dhearg have begun keeping their own spears closer than ever before, against a quarrel none of them will name; the king does nothing about it that anyone can see.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg will not bow

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eve of the Binding

told_in.book: Of the Shares Counted
told_in.section: V. Of the Word Sent Back

events.title: A woman of Clann na Ceiste speaks over the child
events.body: An old woman of Clann na Ceiste, come down from the slab to see the new child, tells Gille-Brìde that a boy born short-lived among the long-lived will learn early what his own kin have never needed to learn until late: how much of a life can be made to matter in however much of it is given.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gille-Brìde's father born in Na Glinn Àrda

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ceallach is born in Na Glinn Àrda

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: I. Of the Eve as It Stood

events.title: Ceallach is born in Na Glinn Àrda
events.body: A son is born to Gille-Brìde of Somhairle's line in Na Glinn Àrda and is called Ceallach; he is slower to walk and to run than the children before him, the first sign, told back afterward, that the years were coming down faster in him than in his father.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A woman of Clann na Ceiste speaks over the child

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearghal Donn dies at Dùn dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: I. Of the Eve as It Stood

events.title: The eve of the Binding
events.body: The handful is kept everywhere in the hills, the keepers are nine, the sharing before the storms is kept on every coast, and the saying is spoken at every gathering. None of it is yet declared, and no oath is yet sworn over the vein. The king holds Dùn ìseal in his own hand, his kin wait about him for their shares, and the spears of the east gather at Dùn dhearg.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first marriage reckoned openly for a share

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A household of the western slopes loses its grazing

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The king takes back Raonaid's grazing

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The spears of the east are kept to hand

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The kin come down household by household

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king goes down to meet the east with a handful of household

events.title: Fearghal Donn dies at Dùn dhearg
events.body: Fearghal Donn, who had held Dùn dhearg since before Niall Òg was sent to him and sent back with nothing, dies an old man in his own bed at the fort; the households east of the vein bury him as they buried Ailis, without word sent to the hill and none expected back.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ceallach is born in Na Glinn Àrda

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Artair takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: II. Of the Father's Three Hundred and Eighth Year

events.title: Artair takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg
events.body: Artair, Fearghal Donn's son, takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg with no more ceremony than his father had used, and says at the burying itself that he will hold what his father held and ask nothing further of the hill until the day it asks something of him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearghal Donn dies at Dùn dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gille-Brìde's father dies in his three hundred and eighth year

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: II. Of the Father's Three Hundred and Eighth Year

events.title: Gille-Brìde's father dies in his three hundred and eighth year
events.body: Gille-Brìde's father dies at Samhain in his three hundred and eighth year, fewer years than his own father had, dying as most of that line has learned to die: without illness or wound, simply slower each year until one morning he does not rise from his own hearthstone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Artair takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: II. Of the Father's Three Hundred and Eighth Year

events.title: Word runs that the kin will gather below Dùn ìseal
events.body: At the burying, word runs among the fires that the king's kin mean at last to come down out of their scattered holdings and gather in the valley below Dùn ìseal, each line with its own tents and its own fire, to wait together upon the shares left uncounted since Catrìona Mhòr's death.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king takes back the hill

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: II. Of the Father's Three Hundred and Eighth Year

events.title: The kin come down household by household
events.body: Through the summer the king's kin come down into the valley below Dùn ìseal household by household and line by line, no single word sent to call any of them, until the valley holds more tents and more fires than any one household has ever seen gathered in one place.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The eve of the Binding

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Murchadh Mòr brings his sons and grandsons down

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: III. Of the Tents and the Steward to Each Line

events.title: Murchadh Mòr brings his sons and grandsons down
events.body: Murchadh Mòr comes down from the northern plain with a column of sons and grandsons that takes three days to pass any one point on the road, carrying more tent-cloth, it is said, than the valley below Dùn ìseal has ever seen brought to one place at once.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The kin come down household by household

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eithne's knot-keeper counts every soul on the new ground

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: III. Of the Tents and the Steward to Each Line

events.title: Eithne's knot-keeper counts every soul on the new ground
events.body: Eithne comes down from below Làrach an Dùin-fhaire with her own household, and her knot-keeper walks at its head with the household's cord wound about his arm, meaning to be seen keeping count of every soul who sets foot on the new ground, and does so from the first day to the last.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh Mòr brings his sons and grandsons down

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ìomhar Dearg pitches nearest the vein

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: III. Of the Tents and the Steward to Each Line

events.title: Ìomhar Dearg pitches nearest the vein
events.body: Ìomhar Dearg comes down from the eastern marches nursing a hundred years' grievance over river-grazing he judges his by use if not by the king's word, and pitches his tents nearer the vein than any other line thinks wise, exactly, everyone agrees, like him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eithne's knot-keeper counts every soul on the new ground

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìne nan Snaidhm keeps the cord of the whole valley

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: III. Of the Tents and the Steward to Each Line

events.title: Sìne nan Snaidhm keeps the cord of the whole valley
events.body: Sìne nan Snaidhm, knot-keeper of the household cord at Dùn ìseal, walks the growing valley of tents checking each new fire against the cord she carries, so that within a season no soul is pitched there, of the king's blood or of any household following it down, whose count she has not kept.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ìomhar Dearg pitches nearest the vein

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A steward is set over every line

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: III. Of the Tents and the Steward to Each Line

events.title: A steward is set over every line
events.body: By the second summer a steward stands over every line camped below Dùn ìseal, holding no ground and no lordship, only charged to speak for its household at the common fires and see its people fed and housed while the waiting goes on, until the valley looks less like a gathering than a town that never raised walls.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìne nan Snaidhm keeps the cord of the whole valley

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: III. Of the Tents and the Steward to Each Line

events.title: Sluagh an Ear begins to gather at Dùn dhearg
events.body: In the spring Sluagh an Ear begins gathering at Dùn dhearg under Artair, who is said to have waited three years, since he first took up his father's holding, for the very stillness of the hill to break; word of the gathering reaches the western fires within the week.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dùn dhearg will not bow

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gille-Brìde and Ceallach come down to see the valley

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: IV. Of Gille-Brìde Come Down

events.title: Gille-Brìde and Ceallach come down to see the valley
events.body: Gille-Brìde walks down out of Na Glinn Àrda with Ceallach, now grown but already, though neither says it, walking more slowly than a man of his years should, and the two stand at evening looking over more fires than either has ever seen gathered at once.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sluagh an Ear begins to gather at Dùn dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìne nan Snaidhm names Gille-Brìde the one soul asking nothing

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: IV. Of Gille-Brìde Come Down

events.title: Sìne nan Snaidhm names Gille-Brìde the one soul asking nothing
events.body: Sìne nan Snaidhm tells Gille-Brìde that his name is on no cord she carries, since he has asked for no ground and no share from anyone, and that he is, that night, the only soul in the whole valley of whom that can be said.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gille-Brìde and Ceallach come down to see the valley

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: IV. Of Gille-Brìde Come Down

events.title: The king goes down to meet the east with a handful of household
events.body: Near the end of summer the king comes down from Dùn ìseal with no more than three tents' worth of his own household, going to meet the east himself, while every line camped in the valley says, each at its own fire, that it will follow him within a day or two.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The eve of the Binding

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The king sends Gille-Brìde home to the hills

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Answer

events.title: The king sends Gille-Brìde home to the hills
events.body: Gille-Brìde asks the king plainly whether he too should come down to the ford; the king tells him to go home to his own people instead, since whatever comes of it will want telling afterward by someone who was not in it, and his line has always been better at the telling than the coming.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The king goes down to meet the east with a handful of household

told_in.book: Of the Tents in the Valley
told_in.section: V. Of the King's Answer

events.title: The host of Dùn dhearg musters at the ford
events.body: Every household east of the vein sends its spears down to the river below Dùn dhearg in the last days of an Lùnastal, camping the whole night along a mile of the east bank under Artair mac Fhearghail, meaning to hold the crossing before the king's kin can gather against them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Camp under Artair mac Fhearghail

events.title: Artair mac Fhearghail recalls the answer sent to the king
events.body: At the fires the first night, Artair mac Fhearghail repeats to the host the answer his father Fearghal Donn once sent back with the king's messenger, that the households east of the vein would keep their own bank and owed the hill at Dùn ìseal nothing, and says the answer has not changed in eighty years.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: I. Of the Camp under Artair mac Fhearghail

events.title: The east finds the king alone at the ford
events.body: At sunrise the host of Dùn dhearg finds a single man sitting on the stone at the head of the ford, his kin nowhere on the far bank; word runs down the fires that the king's own household has quarrelled over the shares of his kingdom and would not follow him east.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: II. Of the Man Alone at the Ford

events.title: The first rush breaks on the king at the ford
events.body: Two hundred spears go into the ford together at sunrise on the first day and are thrown back with the king alone in the water among them; the host sees the river run red below the crossing before the morning mist has fully lifted.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the First Day

events.title: The east tries the ford's edges and its throwing spears
events.body: Through the first day the host tries the deep channel above and below the ford to come at the king from the side, and by afternoon empties its fletchers' whole store throwing spears from the bank; neither the crossing nor the throwing turns him from his stone.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the First Day

events.title: A household of Caol shean loses a man to the first day's ford
events.body: A net-mender's kinsman of Caol shean, twenty years unhurt at every boundary quarrel of the eastern country, goes into the first rush and is not seen to come out of the river; his wife asks after him at every fire down the bank until evening, then asks no more.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: III. Of the First Day

events.title: The dead of the host begin to dam the ford
events.body: On the second day the drowned and the slain lie so thick at the shallows below the crossing that the river backs up over the gravel, running warm and red, and the men of Dùn dhearg must climb their own dead to reach water shallow enough to cross.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Day

events.title: The king draws a boy of Dùn dhearg from the river with his own hand
events.body: In the press of the second day the king takes the spear from the hands of a sixteen-year-old of the eastern host as a mother takes a knife from a child, and the boy is carried out alive on the east bank; the telling of that hand is kept by the east long after his name is forgotten.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Day

events.title: Artair mac Fhearghail counsels the host to go in together
events.body: On the second night, with some of the host ready to go home, Artair mac Fhearghail tells the fires that the king is flesh and must have an end, as a cliff has an end before the sea, and counsels every spear of the east to go into the river together on the third day and not draw back.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Day

events.title: The whole strength of the east goes into the river together
events.body: At first light on the third day every spear the east country has enters the ford at once and does not draw back, the host closing on the king from three sides the whole day long while the dead already in the water rise higher than the shallows had ever stood.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Third Day

events.title: A light is seen on the water around the king
events.body: In the afternoon of the third day men near the middle of the ford see a light low along the river's surface where the king stands, of no colour any of them had a word for, and say afterward only that they saw every colour in it and none, and would say no more.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the Third Day

events.title: The king's kin fail to come to the ford
events.body: Through all three days at the ford below Dùn dhearg, no household of the king's own blood, and no spear of the hills, comes down the western track to stand with him; Sluagh an Ear has the river to itself the whole time.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala

told_in.book: Of the Ford below Dùn dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Day
